1:3.headline: The doubled word hints that God spoke to him earlier
1:3.body: The verse says the word of God הָיֹה הָיָה, "being, it was". Rashi and the Targum read the doubling as saying God had already spoken to Ezekiel in the Land of Israel, since prophecy does not begin outside it.

sources.quote: הָיָה כְּבָר, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה עַל נָבִיא בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁשָּׁרְתָה עָלָיו תְּחִלָּה בָּאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says it means "it had already been", because God's Presence rests on a prophet outside the Land only if it first rested on him in the Land.

sources.quote: עִם יְחֶזְקֵאל בַּר בּוּזִי כַהֲנָא בְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל תָּב תִּנְיָנוּת וְאִתְמַלֵל עִמֵיהּ
sources.says: The Targum says the word came to Ezekiel in the Land of Israel, and then spoke with him a second time in Chaldea.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים כי פעם ראשונה אינו נדבר עם הנביא בחוצה לארץ פעם שניה מדבר
sources.says: Radak brings the view that God does not speak to a prophet outside the Land the first time, only the second.

1:3.headline: "The hand of God" means prophecy seizing him by force
1:3.body: No real hand is meant. Rashi says "hand" in prophecy always means force, the prophecy gripping the prophet against his will, and Maimonides says "the hand of God" is a name for the prophetic vision itself.

sources.quote: כָּל לְשׁוֹן יָד הָאֲמוּרָה בְּסֵפֶר זֶה, וּבְכָל לְשׁוֹן נְבוּאָה, אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן תֹּקֶף, שֶׁהַנְּבוּאָה תּוֹקֶפֶת עַל כָּרְחוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says every "hand" in this book and in prophecy means force, since the prophecy overpowers the prophet against his will.

sources.quote: והיא הנקראת "מראה הנבואה", ונקראת גם "יד ה'"
sources.says: Maimonides says the prophetic vision is also called "the hand of God", and describes it as a frightening state that comes on the prophet while awake.

sources.quote: כח חוזק הנבואה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the strong force of prophecy.

1:5.headline: Why "human" when the creatures also had lion, ox and eagle faces?
1:5.body: Rashi asks why the verse calls them human-looking when they had animal faces too. He answers that the human face was the chief one, and it was the face of Jacob.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁזֶּה אָב לְכֻלָּם, קִלֵּס הַנָּבִיא אֶת הַמֶּרְכָּבָה בּוֹ; וְהוּא דְּמוּת פַּרְצוּפוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the prophet praised the chariot by its human face because that face is chief of them all, and it is the face of Jacob our father.

sources.quote: וכלל צורת כל חיה כצורת אדם, כמו שאמר: "דְּמוּת אָדָם לָהֵנָּה"
sources.says: Maimonides says the overall shape of each creature was human.

1:5.headline: The creatures are only a "likeness"; the wheels never are
1:5.body: Ezekiel says he saw "the likeness of" the creatures, the dome and the throne, but never "the likeness of" the wheels. Maimonides and Malbim say this marks a real difference: the wheels are described as actual bodies.

sources.quote: ואילו על האופנים לא אמר לא "דמות אופן" ולא "דמות אופנים" כלל, אלא הודעה סתמית על צורה מציאותית כפי שהיא
sources.says: Maimonides says Ezekiel never wrote "the likeness of a wheel", but simply described the wheels as a real form.

sources.quote: באופנים לא הזכיר לשון דמות כמו שהזכיר בחיות ובמה שלמעלה מהם, כי החיות אינם גשם
sources.says: Malbim says "likeness" is not used for the wheels as it is for the creatures, because the creatures are not physical while the wheels are.

1:7.headline: Straight legs with no knees, because angels never sit down
1:7.body: Rashi says the creatures' legs had no joints to bend, since they never sit or lie down. Maimonides quotes the sages: this teaches that there is no sitting in heaven.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יְשִׁיבָה וְלֹא שְׁכִיבָה, וְאֵין צְרִיכִין לִהְיוֹת קְפִיצִין
sources.says: Rashi says their legs had no joints because they neither sit nor lie down, so they need none.

sources.quote: מלמד שאין ישיבה למעלה
sources.says: Maimonides quotes the sages that "a straight leg" teaches there is no sitting above.

sources.quote: אין בהם פרקים לכוף את שוקיהם לפי שאין להם לא שכיבה ולא ישיבה
sources.says: Metzudat David says their legs had no joints to bend, since they neither lie nor sit.

1:7.headline: A calf's foot, or a round foot? עגל can sound like both
1:7.body: עגל means calf, but Rashi and Targum Jonathan read it as round, like עגול. Maimonides says the prophet chose such words for what they hint at, and he lists "a calf's foot" among them.

sources.quote: רֶגֶל עָגוֹל, וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says it means a round foot, and that Targum Jonathan translates it the same way.

sources.quote: כְּפַרְסַת רִגְלִית סְגַלְגְלָן
sources.says: The Targum renders it "like the sole of round feet".

sources.quote: משתמשים בנאומיהם במונחים רב־משמעיים ובמונחים שאין הכוונה בהם במשמעותם הראשונית, אלא שהמונח מוזכר בגלל גזִירה מסוימת
sources.says: Maimonides says prophets use words with several meanings, or words picked for what they derive from, and he names "calf's foot" in the chariot as one.

1:7.headline: Burnished bronze: Menachem tied קלל to "roasted in fire"
1:7.body: קלל is a rare word for the bronze's shine. Rashi says it means refined and glowing, and notes that Menachem linked it to קלוי באש, roasted in fire.

sources.quote: מְזֻקָּק וּמֵאִיר, וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״קָלוּי בָּאֵשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it means refined and shining, and that Menachem grouped it with "roasted in fire".

sources.quote: קלל. ממורט וזך
sources.says: Radak says it means polished and pure.

sources.quote: בדברו במרכבה על "נְחֹשֶׁת" ו"קָלָל"
sources.says: Maimonides counts "bronze" and "kalal" among the chariot's words that hold hidden meanings.

1:11.headline: Rashi says only the accent mark showed him how to read this
1:11.body: The verse could mean that both faces and wings were spread out above. Rashi says that without the strong accent on ופניהם he would not know how to explain it: the accent cuts the word off, so only the wings spread above and cover the faces.

sources.quote: אִלְמָלֵא שֶׁרָאִיתִי טַעַם זָקֵף גָּדוֹל נָקוּד עַל וּפְנֵיהֶם, לֹא הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ לְפָרְשׁוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that had he not seen a zakef gadol accent on "and their faces", he would not have known how to explain the verse.

sources.quote: מלת ופניהם נפרדת בטעם לומר שאינה דבקה עם הבאה אחריה
sources.says: Radak says the accent separates the word, to show it is not joined to the word after it.

1:12.headline: Here רוח is not wind but will
1:12.body: רוח can mean wind, breath or spirit. Rashi, Radak and Targum Jonathan read it here as will: the creatures go wherever God wills, and Maimonides says the same.

sources.quote: אֶל אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה שָׁמָּה הָרוּחַ. הָרָצוֹן לָלֶכֶת
sources.says: Rashi says "the spirit" here means the will to go.

sources.quote: ואיש, הרוח. הרצון וכן תירגם יונתן רעוא
sources.says: Radak says it means will, and that Targum Jonathan translates it "desire".

sources.quote: "רוח" כאן אינה רוח (נושבת), אלא היא כוונה, כמו שביארנו על רב־משמעיות "רוח"
sources.says: Maimonides says רוח here is not a blowing wind but intention, as he explained in his chapter on the word's many meanings.

1:14.headline: Running and returning, like a flame leaping from a furnace
1:14.body: רצוא is found only here. Radak says it means running, from the root רצה with an א in place of the ה, and Rashi brings the sages' picture of a furnace flame that keeps darting out and back.

sources.quote: מקור שרשו רצה והאל"ף במקום ה"א ויהיה רצה ורוץ כענין אחד
sources.says: Radak says the root is רצה with an alef in place of the heh, and it means the same as running.

sources.quote: רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כְּלַהֶבֶת הַכִּבְשָׁן, שֶׁיּוֹצְאָה תָּמִיד מִפִּי הַכִּבְשָׁן וּמְמַהֶרֶת לַחֲזוֹר וְלִיכָּנֵס
sources.says: Rashi quotes the sages: like the flame of a furnace that keeps coming out of its mouth and hurries back in.

sources.quote: "רצוא" הוא המקור של "רץ", ו"שוב" הוא המקור של "שָב"
sources.says: Maimonides says רצוא is the verb "run" and שוב is the verb "return".

1:14.headline: Bazak is barak, lightning, with one letter swapped
1:14.body: בזק appears only here. Metzudat Zion and Maimonides say it is ברק, lightning, since ז and ר can trade places, while Rashi brings the sages' picture of colored fire flashing between clay pots where gold is refined.

sources.quote: הבזק. כמו הברק כי זסשר״ץ מתחלף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like ברק, lightning, because the letters ז, ס, ש, ר and צ can replace each other.

sources.quote: ו"בזק" היא מילה נרדפת לברק
sources.says: Maimonides says בזק is another word for lightning.

sources.quote: כְּגוֹוֶן אֵשׁ הַיּוֹצֵא מִבֵּין הַחֲרָסִין
sources.says: Rashi says their color was like the fire that comes out between the clay pieces in which gold is refined.

1:15.headline: One wheel on the ground: the sages saw the angel Sandalfon
1:15.body: Ezekiel sees "one wheel" on the ground. Rashi says the sages read it as the angel Sandalfon, standing on the earth with his head among the creatures, and Maimonides says the four wheels are called one because they are joined.

sources.quote: זֶה סַנְדַּלְפוֹן, הָעוֹמֵד בָּאָרֶץ וְרֹאשׁוֹ מַגִּיעַ לְבֵין הַחַיּוֹת; אֲבָל לְפִי הָעִנְיָן אָנוּ לְמֵדִין, שֶׁהָאוֹפַנִּים אַרְבָּעָה הֵם
sources.says: Rashi says the sages call this Sandalfon, who stands on the earth with his head reaching the creatures, but by the context there are four wheels.

sources.quote: משום שהם דבוקים זה בזה
sources.says: Maimonides says the wheels are called "one wheel" though they are four, because they are joined to each other.

1:16.headline: A sky-blue gem that made some read the wheels as heavens
1:16.body: תרשיש is a precious stone, clear and blue. Maimonides says this sky color is part of why Targum Jonathan took the wheels to be the heavens.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ אֶבֶן טוֹבָה שֶׁשְּׁמָהּ תַּרְשִׁישׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a precious stone named tarshish.

sources.quote: כי אבן תרשיש הוא בעל גוון יפה כעין התכלת וגם הוא זך בהיר עד שיראה בו מעבר אל עבר
sources.says: Metzudat David says the tarshish stone has a fine blue color and is so clear you can see through it.

sources.quote: על האופנים שהם "כְּעֵין תַּרְשִׁישׁ" (שם א,טז), וזה צבע המיוחס לשמים
sources.says: Maimonides says Targum Jonathan's reading of the wheels as the heavens was strengthened by "like tarshish", a color linked with the sky.

1:18.headline: Fear: did the wheels frighten others, or stand in fear?
1:18.body: The verse says the wheels had "fear". Rashi gives two readings: they were frightening to look at, or they themselves stood in awe.

sources.quote: מְאֻיָּמִים הֵם לָרוֹאֶה אוֹתָם; וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין וְיִרְאָה לָהֶם – בְּמוֹרָא עוֹמְדִים
sources.says: Rashi says they were frightening to whoever saw them, and some explain that they stood in fear.

sources.quote: כי הדבר שיהיה מופלג בכמותו יקרא כפלא ונורא
sources.says: Radak says something extreme in size is called wondrous and fearsome.

1:18.headline: Rims "full of eyes": real eyes, or many colors?
1:18.body: The rims were full of עינים. Rashi reads eyes, so the wheels could see every way without turning, while Metzudat Zion reads it as many colors, from כעין, "the look of".

sources.quote: לִרְאוֹת לְכָל רוּחַ, שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא יִסַּבּוּ בְּלֶכְתָּם
sources.says: Rashi says the eyes were for seeing in every direction, since the wheels did not turn as they went.

sources.quote: עינים. גוונים הרבה והוא מלשון כעין תרשיש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says "eyes" means many colors, from the word for "look" as in "the look of tarshish".

sources.quote: המחיצות ההם היו מלאות הרבה גוונים מחולפים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the walls of the wheels were full of many changing colors.

1:24.headline: "Like the voice of Shaddai": God's name, or simply "mighty"?
1:24.body: Radak gives two readings. שדי may mean strong and mighty, or it is God's name, Shaddai, and the sound was like His voice at Sinai.

sources.quote: כקול שדי. פירוש חזק ותקיף וכן כשוד משדי יבא והיה שדי בצריך או פירושו על האל יתברך שנקרא שדי
sources.says: Radak says Shaddai may mean strong and powerful, or it refers to God, who is called Shaddai.

sources.quote: יָכוֹל קוֹל נָמוּךְ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: כְּקוֹל שַׁדַּי
sources.says: Rashi says "like the voice of Shaddai" shows the sound was not a low one.

sources.quote: וכקול שדי בדברו בסיני
sources.says: Metzudat David says it was like God's voice when He spoke at Sinai.

1:26.headline: "The likeness of a throne" means likeness in majesty, not shape
1:26.body: Maimonides says דמות often means likeness in some quality, not in outline. "The likeness of a throne" is like a throne in majesty and honor, not in its legs or its squareness.

sources.quote: דומוּת בעניין הרוממות והנכבדות, לא בריבועו ובעוביו ובאורך רגליו כמו שחושבים הפתאים
sources.says: Maimonides says "the likeness of a throne" is a likeness in loftiness and honor, not in its square shape, thickness or leg length, as simple people think.

1:26.headline: "A likeness like the look of a man": two hedges, not one
1:26.body: Ezekiel does not say he saw a man on the throne, only "a likeness like the look of" one. Metzudat David says the double wording shows God has no likeness at all, and the sages said: great is the power of the prophets, who liken the form to its Maker.

sources.quote: ואמר דמות כמראה לומר שאין לו דמות כלל אבל אמרו בלשון דמות להסביר את האוזן
sources.says: Metzudat David says "likeness of an appearance" tells us God has no likeness at all; the words are there only to help the listener understand.

sources.quote: גדול כוחן שלנביאים שהן מדמין את הצורה ליוצרה
sources.says: Maimonides quotes the sages, "great is the power of the prophets, who liken the form to its Maker", on this verse, and says such forms are created things.

1:27.headline: "A house for it": inside it, or a house around it?
1:27.body: בית לה reads "a house for it". Rashi and Radak take it as "inside it": within the chashmal was a look of fire, while Metzudat David sees a kind of house of fire around it.

sources.quote: בֵּית לָהּ. מִלִּפְנִים לָהּ כְּמַרְאֵה אֵשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it means that within it there was a look of fire.

sources.quote: בית לה. מבפנים לה
sources.says: Radak says it means "inside it".

sources.quote: אל החשמל היה לה כעין בית מסביב ומראה הבית היה כמראה אש
sources.says: Metzudat David says the chashmal had something like a house around it, and the house looked like fire.

1:27.headline: Here even Rashi stops: no leave to look into this verse
1:27.body: At this second chashmal Rashi says no one was given leave to study the verse. Metzudat David reads the word as "be silent" and "speak": better to be silent about God than to describe Him.

sources.quote: לֹא נִתַּן רְשׁוּת לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בְּמִקְרָא זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says permission was not given to look closely into this verse.

sources.quote: וכן אין להשיג את האל יתברך וחשמל היא מלה מורכבת חש מל שראוי לחשות מן המלול בו
sources.says: Metzudat David says God cannot be grasped, and chashmal is a compound of "silent" and "speak": one should keep silent rather than talk about Him.

sources.quote: כלומר מהירות, שהיא הוראת "חש", והפסקה, שעליה מורה "מל"
sources.says: Maimonides brings the sages' reading of chashmal as two parts: חש, speed, and מל, stopping.

1:28.headline: "The glory of God" is not God, says Maimonides
1:28.body: Ezekiel ends by naming what he saw: "the likeness of the glory of God". Maimonides says this glory is something created, so the whole vision shows the chariot and not its Rider.

sources.quote: אינו אלא כבוד ה', דהיינו המרכבה ולא הרוכב, כי הוא יתעלה אינו ניתן להמשלה
sources.says: Maimonides says everything Ezekiel pictured is only God's glory, meaning the chariot and not the Rider, since God cannot be pictured.

sources.quote: המראה הזה שראיתי הוא מראה דמות כבוד ה׳ כי ראהו נוסע מבה״מ כדמות מלך יושב על המרכבה ונוסע
sources.says: Metzudat David says this was the look of the likeness of God's glory, seen leaving the Temple like a king riding a chariot.

10:1.headline: Cherub, כרוב, read as "like a child"
10:1.body: Metzudat David and Radak read כרוב as כ־רביא, "like a child", since רביא is Aramaic for a small boy. So a cherub has the face of a young child.

sources.quote: וקראם כרובים כי תינוק הוא בל׳ ארמי רביא
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are called cherubim because a small child in Aramaic is רביא.

sources.quote: תרגום של תנוק הוא רביא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Aramaic for a small child is רביא.

sources.quote: ופירוש כרוב כרביא שכן בבבל קורין לינוקא רביא
sources.says: Radak says כרוב means "like a child", because in Babylon they call a child רביא.

10:1.headline: "The likeness of a throne": like it in greatness, not in shape
10:1.body: Maimonides says דמות means a likeness in some quality, not in outline: the throne is like a throne in its glory, not a square seat with legs. He adds that Ezekiel names the sky-dome outright but sees only "a likeness" of the throne.

sources.quote: דומוּת בעניין הרוממות והנכבדות, לא בריבועו ובעוביו ובאורך רגליו כמו שחושבים הפתאים
sources.says: Maimonides says "the likeness of a throne" is a likeness in loftiness and honor, not in its squareness, thickness, or length of legs, as simple people think.

sources.quote: הוא הזכיר כאן את הרקיע באופן סתמי, ולא אמר "דמות רקיע"
sources.says: Maimonides says Ezekiel mentions the firmament here plainly and does not say "a likeness of a firmament".

10:2.headline: Throw the coals, but the angel held them for six years
10:2.body: Rashi and Radak, from the midrash, say Gabriel took the coals from a cherub's hand so they would cool, and he held them six years. This vision came in the sixth year, and the city fell in the eleventh.

sources.quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לְגַבְרִיאֵל, וְהוּא בִּקֵּשׁ מִן הַכְּרוּב לְתִתָּם לוֹ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּצְטַנְּנוּ הַגֶּחָלִים וְתֵקַל הַגְּזֵרָה
sources.says: Rashi says God spoke to Gabriel, who asked the cherub to hand him the coals so they would cool and the decree would be lighter.

sources.quote: לֹא הִשְׁלִיכָם עַד לְאַחַר שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים לְקַבָּלָתוֹ, שֶׁנִּתְעַמְּמוּ הַגֶּחָלִים בְּיָדוֹ כָּל שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים
sources.says: Rashi says he did not throw them until six years after receiving them, and the coals dimmed in his hand all six years.

sources.quote: שהרי נבואה זו היתה בשנה הששית ולא חרבה העיר עד שנת אחת עשרה
sources.says: Radak says this prophecy was in the sixth year and the city was not destroyed until the eleventh year.

10:4.headline: נגה is a glow thrown back, not the light itself
10:4.body: Malbim says נגה is reflected light. The glory's own light stayed in the house, and only its glow reached out into the court.

sources.quote: והנוגה אינו אור עצמי רק אור חוזר
sources.says: Malbim says נוגה is not light itself but returning, reflected light.

sources.quote: והאור החוזר התפלש עד החצר מן האור העצמי אשר בבית
sources.says: Malbim says the reflected light spread to the court from the light itself, which was in the house.

10:5.headline: A voice as loud as God's stopped at the outer court
10:5.body: Rashi, from the midrash, asks if the sound reached only that far because it was soft. No: it was as loud as God speaking, but when it reached the outer court it stopped.

sources.quote: יָכוֹל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַקּוֹל נָמוּךְ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: כְּקוֹל אֵל שַׁדַּי בְּדַבְּרוֹ! אֶלָּא מִשֶּׁהוּא מַגִּיעַ לֶחָצֵר הַחִיצוֹנָה הוּא נִפְסָק
sources.says: Rashi says you might think the voice was low, but the verse says it was like God speaking; rather, when it reached the outer court it stopped.

sources.quote: הקול לא היה נשמע אלא עד החצר החיצונה והוא עזרת הנשים ובהגיע שמה היה נפסק הקול
sources.says: Metzudat David says the voice was heard only up to the outer court, the women's court, and when it got there it stopped.

10:8.headline: "The form of a hand": Maimonides says תבנית means a built shape
10:8.body: Maimonides says תבנית comes from בנה, to build, and means an outline like square or round, so Hebrew never uses it of God. Radak says the words "appeared" and "form" show this was a prophetic vision, not cherubim with real hands.

sources.quote: משום ש"תבנית" הוא מונח הגזור מן "בנה", ומשמעותו מבנה הדבר ותכונתו
sources.says: Maimonides says תבנית is a word taken from "build" and means the structure and shape of a thing.

sources.quote: ולכן אין העברית מחילה כלל את הביטויים הללו על תיאורים הקשורים באלוה
sources.says: Maimonides says that is why Hebrew never applies these words to descriptions of God.

sources.quote: מה שאמר וירא ואמר תבנית להראות כי לא היה הכל אלא במראה הנבואה לא שיש לכרובים ידים ורגלים וכנפים כמשמעם
sources.says: Radak says the words "appeared" and "form" show it was all in a prophetic vision, not that cherubim have hands, feet and wings in the plain sense.

sources.quote: דבריו "תבנית" הם כדבריו "דמות"
sources.says: Maimonides says the word "form" here is like the word "likeness".

10:10.headline: A wheel inside a wheel rolls any way without turning
10:10.body: Metzudat David pictures two wheels crossed, one running east to west and one north to south. That way the chariot can roll in any direction without turning around.

sources.quote: והיו כמראית האופן העשוי בתוך האופן זה ממזרח למערב וזה מצפון לדרום שאז יכול הוא להתגלגל לכל רוח מבלי סבוב והחזרה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they looked like a wheel made inside a wheel, one east to west and one north to south, so it can roll toward any side without turning around.

10:12.headline: Wheels "full of eyes": real eyes, or many colors?
10:12.body: Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David say עינים here means colors, many shades all around. Maimonides weighs real eyes, colors, likenesses, or states, and Malbim reads them as God's watchful eyes.

sources.quote: עינים. גוונים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says "eyes" means colors.

sources.quote: היו מלאים הרבה גוונים מחולפים בכל סביבם
sources.says: Metzudat David says they were full of many changing colors all around.

sources.quote: אפשר שכוונתו היא שהוא מלא בעיניים ממש; ב) ואפשר שהוא בעל גוונים רבים
sources.says: Maimonides, on the wheels being full of eyes, says it may mean real eyes, or that they have many colors.

sources.quote: והאופנים גם הם מלאות עינים עיני ה' המשוטטים בהשגחה פרטיית
sources.says: Malbim says the wheels too are full of eyes, the eyes of God that roam in watching over each thing.

10:14.headline: The ox face became a cherub: an accuser cannot defend
10:14.body: In chapter 1 one face was an ox, which recalls the golden calf. Rashi and Metzudat David cite the sages: Ezekiel begged for it to change, since an accuser cannot act as defender.

sources.quote: הֵם הָיוּ פְּנֵי הַשּׁוֹר (יחזקאל א:י) שֶׁנֶּהֶפְכוּ לִכְרוּב
sources.says: Rashi says these were the ox faces of chapter 1, which were changed into a cherub.

sources.quote: יְחֶזְקֵאל בִּקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים וְהָפְכוּ לִכְרוּב, אָמַר לְפָנָיו רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם אֵין קָטֵיגוֹר נַעֲשֶׂה סָנֵיגוֹר
sources.says: Rashi quotes the sages: Ezekiel asked for mercy and it was changed to a cherub; he said, Master of the world, an accuser cannot become a defender.

sources.quote: כי פני השור יזכיר מעשה העגל שחטאו בו ישראל ונהפך פני השור לפני כרוב
sources.says: Metzudat David says the ox face would recall the calf with which Israel sinned, so the ox face was changed to a cherub face.

sources.quote: הרי שאמר במפורש שמה שאמר עליו "פני שור" הוא "פני הכרוב"; ו"כרוב" הוא אדם צעיר
sources.says: Maimonides says Ezekiel states outright that what he called the ox face is the cherub face, and a cherub is a young person.

10:15.headline: Same beings, new name: walking creatures, then flying cherubim
10:15.body: Malbim says by the river they were called חיות, creatures, because they walked, steering the world by its natural order. Here they fly above that order, so they are called cherubim, and Maimonides agrees the two are one.

sources.quote: כי אז השיג אותם כחיות מהלכות, ר"ל מנהיגים ע"פ סדרי המערכה, ופה השיג אותם מעופפים למעלה מן המערכה, לכן נשתנה ענינם עתה מחיות לכרובים
sources.says: Malbim says then he saw them as walking creatures, guiding by the order of nature, and here as flying above that order, so their name changed from creatures to cherubim.

sources.quote: אין זה ענין אחר אלא היא החיה בעצמה אשר ראיתי על נהר כבר
sources.says: Metzudat David says this is not something else but the very creature he saw at the river Kebar.

sources.quote: התברר שהחיות הן הכרובים, והכרובים הם החיות
sources.says: Maimonides says it is now clear that the creatures are the cherubim and the cherubim are the creatures.

10:22.headline: ואותם: "they themselves", or "their signs"
10:22.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak read ואותם as "and they themselves", the very same beings. Malbim reads it from אות, a sign: the marks by which the prophet knew them.

sources.quote: ואותם. ועצמם וכן והשיאו אותם עון אשמה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means "and themselves", as in "they will make them bear the sin".

sources.quote: ואותם. ועצמם כמו ויראו שוטרי בני ישראל אותם ברע
sources.says: Radak says it means "and themselves", as in "the officers of Israel saw themselves in trouble".

sources.quote: מלשון אות וסימן, הסימנים והאותיות שלהם שבם יוכרו לעין החוזה
sources.says: Malbim says it comes from אות, a sign: their marks and signs by which they are known to the one who sees them.

12:3.headline: "Yomam": by daylight, or day after day?
12:3.body: Radak and Malbim say יומם means while the sun is up, the opposite of night. Rashi, citing Rabbi Menachem, says every יומם in the Bible means day after day, over many days.

sources.quote: מן היות השמש על הארץ יקרא יומם אבל יום כולל פעמים היום והלילה
sources.says: Radak says the time when the sun is on the earth is called yomam, while yom sometimes includes both day and night.

sources.quote: כ"מ שנאמר יומם בא לילה עמו, והוא הפך של לילה
sources.says: Malbim says wherever yomam is said, night comes with it, and it is the opposite of night.

sources.quote: וכן כל ׳יומם׳ שבמקרא לשון ׳יום יום׳ הוא, דבר הנוהג ימים רבים, כך שמעתי משמו של רבי מנחם
sources.says: Rashi says every yomam in the Bible means day by day, something that goes on for many days, as he heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem.

12:3.headline: The exile's pack: a cup and a small kneading bowl
12:3.body: Rashi says Ezekiel packed a drinking cup and a small bowl for kneading dough. He was showing the people what to take, so they would not have to knead in holes in the ground full of gravel; they did not listen.

sources.quote: כלי לשתות, ומקידה קטנה (משנה שבת כד,ה) ללוש בה חררה
sources.says: Rashi says the exile's vessels were a drinking vessel and a small bowl to knead a flat cake in.

sources.quote: ולא יצטרכו ללוש בצק בגומא על גבי קרקע והחצצים נכנסים בתוכו; והם לא שמעו לו
sources.says: Rashi says this was so they would not need to knead dough in a pit in the ground where gravel gets in, but they did not listen to him.

sources.quote: תקן לך כלי גולה והם מקל ותרמיל וכוס וכד וקערה
sources.says: Radak says the exile's vessels are a staff, a pack, a cup, a jug and a bowl.

12:7.headline: He dug through the wall by hand, so no one would hear
12:7.body: Radak and Malbim say Ezekiel dug with his bare hands, not iron tools, so the sound would not be heard. Radak says Zedekiah's men did the same when they fled.

sources.quote: לא בכלי ברזל שחותרים בו כדי שלא ישמעו קולו
sources.says: Radak says he dug not with iron tools, so that the sound would not be heard.

sources.quote: וספר שעשה את המחתרת ביד בל ישמע קול מקבות וכלי ברזל
sources.says: Malbim says Ezekiel tells that he made the tunnel by hand so no sound of hammers and iron tools would be heard.

12:10.headline: Massa: a load to carry, here a prophecy
12:10.body: The word means something carried, and the prince will carry his pack on his shoulder. Rashi and Radak say that here it means a prophecy, about King Zedekiah.

sources.quote: על המלך צדקיהו אני מראה המשא הזה; לשון נבואה
sources.says: Rashi says God is showing this massa about King Zedekiah, and massa is a word for prophecy.

sources.quote: פירושו כתרגומו על רבא מטל נביאותא הדא בירושלם והנשיא הוא צדקיהו
sources.says: Radak follows the Aramaic, "this burden of prophecy is about the ruler in Jerusalem", and says the prince is Zedekiah.

12:11.headline: Exile and captivity are not the same thing
12:11.body: Radak and Malbim say there is a kind of exile where a person may go where he likes. Captivity is harsher: Malbim says it is going away with no return.

sources.quote: כי יש גולה שאינה שבי
sources.says: Radak says there is an exile that is not captivity.

sources.quote: יש גולה שיכול ללכת לכ"מ שירצה, ויש גולה שהוא שבוי בארץ שביו
sources.says: Malbim says there is an exile in which one can go wherever he wants, and an exile in which he is a captive in the land of his captors.

sources.quote: שהשבי קשה מן הגולה שהוא ע"מ שלא ישוב עוד מארץ שביו
sources.says: Malbim says captivity is harder than exile, since it means never coming back from the land of captivity.

12:12.headline: He covers his face: from shame, or a sign of blindness
12:12.body: Rashi and Radak say Zedekiah covers his face from shame at fleeing the city he ruled. The Aramaic, quoted by Radak, reads it as a hint that his eyes would be put out and he would not see the land.

sources.quote: פניו יכסה. מחמת כלימה, שהוא בורח מן העיר לילה
sources.says: Rashi says he will cover his face out of shame, because he flees the city at night.

sources.quote: כי בשת הוא לו שיברח מן העיר שהיה מולך עליה
sources.says: Radak says it is shameful for him to flee the city he ruled.

sources.quote: חלף דחב ינקרון ית עינוהי ולא יחזי ית ארעא
sources.says: Radak quotes the Aramaic translation: "because he sinned they will put out his eyes, and he will not see the land".

12:13.headline: God's net: a deer that led the soldiers to Zedekiah's tunnel
12:13.body: Rashi and Radak bring a midrash: Zedekiah fled through a cave from his house to the plains of Jericho. God sent a deer running over the cave, the soldiers chased it, and they caught him as he came out.

sources.quote: מערה היתה לו מביתו עד ערבות יריחו
sources.says: Rashi says Zedekiah had a cave from his house to the plains of Jericho.

sources.quote: הביא צבי אחד לפני חיל כשדים, והלך לפניהם על גג המערה והם רודפים אותו
sources.says: Rashi says God brought a deer before the Chaldean army, and it went ahead of them on the roof of the cave while they chased it.

sources.quote: וכשהגיע על פתח המערה היה צדקיהו יוצא ולכדוהו וזהו שאמר יחזקאל ופרשתי
sources.says: Radak says that when they reached the mouth of the cave Zedekiah was coming out and they caught him, and that is what Ezekiel meant by "I will spread My net".

12:13.headline: Metzudah: a hunter's trap, or a fortress
12:13.body: Metzudat Zion says it is a hunting tool, like a net. Malbim says the word can come from צוד, to hunt, or from מצד, a stronghold, and both fit: Zedekiah was caught, then held in a fortress prison.

sources.quote: שם כלי מכלי הצדיה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the name of a hunting tool.

sources.quote: יש ששרשו מצד ומורה על חוזק ומבצר
sources.says: Malbim says sometimes the root is "metzad", meaning strength and fortress.

sources.quote: ויש ששרשו צוד, ומורה על שצדים שם
sources.says: Malbim says sometimes the root is "tzud", meaning a place where one hunts.

sources.quote: וצדקיהו הושם במבצר
sources.says: Malbim says Zedekiah was put in a fortress.

12:13.headline: Brought to Babylon, yet he would never see it
12:13.body: The verse says Zedekiah will be taken to Babylon but will not see it. Rashi and Radak explain: the king of Babylon blinded him at Riblah before bringing him there.

sources.quote: כי ברבלה בארץ חמת דבר אתו משפטים ועור את עיניו, ואחר כך הביאו לבבל
sources.says: Rashi says that at Riblah in the land of Hamath the king judged him and blinded his eyes, and afterward brought him to Babylon.

sources.quote: כי מלך בבל עור עיניו ברבלתה
sources.says: Radak says the king of Babylon blinded his eyes at Riblah.

12:14.headline: Agafav: his "wings", meaning the troops at his sides
12:14.body: Rashi says the word means his officers, and Radak says his troops. Radak's father took it from the Aramaic גפין, wings, since an army's flanks are called wings, as in Isaiah 8:8.

sources.quote: וכל אגפיו. שריו. ומנחם פתר בו לשון כנפים
sources.says: Rashi says "agafav" means his officers, and Menachem explained it as wings.

sources.quote: ואדני אבי ז"ל פירש אגפיו אגפיך האל"ף נוספת והוא מתרגום כנפים גפין והחיילות יקראו כנפים
sources.says: Radak says his father explained that the aleph is extra and the word comes from the Aramaic for wings, "gappin", and troops are called wings.

sources.quote: ועל התפשטות החיילות יאמר וכמ״ש מוטות כנפיו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it describes the spread of the troops, as in "the spread of its wings".

12:18.headline: Rogez and de'agah: fear of now, worry about later
12:18.body: Malbim says רוגז is trembling over what is happening now, and דאגה is worry about what is coming. So Ezekiel eats and drinks both afraid and anxious.

sources.quote: הרוגז על ההוה, והדאגה על העתיד
sources.says: Malbim says rogez is about the present and de'agah is about the future.

sources.quote: ברגזה. ענין חרדה ופחד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says rogzah means trembling and fear.

12:22.headline: Why their saying is called a "mashal"
12:22.body: Radak says it is called a proverb because it was always in their mouths, like a proverb people repeat. Malbim says they borrowed it from star-gazers, whose predictions fail as time passes.

sources.quote: וקרא הדבר הזה משל ואף על פי שהוא מליצה לפי שהיה הדבר הזה בפיהם תמיד כמשל הנשא בפי האדם תמיד
sources.says: Radak says the verse calls this saying a mashal because it was always in their mouths, like a proverb a person always carries in his mouth.

sources.quote: שהם לקחו משל ודמיון ממה שקרה להגדת הוברי שמים החוזים בכוכבים, שלפעמים לא יבוא דבריהם
sources.says: Malbim says they took the comparison from what happens to the predictions of star-gazers, whose words sometimes do not come true.

12:25.headline: First "it will be done", then "I will do it"
12:25.body: The verse first says the word "will be done", then "I will do it". Radak says the second phrase is there so no one says it happened by chance: God Himself does what He said.

sources.quote: תחילה אמר ויעשה ואחר כך ועשיתיו שלא תאמר יעשה הדבר דרך מקרה אלא אני אעשה הדבר כמו שדברתי אותו טרם באו
sources.says: Radak says that first the verse says "it will be done" and afterward "I will do it", so you will not say it happened by chance, but that God does it as He said before it came.

12:27.headline: "For many days and far-off times": two different ideas of time
12:27.body: Malbim says ימים means a stretch of time, while עתים means the moment something happens. So the people claim the vision covers a long span and its moment is far away.

sources.quote: ימים מציין המשך הזמן, ועתים מציין חלות הדבר בנקודה מיוחדת מן הזמן
sources.says: Malbim says "days" marks a stretch of time, and "times" marks the moment something happens at one point in time.

sources.quote: אמרו שהעת שיחול הדבר הוא רחוק באחרית הימים
sources.says: Malbim says the people said the time when the thing will happen is far off, at the end of days.

13:2.headline: An odd vowel marks prophets who only act the part
13:2.body: Here הנבאים, 'who prophesy', has a vowel found nowhere else. Radak notes it is one of a kind. Malbim says the form itself shows they are not real prophets; they only make themselves seem so.

sources.quote: הנבאים. בקמץ הבי"ת ולית כוותיה
sources.says: Radak says the word is written with a qamatz under the ב, and there is no other like it.

sources.quote: וכן בנפעל מורה שאינם נבאים באמת רק עושים עצמם כן
sources.says: Malbim says this form shows they are not prophets in truth but only make themselves out to be.

13:4.headline: Why the false prophets are like foxes in ruins
13:4.body: Rashi: when a man comes to the gap in a ruin, the fox runs out through another gap; it never stands in the breach to fight. Radak: foxes slip through gaps in a vineyard fence and ruin the vines, as the false prophets ruin Israel.

sources.quote: בּוֹרֵחַ הַשּׁוּעָל עַל דֶּרֶךְ פֶּרֶץ אַחֶרֶת, וְאֵינוֹ עוֹמֵד בַּפֶּרֶץ לְהִלָּחֵם
sources.says: Rashi says the fox runs away through another breach and does not stand in the breach to fight.

sources.quote: כמו השועלים הנכנסים במקום הנפרץ בגדר הכרם ומשחיתים הכרמים
sources.says: Radak says the prophets are like foxes that come in through a break in the vineyard fence and ruin the vineyards.

13:9.headline: Shut out of the 'council' of God's people, or its hidden good?
13:9.body: סוד can mean a gathering or a secret. Metzudat Zion reads it as the gathering of God's people. Radak follows the Targum: the false prophets will have no share in the hidden good stored up for God's people.

sources.quote: בסוד. ענין קבוץ ואסיפה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says סוד here means a gathering.

sources.quote: פירושו כתרגומו ברז טב דגניז לעמי לא יהון
sources.says: Radak explains it like the Targum: they will not be in the good secret hidden away for God's people.

13:10.headline: 'Because, and because': a doubled word for a doubled punishment
13:10.body: The verse says יען וביען, 'because, and by because'. Radak says the doubling makes the punishment stronger. Malbim reads it as punishment within punishment: one for the false words and one for what they led people to do.

sources.quote: יען וביען. הכפל לחזק העונש
sources.says: Radak says the doubled word is there to strengthen the punishment.

sources.quote: וז"ש יען וביען ר"ל עונש תוך עונש, עונש כפול על פרי המעשה חוץ מן המעשה עצמו
sources.says: Malbim says it means punishment within punishment: a double penalty for the results of the deed, beyond the deed itself.

13:10.headline: 'Misled' spelled with ט, the only time in the Bible
13:10.body: Everywhere else in Tanach, 'to lead astray' is spelled with ת, as in התעם. Radak notes this is the only place with ט, the spelling later used in the Mishnah and Talmud. He says the two letters can stand in for each other.

sources.quote: זה לבדו בטי"ת במקר' כי במקרא ישתמשו בענין זה בתי"ו תעה לבבי כי רוח זנונים התעם וכן כלם בתי"ו אבל במשנה וגמרא נשתמשו בענין הזה בטי"ת
sources.says: Radak says this is the only time Scripture spells the word with ט; elsewhere Scripture uses ת, but the Mishnah and Talmud use ט.

13:10.headline: חיץ: a flimsy partition, a word known from the sages' Hebrew
13:10.body: חיץ appears only here. Metzudat Zion and Malbim explain it from the later word מחיצה, a partition, like the Mishnah's partition of reeds. Radak calls it a poor, weak wall: the false prophets' promise of peace.

sources.quote: חיץ. הוא מל׳ מחיצה המוזכר בדרז״ל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חיץ comes from מחיצה, a partition, the word used by the sages.

sources.quote: מענין מחיצת הקנים בלשון משנה, שחוצה המקום לשנים
sources.says: Malbim says it is like the reed partition of Mishnaic Hebrew, which splits a place in two.

sources.quote: נביא השקר בהבטיחו על שקר דומה למי שבנה חיץ והיא מחיצה גרועה
sources.says: Radak says the false prophet who promises a lie is like someone who builds a חיץ, a poor partition.

13:10.headline: Plaster as worthless as food without salt
13:10.body: תפל usually means bland, as in Job's 'food without salt'. Metzudat Zion says anything not properly made is called תפל. Rashi says it is earth that looks like lime but does not last in the rain; Radak's father said unbaked bricks.

sources.quote: כל דבר שאינו מתוקן כל צרכו קרוי תפל וכן היאכל תפל מבלי מלח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says anything not properly prepared is called תפל, as in 'can bland food be eaten without salt'.

sources.quote: קַרְקַע הַדּוֹמֶה לְסִיד, וְאֵינוֹ מִתְקַיֵּם לִפְנֵי הַגְּשָׁמִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is earth that looks like lime and does not hold up against the rain.

sources.quote: ואדני אבי ז"ל פירש תפל לבנים שאינם שרופים
sources.says: Radak says his father explained תפל as bricks that were not fired.

13:11.headline: Hail like crystal, or hail held in the air for Moses
13:11.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion split אלגביש into אל גביש: hail like גביש, crystal, a precious stone. Rashi also cites the sages, who heard על גב איש, 'for a man's sake': the hail Moses stopped in midair over Egypt.

sources.quote: הוא כמו שתי מלות אל גביש ור״ל אבני ברד דומות אל גביש והוא אבן יקר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word is like two words, אל גביש: hailstones that look like גביש, a precious stone.

sources.quote: שֶׁעָמְדוּ בָאֲוִיר עַל גַּב אִישׁ, וְזֶהוּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: these are hailstones that stood in the air for the sake of a man, Moses, and never reached the ground.

13:18.headline: Magic cushions on the arm, a dark copy of tefillin
13:18.body: כסתות are small cushions. Rashi says the women sewed them, hung them on the arms of people who came to ask, and divined with them. Malbim sees a mirror of tefillin, worn on arm and head, used to trap people instead of binding them to God.

sources.quote: כְּמִין כְּסָתוֹת קְטַנּוֹת הָיוּ תּוֹפְרוֹת וְתוֹלוֹת לַנִּשְׁאָלִים אֲלֵיהֶם עַל אַצִּילֵי יְדֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they sewed small cushions and hung them on the arms of those who came to ask them.

sources.quote: שכמו שבקדושה מניחים תפילין על היד כנגד הלב לשעבד תאות ומחשבת הלב לה'
sources.says: Malbim says that just as tefillin go on the arm by the heart to bind the heart to God, these women put cushions on the arm to capture people's hearts.

13:18.headline: Not 'my hands': here ידי simply means 'hands'
13:18.body: ידי looks like 'my hands', but the prophet is not speaking of his own arms. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it means 'hands' with the final ם dropped: the women tied cushions on everyone's arms.

sources.quote: אַצִּילֵי יָדַי. כְּמוֹ ׳אַצִּילֵי יָדַיִם׳
sources.says: Rashi says אצילי ידי means the same as אצילי ידים, 'the joints of hands'.

sources.quote: ידי. כמו ידים ונפלה המ״ם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ידי is like ידים, with the ם dropped.

13:18.headline: Rashi admits he does not know what these head coverings were
13:18.body: מספחות appears only in this chapter. Rashi says he does not know what they are, but since God will 'tear' them, they must be cloth. Metzudat Zion says they are veils, named for how they cling to the head.

sources.quote: וְלֹא יָדַעְתִּי מַה הֵם, וּמִתּוֹךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְקָרַעְתִּי אֹתָם״ אוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל בֶּגֶד
sources.says: Rashi says he does not know what they are, but because the text says 'I will tear them', he says they were made of cloth.

sources.quote: ולפי שהן נדבקות ונצמדות על הראש אמר מספחות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are like veils, and are called מספחות because they stick close to the head.

13:18.headline: Why a person is called a 'height'
13:18.body: The veils go 'on the head of every קומה', literally every height. Metzudat David says a person is called קומה because only humans walk upright. Radak says the women made the people who asked stand up while they worked their magic.

sources.quote: ויקרא האדם קומה על כי הוא לבד הולך בקומה זקופה ולא כן שאר הבריות
sources.says: Metzudat David says a person is called קומה because only a person walks upright, unlike other creatures.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר קומה לפי שהיו מעמידות אותם על רגליהם בעוד שהיו עושות המעשה
sources.says: Radak says it says קומה because the women stood the people on their feet while doing the act.

13:19.headline: Fistfuls of barley: their fee, or part of the spell?
13:19.body: שעלי means fistfuls, as in Isaiah's 'who measured the waters in his fist'. Radak says the barley and bread were the women's pay. He also brings a view that they put them inside the cushions to work the magic.

sources.quote: בשעלי. כן יקרא האגרוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שעל is the word for a fist.

sources.quote: נותנים להם מלא אגרוף שעורים או פת לחם ויש מפרשים כי השעורים והלחם היו נותנות תוך הכסתות ובהם היו עושות המעשה
sources.says: Radak says people paid them a fistful of barley or a piece of bread, and some say the barley and bread went inside the cushions for the magic.

13:20.headline: Souls made to 'fly': to ruin, or raised from the grave?
13:20.body: לפרחות means 'to fly'. Rashi says the women send souls flying to Gehinnom. Radak brings a view that they raised the dead, whose souls flew up from their graves into the air.

sources.quote: לִהְיוֹת פּוֹרְחוֹת עַל יְדֵיכֶן לְגֵיהִנֹּם
sources.says: Rashi says the souls fly off to Gehinnom because of the women.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים הענין הזה בדרישת המתים שהיו הנשים בעלות אוב מעלות נפשות המתים בדבריהן ומפרשים לפורחות בעבור אותן נפשות שאומר שהיו מעלות מקבריהן ופורחות באויר
sources.says: Radak says some explain the passage as raising the dead, reading 'to fly' as the souls brought up from their graves flying in the air.

16:3.headline: Where you lived, or where you came from?
16:3.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read מכרתיך as מגורותיך, "your dwellings", since ג and כ can swap. Rashi adds that Menachem read it as "your origins", like the word in Jacob's blessing of Simeon and Levi.

sources.quote: כמו מגורותיך. ומנחם חברו לשון ׳תולדה׳
sources.says: Rashi says the word means your dwellings, and that Menachem grouped it with words for birth and origin.

sources.quote: מגורותיך כי גיכ״ק מתחלף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means your dwellings, since the letters ג and כ swap.

16:4.headline: Washed smooth, or washed for delight?
16:4.body: Metzudat Zion reads למשעי as "to smooth", the word the Targum uses for Jacob's smooth neck. Rashi adds that Menachem tied it to שעשועים, delight.

sources.quote: ענין החלקה כי חלקת צואריו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means smoothing, as the Targum translates "the smooth part of his neck".

sources.quote: ומנחם חבר למשעי לשון שעשועים
sources.says: Rashi says it means cleaning to a shine, and that Menachem linked it to delight.

16:6.headline: Said twice for the two bloods that freed Israel
16:6.body: God says "in your blood, live" twice. Rashi explains that Israel was freed from Egypt through two kinds of blood: the Passover lamb and circumcision.

sources.quote: וששנה לומר שני פעמים, לפי שבדם פסח ודם מילה נגאלו
sources.says: Rashi says the phrase is repeated because Israel was redeemed through the blood of the Passover offering and the blood of circumcision.

sources.quote: ורבותינו ז"ל דרשו הכפל לדם פסח ודם מילה
sources.says: Radak says the plain reason for doubling is to give her courage, and that the sages read it as the two bloods of Passover and circumcision.

16:7.headline: Finest jewels, or the body's own signs of growing up?
16:7.body: Radak reads בעדי עדיים as the finest jewels, the silver and gold Israel took from Egypt. His father read it as the body's own adornment, the signs of growing up that the verse lists next.

sources.quote: והעדי הוא כלי כסף וכלי זהב ושמלות שנצלו את מצרים
sources.says: Radak says the jewels are the silver, gold and clothing Israel took from Egypt.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש עדי עדים עדי הגוף
sources.says: Radak says his father read it as the adornment of the body itself.

sources.quote: אבל דונש פתר אותו לשון ״עדי״
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem read the word as "forever", but Dunash read it as jewelry.

16:7.headline: Naked means bare of good deeds
16:7.body: The girl is "naked and bare". Rashi, following the Mekhilta, says it means Israel in Egypt had no mitzvot of its own, and Radak says they had left the ways of their forefathers.

sources.quote: ואת ערם ועריה. מן המצות
sources.says: Rashi says "naked and bare" means bare of commandments.

sources.quote: או יהיה דרך משל שהיו ערומים ממצות האבות לשמור דרך ה'
sources.says: Radak says it may mean they were bare of their forefathers' ways of keeping God's path.

16:10.headline: Silk that never moves away: the clouds of glory
16:10.body: משי usually means silk. A midrash in Rashi hears ימיש, "move away", in it: these were the clouds of glory that never moved away from Israel.

sources.quote: ואכסך משי אלו שבעת ענני כבוד, דכתיב ״לא ימיש עמוד הענן יומם״
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that the silk is the seven clouds of glory, as it says the pillar of cloud did not move away by day.

16:18.headline: Written "I gave": God's own gifts made the sin possible
16:18.body: The word is read נתת, "you gave", but written נתתי, "I gave". Radak says the written form admits: I caused this, because I gave you the oil and incense, like the saying "who made you kick me? The feed I gave you."

sources.quote: והכתוב כאילו נתתי לפניהם אני גרמתי לך כיון שנתתי לך
sources.says: Radak says the written form reads as if God says: I caused it, since I gave these things to you.

16:19.headline: Even after the golden calf, the manna kept falling
16:19.body: Rashi brings a midrash: on the day of the golden calf, Israel set manna before the idol. Yet "and it was": the manna still came down the next day.

sources.quote: יום שעשו את העגל, ירד להם המן, ונתנו ממנו לפני העגל, ואף על פי כן ויהי – ביום מחר, ולא פסק
sources.says: Rashi says that on the day they made the calf the manna fell and they offered some to the calf, and still it came the next day and did not stop.

16:22.headline: Written "I did not remember": God overlooked sins to come
16:22.body: The word is read זכרת, "you did not remember" God's kindness. Written זכרתי, Radak says, it means God did not hold against young Israel the sins it would later commit.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר אני לא זכרתי לך בימי נעוריך מה שאת עתידה לחטא
sources.says: Radak says the written form means God did not count against Israel in its youth the sins it would commit later.

16:29.headline: Canaan here means a land of traders
16:29.body: Babylon is not in Canaan. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say כנען here means "trader", as in Hosea, so the verse calls Chaldea a land of merchants.

sources.quote: ולי נראה: כנען – כמו סוחר
sources.says: Rashi says that in his view כנען here means a merchant, so Chaldea is called a land of traders.

sources.quote: ענינו תגר וסוחר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כנען means a dealer and merchant.

16:30.headline: A heart named for a flame of desire
16:30.body: לבתך is an odd feminine form of לב, heart. Radak says the feminine form is a put-down, and Malbim hears לבת, a flame, the fire of desire burning in her.

sources.quote: זכר לב בלשון נקבה לגריעות
sources.says: Radak says the word heart is put in a feminine form to belittle.

sources.quote: וי"ל שקורא הלב לבת, ע"ש לבת אש התאוה הבוער בו
sources.says: Malbim suggests the heart is called לבת after the flame of desire burning in it.

16:43.headline: Wickedness, or a plan that can be good or bad?
16:43.body: Metzudat Zion reads הזמה as shame and wickedness. Rashi says every זמה in Scripture means a plan, good or bad: Israel made no plan to turn back from its sins.

sources.quote: כל זמה שבמקרא לשון עצה הוא, יש לטובה ויש לרעה
sources.says: Rashi says every זמה in Scripture means a plan, sometimes for good and sometimes for bad.

sources.quote: הזמה. ענין גנות ורשע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means disgrace and wickedness.

16:45.headline: Your mother a Hittite? No, Sarah only lived among them
16:45.body: The Targum, quoted by Rashi, turns the verse around: Sarah lived among the Hittites and did not act like them. Radak says Israel's real parents were righteous, but Israel learned from the land instead.

sources.quote: הלא אמכון שרה ביני חתאי הות ולא עבדת כעובדיהון
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: your mother Sarah lived among the Hittites and did not act as they did.

sources.quote: ולא כן אלא אמכן ואביכן היו צדיקים אברהם ושרה
sources.says: Radak says Israel's mother and father were not really Hittite and Amorite but righteous: Abraham and Sarah.

16:47.headline: "You did not walk in their ways" means "if only you had"
16:47.body: Rashi reads ולא here as a wish: if only Jerusalem had walked in Sodom's ways and done no worse. He shows the same use of לא in other verses.

sources.quote: והלואי בדרכיהן הלכת, ולא התעבת יותר מהם
sources.says: Rashi says it means: if only you had walked in their ways and not done worse than them.

16:61.headline: Not because you kept the covenant, and not your inheritance
16:61.body: Rashi first reads it as: I give you this not because you kept my covenant, but out of mercy. A midrash he brings reads it as: these lands were not part of what Abraham was promised.

sources.quote: ולא משמרך את הברית אשר כרתי אתך, אלא בחסדי וברחמי
sources.says: Rashi says it is not because Israel kept the covenant but because of God's kindness and mercy.

sources.quote: לא נתתיה לאברהם אביך בין הבתרים
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that these places were not given to Abraham at the covenant between the pieces.

17:2.headline: A riddle is something that sharpens the mind
17:2.body: חידה means a riddle, a hidden saying. Malbim ties the word to חידוד, sharpening, because a riddle sharpens the listener's mind. Radak says only the wise will understand it.

sources.quote: ומתאחד עם חידוד, כי יחדד השכל
sources.says: Malbim says the word for riddle is related to the word for sharpening, since a riddle sharpens the mind.

sources.quote: החידה הוא הדבר הסתום יבינו ממנו דבר אחר
sources.says: Radak says a riddle is a hidden saying from which another meaning is understood, and only the wise will grasp it.

17:4.headline: Young branches are called 'sucklings', soft like a nursing child
17:4.body: יניקות comes from the word for nursing. Radak says the soft top shoots of a tree get this name because they are tender like a baby that still nurses.

sources.quote: הענפים הרכים והם העליונים יקראו יניקות כמו הנער היונק שהוא רך
sources.says: Radak says the soft top branches are called יניקות, like a nursing child, who is soft.

sources.quote: ענפיו הרכות והקטנות כמו ויעל כיונק לפני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means the soft small branches, and compares Isaiah's 'he grew up like a sapling'.

17:4.headline: 'Land of Canaan' here means a land of merchants: Babylon
17:4.body: The eagle carries the treetop to 'the land of Canaan', yet the story is about Babylon. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read כנען as a word for trader, so it means a land of merchants.

sources.quote: אֶל אֶרֶץ תַּגָּרִים, הִיא בָּבֶל
sources.says: Rashi says it means a land of traders, which is Babylon.

sources.quote: ענינו תגר וסוחר כמו כנען בידו מאזני מרמה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כנען means a trader or merchant, as in Hosea's 'a trader with false scales in his hand'.

sources.quote: לפיכך דמה אותה הארץ והיא בבל לארץ כנען
sources.says: Radak explains Targum Jonathan's reading: Babylon is likened to Canaan, which served no other king before Israel came.

17:6.headline: Odd spelling: thin branches, or boughs that bear fruit
17:6.body: The word is spelled with its letters in an unusual order. Metzudat Zion says it is פארות, thin branches, with letters swapped. Malbim reads it from פרה, to bear fruit.

sources.quote: פראות כתיב רי"ש קודם לאל"ף
sources.says: Radak notes the word is written with the resh before the aleph.

sources.quote: היא הפוך מן פארות והם הענפים הדקים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is פארות with letters reversed, meaning thin branches.

sources.quote: ר"ל סעיפים נושאי פרי, ושרשו פרה כי שורש פרי
sources.says: Malbim says it means boughs that bear fruit, from the root of the word for fruit.

17:7.headline: The vine's roots 'hungered' for Egypt, or gathered toward it
17:7.body: כפנה appears only here. Rashi gives two readings: from כפן, famine, so the roots hungered for the second eagle. Or it is כנפה with letters swapped, meaning gathered.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן רְעָבוֹן, כְּמוֹ ״לְשֹׁד וּלְכָפָן״
sources.says: Rashi first reads it as hunger, as in Job's 'at destruction and famine'.

sources.quote: וְכָפְנָה הוּא כְּמוֹ כָּנְפָה
sources.says: Rashi then gives a second reading: it is the word for gathering with two letters reversed.

sources.quote: ענין אסיפה ובדרז״ל יש כנופיא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion reads it as gathering, like the sages' word כנופיא for a crowd.

sources.quote: שהוא על תאות המזון בעת הרעב
sources.says: Malbim reads it as craving food in famine, so the vine craved water from the second eagle.

17:9.headline: A one-time verb read as 'cut off', with letters swapped
17:9.body: יקוסס appears nowhere else. The commentators read it as יקוצץ, he will cut off, since ס and צ can trade places. The fruit cut off stands for Zedekiah's sons.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ יְקוֹצֵץ, הֵם בְּנֵי צִדְקִיָּהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'will cut off', and the fruit is Zedekiah's sons.

sources.quote: ענין כריתה והוא כמו יקוצץ כי זסשר״ץ מתחלפים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means cutting, like יקוצץ, because the letters ז ס ש ר צ can swap.

sources.quote: אין לו ריע וענינו כמו יקוצץ
sources.says: Malbim says the word has no twin elsewhere and means 'will cut off'.

17:9.headline: Here טרף means leaves, called food for worms
17:9.body: טרף usually means prey, but here it means leaves. Metzudat Zion points to the Aramaic Targum, which calls fig leaves טרפי. Malbim cites a view that fresh leaves get the name because they are food for worms and flies.

sources.quote: עלים כי עלי תאנה (בראשי׳ ג) ת״א טרפי תאנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means leaves, since the Targum translates 'fig leaves' as טרפי תאנה.

sources.quote: שטרף הם העלים הלחים שהם טרף ומזון לתולעים ולזבובים
sources.says: Malbim quotes a scholar who says טרף means fresh leaves, which are food for worms and flies.

17:18.headline: 'He gave his hand': a sworn pledge, or giving up the fight
17:18.body: Rashi reads 'he gave his hand' as a solemn promise, so breaking it was a broken oath. Malbim offers other readings: Zedekiah stopped fighting yet kept rebelling, or Nebuchadnezzar offered his hand in peace.

sources.quote: הִבְטִיחַ בֶּאֱמוּנָה, וְנָשָׂא יָדוֹ בִּבְרִית
sources.says: Rashi says he made a faithful promise and raised his hand in a covenant.

sources.quote: ר"ל שחדל להלחם ועדן עמד במרדו ויל"פ שנ"נ נתן לו יד להשלים
sources.says: Malbim says it means he stopped fighting yet still rebelled, or that Nebuchadnezzar offered him a hand to make peace.

sources.quote: כי נתינת היד הוא קיום אהבה ושלום
sources.says: Radak says giving the hand confirms friendship and peace.

17:20.headline: God does not just judge him, He argues the case
17:20.body: ונשפטתי looks like 'I will judge', but the commentators read it as 'I will argue with him'. God is pictured as a party pressing a case against Zedekiah in Babylon.

sources.quote: וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּי. וְאֶתְוַכַּח עִמּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'I will argue with him'.

sources.quote: ענין ויכוח וכן כי באש ה׳ נשפט
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means debate, as in Isaiah's 'for by fire the Lord will contend'.

sources.quote: וכאילו אני נשפט ומתוכח עמו
sources.says: Radak says it is as if God enters a lawsuit and argues with him about his betrayal.

18:2.headline: Sour unripe grapes stand for the fathers' sins
18:2.body: The exiles have a saying: the fathers eat בסר and the children's teeth go blunt. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say בסר is fruit that has not yet ripened. The Targum drops the picture and says plainly: the fathers sinned and the sons are punished.

sources.quote: אָבוֹת יֹאכְלוּ בֹסֶר. פְּרִי עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבַּשֵּׁל
sources.says: Rashi says בסר is fruit that has not yet ripened.

sources.quote: כן יקרא פרי שלא נגמר בשולו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says fruit that has not finished ripening is called this.

sources.quote: אֲבָהָתָא חָטָן וּבְנַיָא לְקָן
sources.says: The Targum renders the saying as 'the fathers sinned and the sons are punished'.

18:7.headline: A pledge taken for a debt, given back by nightfall
18:7.body: חבלה is something a lender takes as security for a loan. Rashi says the good man gives back the cloak he took by sunset, as Exodus 22:25 commands. Radak says he returns it to the poor man.

sources.quote: אִם חָבַל שַׂלְמַת רֵעֵהוּ בְּחוֹבוֹ, יָשִׁיב אוֹתָהּ לוֹ כְּבֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says if he took his neighbor's cloak as a pledge for a debt, he gives it back by sunset.

sources.quote: בחבולה שהיה לו בחובו ישיב אותה לעני
sources.says: Radak says he gives the pledge he held for the debt back to the poor man.

sources.quote: ענין משכון כמו אם חבל תחבל שלמת רעך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a pledge, as in Exodus 22:25.

18:8.headline: Two words for interest: money and food, or one sin twice
18:8.body: The verse names נשך and תרבית, both kinds of interest on a loan. Metzudat Zion says נשך is interest on money and תרבית is interest on food. Radak quotes the sages: they are one thing, named twice so the lender breaks two laws.

sources.quote: לשון נשך נאמר בכסף ותרבית באוכל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נשך is said of money and תרבית of food.

sources.quote: אמרו רז"ל הוא נשך הוא תרבית ולא חלקו עליו הכתוב אלא לעבור עליו בשני לאוין
sources.says: Radak says the sages taught they are the same thing, split in two only so the lender breaks two commands.

18:10.headline: 'Brother' or 'one'? A two-letter word read two ways
18:10.body: The verse says ועשה אח. The Targum, Rashi and Metzudat David read אח as 'brother': he does one of these wrongs to his brother. Radak reads אח as a short form of אחד, 'one': he commits any one of these sins.

sources.quote: אח כמו אחד
sources.says: Radak says אח is the same as אחד, 'one'.

sources.quote: ופירוש ועשה אח ועשה עון אחד
sources.says: Radak says the phrase means he commits one sin.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְיַעֲבִד לַאֲחוֹהִי מֵחֲדָא מֵאִילֵּין״
sources.says: Rashi cites the Targum: 'he does to his brother one of these'.

sources.quote: ועשה לאחיו מאחד מאלה הנזכרים כגזל וכדומה
sources.says: Metzudat David says he does one of these wrongs, like robbery, to his brother.

18:14.headline: He saw his father's sins, then truly saw them
18:14.body: The son saw (וירא) his father's sins, and saw (ויראה) and did not copy them. Malbim says the first is seeing with the eyes and the second is seeing with the mind. Rashi says he saw in his heart that it was not good.

sources.quote: ויראה הראשון ראיית החוש, והשני ראיית השכל
sources.says: Malbim says the first 'saw' is seeing with the senses and the second is seeing with the mind.

sources.quote: רָאָה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁאֵין טוֹב לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says he saw in his heart that it is not good to act that way.

sources.quote: וירא בראיית שכלו כי רע ומר דרך אביו
sources.says: Malbim says he saw with his mind that his father's way was bad and bitter.

18:25.headline: Is God's way 'not fair', or 'not made clear to us'?
18:25.body: The people say God's way לא יתכן. Malbim says תכן means measured exactly, with nothing extra and nothing missing, so they are calling it unfair. Rashi reads it as 'not set right'. The Targum reads it as 'not explained to us'.

sources.quote: פעל תכן הוא על דבר השוה במדה במשקל בלי עודף ומגרעת
sources.says: Malbim says the verb תכן is used for something even in measure and weight, with nothing extra or missing.

sources.quote: לֹא יִתָּכֵן. כְּמוֹ: לֹא יִתָּקֵן
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'is not set right'.

sources.quote: לָא מַפְרְשַׁן לָנָא אוֹרְחַת טוּבָא דַייָ
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the way of the LORD's goodness is not explained to us'.

18:30.headline: Turn back, and turn others back too
18:30.body: שובו means 'return yourselves'. Rashi says והשיבו means bring others back too, and Metzudat David says your wives and children. Malbim says it means turning your past sins themselves into good.

sources.quote: שׁוּבוּ אַתֶּם, וְהָשִׁיבוּ אֶת אֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi says: return yourselves, and bring others back.

sources.quote: שובו אתם בעצמיכם והשיבו את נשיכם ובניכם
sources.says: Metzudat David says: return yourselves, and bring back your wives and children.

sources.quote: רק שתשיבו את המעשים הרעים ופשעיכם הקודמים אל הטוב עד שיהיו מהעונות זכיות
sources.says: Malbim says it means turning your past bad deeds back to good, until the sins become merits.

18:32.headline: The sinner is called 'the dead man' while still alive
18:32.body: God says He does not want the death of המת, 'the dead one'. Radak and Metzudat Zion say the sinner is called dead because of how he will end. The Targum says 'one who deserves to die'.

sources.quote: במות המת. קראו מת ע״ש סופו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says he is called dead because of his end.

sources.quote: כי לא אחפוץ במות המת. על שם סופו
sources.says: Radak says he is named for his end.

sources.quote: בְמוֹתָא דְחַיָב לִמְמָת
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the death of one who is liable to die'.

19:2.headline: Your mother, a lioness: the mother of a royal line
19:2.body: Radak says the lion is king of the beasts, so the lioness is the mother of kingship: here, the house of David. He notes the word stands for לביאה, lioness. The Targum says the mother is the people of Israel.

sources.quote: והמשילה ללביא והיא אם האריות ואריה מלך החיות והלביאה אם המלוכה לפיכך המשיל בהם מלכות בית דוד
sources.says: Radak says the lioness is the mother of lions and of kingship, so she stands for the royal house of David.

sources.quote: מַה כְּנִשְׁתָּא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל דַהֲוַת דַמְיָא לְלַיְתָא
sources.says: The Targum says the mother is the congregation of Israel, which was like a lioness.

19:5.headline: The second cub, Jehoiakim: made a young lion by others
19:5.body: Rashi says the second cub is Jehoiakim. Malbim says he was weak by nature, and only the people made him into a 'young lion'.

sources.quote: וַתִּקַּח אֶחָד מִגּוּרֶיהָ. יְהוֹיָקִים
sources.says: Rashi says the second cub is Jehoiakim.

sources.quote: הוא לא היה כפיר כי היה חלוש בטבעו, רק העם שמו אותו שיהיה כפיר
sources.says: Malbim says he was not a young lion by nature, being weak; the people set him up as one.

19:11.headline: Staff and scepter: the office, and the men who enforce it
19:11.body: The verse uses both מטה and שבט, two words for a rod. Malbim says שבט stands for the office of ruling, and מטה for the officers and soldiers.

sources.quote: כי שבט מציין המשרה, ומטה מציין השוטרים ואנשי החיל
sources.says: Malbim says שבט points to the office of rule and מטה to the officers and soldiers.

19:12.headline: The east wind is the king of Babylon
19:12.body: Rashi says the east wind that dried the vine is Nebuchadnezzar. Radak says the east wind is hot and dry, and Babylon lies to the northeast of Israel.

sources.quote: וְרוּחַ הַקָּדִים. נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר
sources.says: Rashi says the east wind is Nebuchadnezzar.

sources.quote: כי המשיל מלך בבל לרוח הקדים כי היא חמה ויבשה ועוד כי בבל מזרחית צפונית לארץ ישראל
sources.says: Radak says the king of Babylon is likened to the east wind because it is hot and dry, and Babylon is northeast of Israel.

19:14.headline: A lament in prophecy that became a real lament
19:14.body: The chapter ends 'it is a lament, and it became a lament'. Radak says it was a lament when spoken as prophecy, and it became one again when the destruction and exile came.

sources.quote: קינה היא בדבר הנבואה וכן היתה לקינה בעת החרבן והגלות
sources.says: Radak says it is a lament as prophecy, and it became a lament at the time of the destruction and exile.

sources.quote: אֲמַר נְבִיָא אִלְיָא הִיא נְבוּאֲתָא וּתְהֵי לְאִלְיָא
sources.says: The Targum says: the prophet said, this prophecy is a lament and will become a lament.

21:2.headline: Prophecy that falls in drops
21:2.body: הטף means to let something drip. The commentators say it is borrowed for speech. Malbim says a long prophecy flows like water, and a short one falls drop by drop, as here.

sources.quote: הוא מל׳ נטיפה והזלה ומושאל בענין הדבור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means dripping and is borrowed for speaking.

sources.quote: והדבור הקצר כנוטף טיפים טיפים
sources.says: Malbim says a short speech is pictured as water falling drop by drop.

21:5.headline: They mocked him as a teller of parables, so God spoke plainly
21:5.body: The people brushed Ezekiel off as one who just tells parables. Radak says God then gave the same prophecy again with no parable at all. Maimonides cites this verse to show how much the prophets spoke in parables.

sources.quote: לפיכך שונה אליו הדבר בענין זה מבואר בלא משל
sources.says: Radak says that is why the prophecy is repeated in the next verses, spelled out without a parable.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Prefatory Remarks 19
sources.quote: ויודע אתה שמרוב שימושם של הנביאים במשלים, אמר הנביא
sources.says: Maimonides says the prophets used parables so much that Ezekiel complained of being called a teller of parables.

21:7.headline: Why 'sanctuaries' in the plural
21:7.body: There was one Temple, yet the verse says מקדשים. Rashi says it hints at two destructions. Radak adds another reason: the Temple had three parts, the hall, the sanctuary and the inner room.

sources.quote: מִקְדָּשִׁים. שְׁנֵי חֻרְבָּנִים
sources.says: Rashi says the plural points to two destructions.

sources.quote: אמר לשון רבים כי בית המקדש ג' בתים אולם היכל ודביר
sources.says: Radak says it is plural because the Temple had three rooms, or it hints at the first and second destructions.

21:8.headline: Why would God cut off the righteous?
21:8.body: God says He will cut off both the righteous and the wicked. Radak says the few righteous are swept away along with the many wicked. He also brings Saadia Gaon: here 'righteous' means the devoted Baal worshipper, so both are wicked in God's eyes.

sources.quote: ורב סעדיה פירש צדיק לבעל ורשע לבעל
sources.says: Radak says the righteous die for the sins of the wicked, and cites Saadia, who reads 'righteous' as one faithful to Baal.

sources.quote: צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע. הוּא הַ״לַּח״ וְהַ״יָּבֵשׁ״
sources.says: Rashi says these are the wet and dry trees of the fire parable just before.

21:14.headline: A sword, a sword: two swords, or a cry of pain
21:14.body: The word sword is said twice. Rashi says there are two swords: Babylon's, and then the sword of Ammon's agent that killed Gedaliah. Radak says it is how a person in pain repeats a word.

sources.quote: שְׁתֵּי חֲרָבוֹת: חֶרֶב מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל רִאשׁוֹנָה
sources.says: Rashi says there are two swords: first the king of Babylon's, then the sword of Ammon.

sources.quote: וכפל חרב חרב כדרך הנוהים והכואבים שכופלים דבריהם
sources.says: Radak says the word is doubled the way mourners and people in pain repeat their words.

21:14.headline: A sword that is 'plucked': polished, not sharpened
21:14.body: מרט usually means to pluck out hair. Radak says here it means the rust is rubbed off so the blade shines. Malbim stresses that the word never means sharpening.

sources.quote: ענין המריקה והעברת החלודה יפה עד שתבריק
sources.says: Radak says it means scouring off the rust until the sword shines.

sources.quote: פעל מרט לא נמצא על החידוד בשום מקום
sources.says: Malbim says the verb is never used for sharpening; its root meaning is plucking hair.

21:17.headline: Gathered for the sword, or afraid of it
21:17.body: מגורי can come from two roots. Rashi reads it as gathered, like grain stored in a granary. Menachem and Radak read it as fear, as when Moab feared Israel.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ לְשׁוֹן יִרְאָה
sources.says: Rashi reads it as gathering, like a granary, and says Menachem reads it as fear.

sources.quote: מענין ויגר מואב ענין פחד ויראה
sources.says: Radak says it means fear, as in 'Moab was afraid'.

21:19.headline: The third sword, or the great one
21:19.body: שלישתה looks like 'third'. Radak says the blows will come three times over. Others he cites read it as 'great', like the שליש, the king's chief officer.

sources.quote: יש מפרשים שלישיתה גדולה כמו השליש אשר למלך
sources.says: Radak says it means tripled, and that some read it as 'great', like the king's officer.

sources.quote: עוֹד יֵשׁ חֶרֶב שֶׁל שְׁלִישִׁית
sources.says: Rashi says after the two swords there is yet a third.

21:19.headline: A sword that follows you into your rooms, or makes you tremble
21:19.body: החדרת comes from חדר, an inner room. Rashi says the sword will chase them even into their inner rooms. Radak says the Aramaic translation reads it with letters swapped, as חרדה, terror.

sources.quote: תִּרְדֹּף אֶתְכֶם בְּחַדְרֵי חֲדָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says the sword will pursue them into their innermost rooms.

sources.quote: ותרגומו כמו הפוך החודרת ענין חרדה
sources.says: Radak says the Targum reads it as if the letters were reversed, meaning trembling.

21:20.headline: A word found nowhere else: slaughter, terror, or barking
21:20.body: אבחת appears only here. Some swap letters and read טבחת, slaughter. Others read it as terror. Rashi offers his own idea: from נביחה, barking, the noise of those cut down by the sword.

sources.quote: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אִבְחַת חָרֶב הַשְׁמָעַת קוֹל הֲרוּגֵי חֶרֶב, לְשׁוֹן נְבִיחָה
sources.says: Rashi rejects other readings and says it means the sound of the slain, from the word for barking.

sources.quote: עניינו כמו טבחת בחלוף אל״ף בטי״ת באטב״ח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like טבחת, slaughter, by a fixed swap of letters.

21:24.headline: Not 'create' but clear a space, or choose one
21:24.body: ברא usually means to create. Rashi says here it means to clear a spot of thorns, as when Joshua told the tribes to clear the forest. Menachem and Radak read it as 'choose'.

sources.quote: מָקוֹם פַּנֵּה מִן הַקּוֹצִים וְהַבַּרְקָנִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means clear a place of thorns, and notes Menachem's reading 'choose'.

sources.quote: ברא צווי. מענין ברו לכם איש שהוא ענין בחירה
sources.says: Radak says it is a command meaning 'choose', as in 'choose yourselves a man'.

21:26.headline: The 'mother of the road', where the roads split
21:26.body: The king stands at אם הדרך, the mother of the road. Radak explains the image. The roads branch out from that point the way daughters come from a mother.

sources.quote: ונקראת אם הדרך שהדרכים פונים אליה והיא להם כאם והם לה כבנות
sources.says: Radak says it is called the mother of the road because the roads turn to it like daughters to a mother.

21:26.headline: Shaking the arrows: tossing them, or polishing them to read
21:26.body: קלקל describes how the king of Babylon read the future with arrows. Rashi says he shot an arrow up and saw which way it fell. Radak says he polished the arrowhead until it shone and looked into it.

sources.quote: זָרַק חֵץ כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה, וְהִיא פּוֹנָה מֵאֵלֶיהָ לְיָמִין אוֹ לִשְׂמֹאל
sources.says: Rashi says he threw an arrow upward, and the way it turned decided the lot.

sources.quote: שמחדדין ומלטשין פני ברזל החץ עד שיהיה בהיר מאד ורואין בו בעלי הקסם
sources.says: Radak says they polished the iron arrowhead until it shone, and diviners looked into it.

21:28.headline: Oaths upon oaths, or seven times seven
21:28.body: שבעי שבעות can come from oath or from seven. Radak reads it as many oaths. Rashi brings the midrash: Nebuchadnezzar cast his lots 49 times, and every one pointed to Jerusalem.

sources.quote: אַרְבָּעִים וְתִשְׁעָה פְּעָמִים קָסַם לָהֶם נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר
sources.says: Rashi says Nebuchadnezzar cast lots for them 49 times, and all came out the same.

sources.quote: כאילו נשבעו להם שבועות רבות
sources.says: Radak reads it as if they had sworn many oaths to them.

21:31.headline: Lift the crown off, or lift it high
21:31.body: הרים means to raise. Most read it here as removing the crown from the king's head. Malbim objects that the word never means removing, and reads it as raising someone's honor.

sources.quote: וארים העטרה מעל ראש המלך
sources.says: Radak reads it as lifting the crown off the king's head.

sources.quote: ולא נמצא לשון הרמה על הסרת הדבר
sources.says: Malbim says the word is never used for removing something, so it means raising in honor.

21:32.headline: Ruin, ruin, ruin: why three times
21:32.body: עוה is said three times. Rashi reads it as ruin after ruin, like a heap in a field. Radak reads it as 'twisted': the crown stayed bent for three generations until Zerubbabel.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן חֻרְבָּה אַחַר חֻרְבָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means ruin after ruin, and that Menachem linked it to wrongdoing.

sources.quote: ואמר שלשה פעמים עוה כי ג' דורות היתה בטלה העטרה
sources.says: Radak says it is said three times because the crown was lost for three generations.

21:33.headline: A sword made to hold many slain, or to devour them
21:33.body: להכיל usually means to hold. Metzudat Zion keeps that sense. Radak's father read it as להאכיל, to make it eat, with the aleph dropped: the sword devours.

sources.quote: ענין החזקה וסבל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means holding and bearing.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש להכיל כמו להאכיל
sources.says: Radak says his father read it as 'to feed', meaning the sword devours.

21:36.headline: Brutish men, or men who burn
21:36.body: בוערים can mean fools or burners. Radak gives both: reckless men who kill without thought, or men who destroy like fire. He notes the scribes' tradition marks this word as having two meanings.

sources.quote: וכן אמר המסרה על בינו בוערים בתרי לישני
sources.says: Radak says the word means fools or burners, and the Masorah notes it has two senses.

21:36.headline: Rashi changes his mind: the prophet is speaking to the sword
21:36.body: Rashi writes that he explained this passage long ago one way. Now he sees that words like אפיח, 'I will blow fire on you', fit only metal. So the prophet is speaking to the sword itself.

sources.quote: אֵינוֹ נוֹפֵל לָשׁוֹן זֶה אֶלָּא עַל מַתֶּכֶת
sources.says: Rashi says this wording only fits metal, and that he now reads the passage as speaking about the sword.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן נְפִיחַת אֵשׁ בְּמַפּוּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means blowing on a fire with bellows.

22:3.headline: Idols are called גלולים, and Metzudat David compares them to dung
22:3.body: The prophet's word for idols is גלולים. Metzudat David says the city made repulsive things, like גלל של רעי, dung, and so made itself unclean.

sources.quote: דברים תועבים ומאוסים כגלל של רעי למען טמא את העיר הזאת
sources.says: Metzudat David says the city made abominable, repulsive things, like the dung of waste, to make itself unclean.

22:5.headline: 'Defiled of name': once called holy, now called unclean
22:5.body: השם here is the people's name, their reputation. Rashi says they were called 'a holy people' and 'sons' of God, and made themselves called 'a people of unclean lips'.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ נִקְרָאִים ״עַם קָדוֹשׁ״, ״בָּנִים״ לְיוֹצְרָם
sources.says: Rashi says they used to be called a holy people and children of their Maker.

sources.quote: וְגָרְמוּ עַצְמָם לְהִקָּרְאוֹת ״עַם טְמֵא שְׂפָתַיִם״
sources.says: Rashi says they caused themselves to be called a people of unclean lips.

sources.quote: שיש לך שם טומאה בגוים כי מלבד שאת טמאה בגופך את טמאה בשמך
sources.says: Radak says she has a name for uncleanness among the nations, unclean in her body and unclean in her name.

22:9.headline: זמה: sexual vice, or wicked schemes?
22:9.body: Rashi says זמה here is עצות של רשעה, 'wicked plots'. Radak reads it as lewdness, a general word for forbidden relations, which the next verses then list one by one.

sources.quote: זִמָּה עָשׂוּ. עֵצוֹת שֶׁל רְשָׁעָה
sources.says: Rashi says זמה עשו means wicked plans.

sources.quote: אמר זמה דרך כלל לכל העריות ואחר כך פרט קצתם
sources.says: Radak says זמה is a general word for all forbidden relations, and then the verses list some of them.

22:12.headline: Two words for interest, נשך and תרבית, so two laws are broken
22:12.body: Radak says the verse repeats one idea in two words. The sages taught that the Torah names both so that a lender breaks two prohibitions. Metzudat David says נשך is for money, and תרבית is for food.

sources.quote: ולא חלקו הכתוב אלא לעבור עליו בשני לאוין
sources.says: Radak says the Torah split them only so that a lender breaks two prohibitions.

sources.quote: לשון נשך אמור בכסף תרבית באוכל
sources.says: Metzudat David says נשך is said of money, and תרבית of food.

22:16.headline: ונחלת: 'you will be inherited', or 'you will be profaned'?
