22:16.body: Radak gives two readings. One comes from נחלה, an inheritance: you were My inheritance and now you are not. The other comes from חלול, profaning. Metzudat Zion reads it as profaning, and Rashi says you will tremble at what you did.

sources.quote: ופירושו תהי ננחלת בעצמך כי עד עתה היית נחלתי ומעתה אין את נחלתי ויש מפרשים ונחלת ענין חלול
sources.says: Radak says it means you will be inherited by yourself, since you were My inheritance and now you are not, and that some explain it as profaning.

sources.quote: ונחלת. מל׳ חלול
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ונחלת comes from the word for profaning.

sources.quote: תִּתְחַלְחֲלִי בְּעַצְמֵךְ עַל מַה שֶּׁעָשִׂית
sources.says: Rashi says it means you will tremble within yourself over what you did.

22:20.headline: Three verbs for gathering: קבץ, אסף and כנס differ
22:20.body: Malbim says קבץ gathers what was scattered, אסף brings things to one place, and כנס shuts them in a place they cannot leave. The last fits the furnace, which holds the metal in.

sources.quote: הקובץ מקבץ הנפזרות, והאוסף אוסף אל מקום אחד
sources.says: Malbim says one who gathers (קובץ) collects what was scattered, and one who collects (אוסף) brings things to one place.

sources.quote: והכונס כונס למקום שמור בל יצא משם
sources.says: Malbim says one who shuts in (כונס) puts things in a guarded place so they do not leave it.

22:25.headline: חסן: strength, or treasure? Two readings of one rare word
22:25.body: Metzudat Zion reads חסן as strength, like וחסון הוא כאלונים. Radak reads it as treasure, like לא יאצר ולא יחסן.

sources.quote: ענין חוזק כמו וחסון הוא כאלונים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means strength, like וחסון הוא כאלונים in Amos.

sources.quote: חסן כמו אוצר וכן לא יאצר ולא יחסן
sources.says: Radak says חסן is like אוצר, a treasure, as in לא יאצר ולא יחסן.

22:26.headline: חמסו here means 'took away': the priests robbed people of Torah
22:26.body: חמס usually means violence. Metzudat Zion says here it means removal, like נחמסו עקביך. Rashi says the priests should have taught, and by not teaching they robbed the Torah from those who needed to learn. Malbim cites R. Yonah that חמס in Arabic means taking a thing from its place.

sources.quote: ענין הסרה כמו נחמסו עקביך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חמסו means removal, like נחמסו עקביך in Jeremiah.

sources.quote: שֶׁחֲמָסוּהָ מִן הַצְּרִיכִין לִלְמֹד
sources.says: Rashi says they robbed the Torah from those who needed to learn.

sources.quote: ור' יונה כתב שחמס בלשון ערבי הסרת הדבר ממקומו
sources.says: Malbim says R. Yonah wrote that חמס in Arabic means taking a thing away from its place.

22:27.headline: Princes are 'wolves', not lions: wolves kill even when not hungry
22:27.body: Malbim says a lion kills a person only when it is hungry, but a wolf kills to shed blood even when it is not. So 'wolves' fits rulers who shed blood and also grab wealth.

sources.quote: האריה אינו טורף את האדם רק בעת רעבונו אבל הזאב טורף לשפך דם גם כשאינו רעב
sources.says: Malbim says the lion attacks a person only when hungry, but the wolf kills to shed blood even when it is not hungry.

22:29.headline: עשק: withholding wages, or hurting the body? Two readings
22:29.body: Malbim says עשק is holding back a hired worker's pay, which is lighter than גזל, outright robbery. Metzudat David says here it means harming a person's body, such as by beating.

sources.quote: עשק המעכב שכר שכיר והוא קל מגזל
sources.says: Malbim says עשק is withholding a worker's wages, and it is lighter than גזל.

sources.quote: זה עושק הגוף במכות וכדומה
sources.says: Metzudat David says this עושק is oppression of the body, by blows and the like.

23:4.headline: Oholibah: "my tent is in her"
23:4.body: אהליבה sounds like אהלי בה, "my tent is in her". Rashi and Radak say the name points to the Temple in Jerusalem, where God dwelt.

sources.quote: אהליבה. על שם שאהלי היה בה ומקדשי
sources.says: Rashi says Jerusalem is called אהליבה because God's tent and sanctuary were in her.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר כי אהלי בה ושם אני שוכן
sources.says: Radak says the name means "my tent is in her", where God dwells, because the Temple was there.

23:5.headline: A word only for lust, so poets erred using it for God
23:5.body: ותעגב means she lusted. Radak's father noted that this word is always used for illicit desire, so the synagogue poets were wrong to use it for love of God.

sources.quote: וכתב אדוני אבי ז"ל כי כל הנמצא בלשון הזה הוא בענין חשק הזנות על כן טעו הפייטים
sources.says: Radak says his father wrote that every use of this word is about lustful desire, so the liturgical poets erred in using it for longing for God.

23:15.headline: Dyed turbans, or just large hats?
23:15.body: Rashi says טבולים has no parallel, and reads it from context as large hats. Menachem and Radak read it from טבל, "dip": turbans dipped in dye, like Joseph's coat dipped in blood.

sources.quote: טבולים אין לו דמיון, ופתרונו לפי הענין
sources.says: Rashi says the word has no parallel and must be explained from context, and brings Menachem's view that it means dyed.

sources.quote: טבולים אומר על הצניפים הצבועים במיני צבעונים
sources.says: Radak says טבולים describes turbans dyed in many colors.

23:17.headline: One word for both fastening and tearing loose
23:17.body: ותקע נפשה means she pulled away, the word used when Jacob's hip was wrenched. Rashi notes the same root means both driving a stake into the ground and pulling it out, as שרש means both root and uproot.

sources.quote: הוקעה, לשון חבור ותקיעת עץ בארץ הוא, וכן בהשתלפו מן הארץ יפול בו לשון קעיה
sources.says: Rashi says the root means fixing a stake in the ground, and the same word is used when it is pulled out of the ground.

sources.quote: ענין הסרה כמו ותקע כף ירך יעקב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means removal, as when Jacob's hip came out of place.

23:23.headline: Names of countries, or titles of officers?
23:23.body: The Targum reads פקוד, שוע and קוע as names of countries, and Rashi supports it from Jeremiah. Radak reads them as titles: an officer, a noble, a great lord.

sources.quote: פקוד ושוע וקוע. תרגם יונתן שם מדינות
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum takes them as names of countries, and that others read them as officers and rulers.

sources.quote: פקוד כמו פקיד וכן שוע שם לנדיב גדול
sources.says: Radak says פקוד is like פקיד, an officer, and שוע is a name for a great noble.

23:24.headline: A weapon, a ring of camps, or an army?
23:24.body: Dunash read הצן as a kind of weapon. Rashi reads it as camps surrounding the city, and Radak's father reads it as חצן, an arm, meaning an army.

sources.quote: פרש דונש: אחד מכלי המלחמה הוא; ואני אומר: לשון הקפות מחנות
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash explained it as a weapon, but he himself reads it as camps surrounding the city.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש כמו חוצן בחי"ת מן והביאו בניך בחוצן שפירושו זרוע
sources.says: Radak says his father read it as חוצן, an arm, and an army is called an arm.

23:25.headline: Nose and ears stand for king and priest
23:25.body: Rashi says the nose and ears are the face's glory, here standing for kingship and priesthood. Radak explains: the nose rises above the face like a king, and the ears hear the bells of the priest.

sources.quote: אפך ואזניך. הם תפארת הפרצוף, ולהם המשיל הכהונה והמלכות
sources.says: Rashi says nose and ears are the beauty of the face and stand for the priesthood and the kingship.

sources.quote: ואזניך הוא הכהן המשמיע קול לאזנים בבואו אל הקדש בפעמוני הזהב
sources.says: Radak says the nose stands for the king, who is tall over the people, and the ears for the priest whose golden bells sound when he enters the sanctuary.

23:34.headline: Israel's cup of punishment is clay, so it breaks for good
23:34.body: Rashi says Israel's cup of suffering is pictured as clay: once broken it cannot be fixed, so it will never be filled for Israel again. When the nations are punished, the cup is gold, as in Jeremiah.

sources.quote: דמה כוס המשקה פרענות לישראל לכלי חרש, שמשנשתבר אין לו תקנה
sources.says: Rashi says the cup of punishment for Israel is likened to clay, which cannot be repaired once broken.

sources.quote: וכשהוא מדבר בהשקאת העובדי כוכבים ומזלות, קורא אותו זהב
sources.says: Rashi says that when the prophet speaks of the nations' cup, he calls it gold.

23:34.headline: Gnawing the cup's shards like bones
23:34.body: תגרמי comes from גרם, a bone. Rashi says it means scraping with the teeth as one gnaws a bone, and Metzudat Zion says a word for bones is borrowed here for the cup's broken pieces.

sources.quote: גורר בשניו את סביבות העצם או החרש
sources.says: Rashi says it means scraping with the teeth around a bone or a shard to get the last bits off.

sources.quote: העצם יקרא גרם כמו גרמיו כמטיל ברזל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a bone is called גרם, and the word is borrowed for the shards.

23:45.headline: "Righteous men" who are righteous only by comparison
23:45.body: The judges here are the officers of Babylon and Assyria. Rashi brings the Targum: next to these two sisters, even idol worshippers look righteous; Radak's father says it only means men sharp in law.

sources.quote: צדיקים העובדי כוכבים ומזלות מהנה
sources.says: Rashi says the judges are Babylon's and Assyria's officers, and by the Targum the idol worshippers are more righteous than these women.

sources.quote: אינו אומר צדיקים ממש אך בעלי טענות ומחודדין בדין
sources.says: Radak brings his father's view that it does not mean truly righteous, but men skilled in argument and sharp in judgment.

23:47.headline: Not "create" but "cut down"
23:47.body: ברא usually means create. Here Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it means cut down, as when Joshua told the tribes to clear the forest.

sources.quote: וברא לשון קציצה, וכן ״ובראתו״
sources.says: Rashi says וברא means cutting, as in Joshua's words about clearing the forest.

sources.quote: ענין כריתה כמו כי יער הוא ובראתו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means cutting down, as in "it is a forest, and you shall cut it down".

24:2.headline: Malbim counts the siege date inside the spelling of Jerusalem
24:2.body: Malbim points out that ירושלם is written here without a י. Its letters then add up to 586. That is עשור, 'the tenth', plus ten: the tenth of the tenth month, the day the siege began.

sources.quote: שעשור עולה בחשבונו תקע"ו ועם מספר עשרה שהוא עצם היום הוא תקפ"ו כמספר ירושלים שנכתב פה חסר י'
sources.says: Malbim says עשור adds up to 576, and with ten for the day it makes 586, the number of ירושלם as written here without a י.

24:3.headline: The people called Jerusalem a safe pot; now the pot boils
24:3.body: Earlier the people boasted, 'the city is the pot and we are the meat', trusting the walls to protect them. Rashi and Radak say Ezekiel turns their own picture around: the pot is put on the fire, with them cooking inside.

sources.quote: עַתָּה בָּא הָעֵת שֶׁתִּהְיֶה לְסִיר וְאַתֶּם בְּתוֹכָהּ לְבָשָׂר
sources.says: Rashi says that the time has now come for the city to be a pot with them inside it as meat, when Nebuchadnezzar puts it on the fire.

sources.quote: משל הסיר היא ירושלם וזה המשל אתה תמשול אותו לא כמו שהם היו מושלים ואומרים היא הסיר ואנחנו הבשר
sources.says: Radak says the pot is Jerusalem, and Ezekiel must tell the parable differently from the way they told it when they said 'it is the pot and we are the meat'.

sources.quote: שהיו אומרים שחומת ירושלים הבצורה תגן עליהם כמו שתגן הסיר על הבשר
sources.says: Malbim says they meant that Jerusalem's strong wall would protect them, as a pot protects the meat.

24:7.headline: The sages say this is the blood of the prophet Zechariah
24:7.body: Whose blood lies uncovered? Rashi and Radak cite the sages: the blood of Zechariah son of Jehoiada. Rashi says they did not even treat it like the blood of a deer or ram. Radak adds that Babylon's chief executioner later saw it still seething.

sources.quote: בְּדָמוֹ שֶׁל זְכַרְיָה בֶּן יְהוֹיָדָע, לֹא נָהֲגוּ בּוֹ לֹא כְּדַם הַצְּבִי וְלֹא כְּדַם הָאַיִל
sources.says: Rashi says the sages explained it as the blood of Zechariah son of Jehoiada, which was not treated even like the blood of a deer or a ram.

sources.quote: ובדרש כי על דם זכריה נאמר שראהו רב טבחים רותח והרג עליו אלפים ורבבות
sources.says: Radak says the midrash applies it to Zechariah's blood, which the chief executioner saw seething and killed thousands over.

24:10.headline: Spice the stew, or cook it down to a paste?
24:10.body: רקח is the word for mixing spices. Metzudat David says the spices go in once the meat has cooked down. Malbim says the meat cooks until it loses its shape and becomes like a paste.

sources.quote: אשים בה מרקחת הבשמים כי כן הדרך להשים הבשמים בתבשיל לאחר שנצטמק הרבה
sources.says: Metzudat David says spices are put in, since that is how a dish is seasoned after it has cooked down.

sources.quote: כי יתבשל עד שיאבד צורת בשר ויהיה כמרקחה ודבר דק הנרקח בחום האש
sources.says: Malbim says the meat will cook until it loses the form of meat and becomes like a fine paste ground in the fire's heat.

24:11.headline: Its copper, or its bottom?
24:11.body: נחשת usually means copper, and Rashi says this is a copper pot. Metzudat Zion and Radak read it as the pot's bottom, a sense Radak also finds in the Mishnah's 'the נחושת of an oven'.

sources.quote: סִיר שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת הִיא
sources.says: Rashi says it is a copper pot, and the scum will be absorbed into its copper.

sources.quote: נחושתה. עניינו תחתית הדבר ושוליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נחושתה means the bottom and base of a thing.

sources.quote: ובמשנה הבית שהיא מלאה משקין טהורין ונתנן למטה מנחושתו של תנור פירוש תחתיתו
sources.says: Radak says it means its bottom, and cites the Mishnah's 'below the נחושת of an oven', meaning its base.

24:12.headline: A one-time word: worn out by lies, or by mourning?
24:12.body: תאנים appears only here. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as pretexts and lies, like תואנה. Malbim reads it from תאניה, mourning, as in Isaiah's 'there will be mourning and moaning'.

sources.quote: בְּתוֹאֲנָה וְתַרְמִית הֶלְאָת אֶת הָעֲנִיִּים
sources.says: Rashi says the city wore out the poor with pretexts and deceit.

sources.quote: תאונים. ענין עלילה ושקר כמו כי תואנה הוא מבקש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means false pretexts and lies, like תואנה.

sources.quote: תאנים.  לשון והיתה תאניה ואניה
sources.says: Malbim says תאנים comes from תאניה, mourning.

24:12.headline: 'In fire', or 'it stinks'?
24:12.body: באש normally reads 'in fire': Radak says the scum can only be ended in the fire. Malbim notes it can also come from באש, 'to stink', as when the manna bred worms and stank.

sources.quote: כיון שהיא רבת חלאה אין לה תקנה אלא שתתם באש
sources.says: Radak says that since there is so much scum, the only fix is for it to be finished off in fire.

sources.quote: יל"פ ג"כ מענין וירום תולעים ויבאש
sources.says: Malbim says it can also be read from the root of 'it bred worms and stank'.

24:16.headline: 'The delight of your eyes': Ezekiel's wife, and the Temple
24:16.body: God tells Ezekiel he will lose מחמד עיניך, 'the delight of your eyes'. Rashi says it is his wife, as the story goes on to show. Radak says her sudden death is a sign: the people will suddenly lose the delight of their eyes, the Temple.

sources.quote: מַחְמַד עֵינֶיךָ. אִשְׁתְּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says 'the delight of your eyes' is Ezekiel's wife.

sources.quote: וזה למופת כי פתאום יבא שברם במחמד עיניהם שהוא בית המקדש
sources.says: Radak says her sudden death is a sign that disaster will suddenly strike the delight of the people's eyes, the Temple.

24:17.headline: Groan, but silently
24:17.body: God says האנק דם, 'groan, be still'. Rashi reads it as wasting away in silence. Radak brings the sages, who read the two words as two mourning rules Ezekiel must keep: cry out for the dead, and do not greet people.

sources.quote: הָאָנֵק. הִתְמַקְמֵק בִּשְׁתִיקָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means to waste away in silence.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל האנק מכאן שמצוחין על המתים ולמדו ממלת דום שאבל אסור בשאלת שלום
sources.says: Radak says the sages learned from 'groan' that one cries out for the dead, and from 'be still' that a mourner may not greet others.

24:26.headline: News for the ears, not something seen with the eyes
24:26.body: להשמעות is a one-time noun from 'to make hear'. Malbim says it simply means 'to let the ears hear'. Radak also suggests the survivor brought a report he had heard, not something he saw himself.

sources.quote: שם בתוס' ו"ת, ופי' להשמיע לאזנים
sources.says: Malbim says it is a noun with an added ות, meaning to let the ears hear.

sources.quote: ויש לפרש להשמעות אזנים כי הפליט יבא אליך ויגיד לך החורבן להשמעות אזנים לא למראה עינים
sources.says: Radak says it can mean the survivor will tell of the destruction as something heard, not something his own eyes saw.

26:2.headline: Jerusalem as the nations' door: an open gate or a closed one?
26:2.body: Tyre gloats that 'the doors of the nations' are broken. Rashi and Malbim read Jerusalem as the door every trader came through. Malbim adds a second reading: a closed door that blocked trade to Tyre, now forced open.

sources.quote: עִיר שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים הָיוּ נִכְנָסִים לָהּ לִסְחוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is the city all the nations entered to trade.

sources.quote: וקראה דלתות העמים שכולם נכנסו אל הדלת הזה
sources.says: Malbim says it is called the nations' doors because they all came in through it.

sources.quote: וגם י"ל שקראה דלתות העמים מפני שהיתה חוצצת בפני העמים
sources.says: Malbim also suggests it was called a door because it stood in the way of the nations heading to Tyre.

26:9.headline: Towers knocked down with swords, or with hammers?
26:9.body: חרבות usually means swords. Radak and Rashi read them here as tools for smashing stone. Malbim keeps 'swords' and calls it a boast: the city falls so easily that swords are enough.

sources.quote: הם כלי המפץ שמנפצים ומשברים בהם האבנים
sources.says: Radak says they are smashing tools used to break stones.

sources.quote: בְּאוּמָנוּת חוּרְבָּן שֶׁיָּבִיא עִמּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says they are the tools of destruction he will bring with him.

sources.quote: שבחרבות לבד יתוץ מגדלות ולא יצטרך כרים ואילי ברזל
sources.says: Malbim says that, as a figure of speech, he will tear down towers with swords alone, without rams.

26:12.headline: Two words for plunder that are not the same
26:12.body: The verse uses both שלל and בזז. Malbim says שלל is what is left lying after a battle, and בזז is what soldiers grab for themselves from people.

sources.quote: ששלל הוא הנשאר מעצמו אחרי המלחמה במקום א'
sources.says: Malbim says שלל is what remains on its own in one place after the war.

sources.quote: והבז הוא מה שאנשי המלחמה בוזזים איש לו מאת היחידים
sources.says: Malbim says בז is what each soldier takes for himself from individual people.

26:15.headline: The groan of a dying man's last breath
26:15.body: אנק is not just any groan. Radak says it is the sound of the breath leaving the throat as a wounded man dies.

sources.quote: ואנקת החלל היא יציאת נשמתו מהקנה בקול בעת מותו
sources.says: Radak says the groan of the slain is his breath leaving his windpipe with a sound as he dies.

sources.quote: באנוק. ענין אנחה וגניחה שהיא בעת יציאת הנפש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the sigh and groan made when the soul leaves.

26:17.headline: Settled since ancient days, or settled by the seas?
26:17.body: מימים can mean 'from days', so Tyre was settled since long ago. Read with a doubled מ it means 'from seas': Tyre was settled and kept strong by the seas around it.

sources.quote: יֵשׁ נוֹקְדִין רָפֵי, וּפוֹתְרִין: מְיוּשֶׁבֶת מִיָּמִים קַדְמוֹנִים; וְיֵשׁ נוֹקְדִים דָּגֵשׁ, וּפוֹתְרִין מְיוּשֶׁבֶת בְּחָזְקָה עַל יְדֵי יַמִּים הַסּוֹבְבִים לָהּ
sources.says: Rashi gives both readings, 'settled since ancient days' and 'settled strongly by the surrounding seas', and favors the second.

sources.quote: ואמר מימים לשון רבים כלומר ים אוקינוס וים סוף וים מערבי ושאר הימים
sources.says: Radak reads it as 'seas', plural, because traders reached Tyre over many seas.

26:20.headline: The 'people of old' that Tyre goes down to join
26:20.body: Tyre will go down to the עם עולם, the people of long ago. Radak reads this as the long dead, turned to dust. Malbim reads it as the generation of the Flood, who were also wiped out by water.

sources.quote: כלומר עם שמתו מעולם היום זמן רב שנשחת גופם ואבד ושב עפר
sources.says: Radak says it means people who died long ago, whose bodies have returned to dust.

sources.quote: אל עם עולם, אל דור המבול שנמחו ג"כ כולם במים
sources.says: Malbim says it means the generation of the Flood, who were also all wiped out by water.

sources.quote: עִם שְׁאָר הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת אֲשֶׁר שָׁם מֵעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means the other idol worshippers who have been there since long ago.

26:20.headline: Glory for the Land of Israel, or lasting standing?
26:20.body: צבי usually means beauty or glory, and Rashi reads it that way. Malbim reads it from מצב, standing firm and lasting.

sources.quote: וְאֶתֵּן הַתִּפְאֶרֶת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says God will put glory in Jerusalem.

sources.quote: צבי.  מענין מצב וקיום
sources.says: Malbim says the word comes from standing and lasting.

26:20.headline: Why Israel is 'the land of the living'
26:20.body: Tyre goes to the land of the dead, so Israel is called the opposite, the land of the living. The sages also read it as the land whose dead will live again.

sources.quote: ולפי שאמר על צור בארץ תחתיות שהיא ארץ מתים שאבדו מן העולם אמר בהפך על ארץ ישראל שהיא ארץ חיים. ורבותינו ז"ל דרשו ארץ שמתיה חיים
sources.says: Radak says Israel is called the land of the living as the opposite of Tyre's land of the dead, and quotes the sages: the land whose dead live.

sources.quote: והיא א״י הקרויה כן ע״ש שבה יחיו המתים בזמן התחיה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the Land of Israel is called this because the dead will live there at the resurrection.

26:21.headline: Terror, demons, or 'you will be as if you never were'
26:21.body: Radak reads בלהות as בהלות, terror, with two letters swapped. Some read it as a place of demons. The Aramaic translation splits it into בל הות, 'you were not'.

sources.quote: בלהות אתנך. הפוך כמו בהלות ענין בעתה וכליון
sources.says: Radak says the word is בהלות with letters reversed, meaning terror and destruction.

sources.quote: וְהַפּוֹתְרִים אוֹמְרִים לְשׁוֹן מְקוֹם מְרַקֵּד שְׂעִירִים
sources.says: Rashi reports interpreters who read it as a place where demons dance.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם בלהות שתי מלות כדלא הוית בל הות
sources.says: Radak notes the Aramaic translation reads it as two words, בל הות, 'as if you had not been'.

27:3.headline: Tyre claims a title that belonged to Jerusalem
27:3.body: כלילת יפי means "perfect in beauty". Rashi notes that people used to say this about Jerusalem, and now Tyre boasts it about itself.

sources.quote: עד עכשיו הכל אומרים על ירושלים
sources.says: Rashi says that until now everyone said "perfect in beauty" about Jerusalem, and now Tyre proudly says it of itself.

sources.quote: מלשון כל וכן מכלל יופי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from כל, "all", as in the Psalm's phrase for complete beauty.

27:6.headline: Made by Assyrians, or made of boxwood?
27:6.body: Metzudat Zion reads בת אשרים as "the company of Assyrians", who made the ship's planks of ivory. Rashi says the planks must be wood, and reads it as one word for a tree, the תאשור, set with ivory.

sources.quote: עדת אשורים וכן בת בבל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בת אשורים means the community of Assyrians, the way בת בבל means the people of Babylon.

sources.quote: אי אפשר לו להיות אלא של עץ, וזהו בת אשרים, כאלו הוא תיבה אחת
sources.says: Rashi says the plank can only be wood, so בת אשרים is read as if it were one word, the tree called תאשור.

27:8.headline: The ship's officers are named for the ropes they pull
27:8.body: חבליך means your sailors. Metzudat Zion and Radak tie the word to חבל, a rope, because these men work the ropes of the sail.

sources.quote: מלשון חבל וקו ויקראו כן מנהיגי הספינה על כי מושכים בחבלי הוילון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from חבל, a rope, because those who steer the ship pull the ropes of the sail.

sources.quote: חובל יקרא מושך חבלי הוילון במשפט
sources.says: Radak says a חובל is the one who pulls the sail ropes the right way, which takes skill.

27:9.headline: Sailors named for mixing, as their oars churn the water
27:9.body: מלחים are sailors. Metzudat Zion and Malbim link the word to ממולח, "mixed", because the rowers stir up the sea with their oars.

sources.quote: והוא ענין ערבוב כמו ממולח טהור קדש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means mixing, as in ממולח in Exodus, because the sailors mix the water with their oars.

sources.quote: שמלח ישמש על העירוב, כמו ממולח טהור קודש
sources.says: Malbim says מלח is used for mixing, and the rowers push the sea water aside to move the ship.

27:9.headline: Trade goods named for the pledges merchants give each other
27:9.body: מערב here means your trade goods, a use found only in this chapter. Radak ties it to ערב, a guarantee, because merchants vouch for one another when they buy and sell.

sources.quote: ונקראה הסחורה מערב והסוחרים עורבין לפי שהסוחרין עורבים זה לזה
sources.says: Radak says goods are called מערב and merchants עורבים because merchants stand surety for each other in their deals.

sources.quote: לשון ערובה, הם כל צרכי האדם שהוא חי בהם, וממונו הוא ערובתו
sources.says: Rashi says the word means a pledge: a person's money is the security that keeps him alive.

sources.quote: ושני הלשונות האחרונים לא נמצא על המסחר רק בפ' זאת
sources.says: Malbim says these two words are used for trade only in this passage.

27:11.headline: Short men on the towers, or divers who sound the deep?
27:11.body: Metzudat Zion reads גמדים as short men, from גומד, a forearm's length. Rashi also reports a teaching that they were divers, named for going down to the sea floor measured in cubits.

sources.quote: כן יקראו אנשי מדה קצרה והוא מלשון גמד ארכה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says short people are called גמדים, from the word גומד, the length of a forearm.

sources.quote: על שם שיורדין בים עד התהום
sources.says: Rashi reports in the name of Rabbi Menachem that they were called this because they go down into the sea to the deep; others say they were dwarfs.

27:12.headline: Goods named for strength, or for what is left behind
27:12.body: עזבונים means trade goods. Rashi links it to a sense of "strengthen", since money holds a person up. Malbim takes it from עזב, "leave", for the goods left in the city's stores.

sources.quote: וממונו של אדם הוא חזקו, המעמידו על רגליו
sources.says: Rashi says the word means strength, because a person's money is what keeps him on his feet.

sources.quote: ועזבון, נגזר מפעל עזב, הסחורה שעוזבים בעיר בבתי המסחר
sources.says: Malbim says עזבון comes from עזב, "leave": the goods that are left in the city's trading houses.

27:17.headline: Wheat from the town of Minnith, or wheat sold by count?
27:17.body: Radak reads מנית as a town in the land of Israel known for good wheat. Rashi also brings a midrash that it means wheat so fine and large it was sold by number, from מנין, a count.

sources.quote: שם מקום בארץ ישראל שהחיטים שם יפות
sources.says: Radak says Minnith is a place in the land of Israel where the wheat is fine.

sources.quote: ומדרש אגדה: חטין יפין וגסין הנמכרים במנין
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that these were fine, large grains of wheat sold by count.

27:24.headline: Packed in cedar, or strung like beads?
27:24.body: Rashi reads ארוזים with ארז, cedar: the boxes of goods were packed inside cedar wood. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as חרוזים, strung beads, since the letters א and ח can swap.

sources.quote: ובגנזי ברומים החבושים בחבלים וארוזים בתוך עץ ארז
sources.says: Rashi says the chests were tied with ropes and packed inside cedar wood.

sources.quote: כמו וחרוזים כי אחה״ע מתחלף ועניינו דברים מושמים על החוט
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like חרוזים, since the throat letters swap, and means things strung on a thread.

27:25.headline: The ships were Tyre's highway, or its caravans
27:25.body: Rashi reads שרותיך from שרון, flat land: the ships were Tyre's smooth road for bringing in goods. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it from שיירה, a caravan of many traveling together.

sources.quote: כשם שהמישור הוא דרך כבושה להביא בו סחורה
sources.says: Rashi says that just as a plain is a paved road for bringing goods to a city on land, the ships were Tyre's road.

sources.quote: שיירות הולכות בסחורתך כלומר רבות ביחד כמו שיירא
sources.says: Radak says it means caravans carrying Tyre's goods, many together.

27:26.headline: The rowers who carried Tyre, or the plunderers who sank it?
27:26.body: Metzudat Zion reads השטים as rowers, the same word as in verse 8. Radak reads it as plunderers, and the "many waters" as many troubles that came on Tyre.

sources.quote: מלשון שטיה ושחיה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from rowing and swimming.

sources.quote: השטים בלא אל"ף וענינו ענין בזה ושלל
sources.says: Radak says השטים is spelled without an alef and means plunder and spoil.

27:32.headline: Not "their sons" but "their wailing"
27:32.body: בניהם looks like "their sons". Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it from נהי, a wail: the sailors raise a lament for Tyre in their crying.

sources.quote: ונשאו אליך בניהם. בנהי שלהם
sources.says: Rashi says בניהם means "in their wailing".

sources.quote: בניהם. מלשון נהי ויללה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from wailing and howling.

27:32.headline: Who was like Tyre, or who was cut off like Tyre?
27:32.body: Rashi gives the Targum's reading, "none is like her", from דמה, to resemble. Metzudat Zion and Radak read it as "cut off" or "silenced": Tyre now lies ruined in the sea.

sources.quote: כדמה. כדגמתה
sources.says: Rashi says that by the Targum, כדמה means "like her".

sources.quote: ענין כריתה וחורבן כמו גם מדמן תדמי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means being cut off and destroyed.

sources.quote: ודומה נכרתת וכן שכנה דומה נפשי
sources.says: Radak says דומה means cut off, as in the Psalm about the soul dwelling in silence.

28:2.headline: נגיד, 'prince', is not the same as 'king'
28:2.body: Malbim says נגיד is anyone appointed to lead, a wider word than מלך. So the 'prince of Tyre' here is a different man from the king of Tyre named in verse 12. Metzudat David simply calls him the ruler of Tyre.

sources.quote: יש הבדל בין נגיד ובין מלך, שהנגיד כולל כל הממונה להנהיג
sources.says: Malbim says there is a difference between נגיד and מלך, because נגיד covers anyone appointed to lead.

sources.quote: שנגיד צור אינו המלך שמוזכר בפסוק
sources.says: Malbim concludes that the נגיד of Tyre is not the king who is mentioned in verse 12.

sources.quote: לנגיד צור. על מושל צור
sources.says: Metzudat David says לנגיד צור means 'to the ruler of Tyre'.

28:2.headline: 'Seat of God': a platform in the air, or a safe stronghold?
28:2.body: Rashi says the king built himself a contraption in the air over the sea, like seven heavens, and sat on the top one. Radak says it only means a secure spot in the middle of the seas that no one can touch, as God sits in heaven.

sources.quote: עָשָׂה לוֹ בָּאֲוִיר עַל הַיָּם בְּמַנְגְּנוֹן, כְּמִין שִׁבְעָה רְקִיעִים, וְיָשַׁב לוֹ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says he made himself a device in the air over the sea, like seven heavens, and sat on the highest.

sources.quote: כי אני ישבתי במקום חזק כי אני בלב ימים שהימים מקיפים אותי ומי יוכל לגעת בי כמו אלהים שיושב בשמים
sources.says: Radak says the king sits in a strong place in the heart of the seas, surrounded by water so no one can touch him, like God who sits in heaven.

28:4.headline: ותעש: 'you made' gold, or 'you gathered' it?
28:4.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say ותעש here means gathering, not making, like ואת הנפש אשר עשו בחרן. Malbim says it is making in the plain sense.

sources.quote: ענין אסיפה וקבוץ
sources.says: Radak says עשית and ותעש here mean gathering and collecting.

sources.quote: ענין קבוץ ואסיפה כמו ואת הנפש אשר עשו בחרן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ותעש means gathering, as in ואת הנפש אשר עשו בחרן.

sources.quote: עשיה ממש כפשוטו
sources.says: Malbim says ותעש זהב is making in the real, plain sense.

28:5.headline: חיל: wealth, or an army? Radak allows both
28:5.body: Radak says חילך means your riches or your armies, and Targum Jonathan translates it as 'your camp'. Metzudat Zion says it means wealth, as in ישא את חיל דמשק.

sources.quote: נכסיך או צבאיך וכן תרגם יונתן משרייתך
sources.says: Radak says חילך is your possessions or your armies, and Jonathan translates it as 'your camp'.

sources.quote: ענין עושר כמו ישא את חיל דמשק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חילך means wealth, as in ישא את חיל דמשק.

28:7.headline: יפעתך: 'your radiance', or the midrash's 'the beauty of your time'
28:7.body: Rashi says the word means your radiance, from the look of the face. The midrash splits it into two words, יופי עתך, 'the beauty of your time'. Metzudat Zion says it means shine, like הופיע מהר פארן.

sources.quote: הוֹפָעָתְךָ, לְשׁוֹן תֹּאַר פָּנִים; וְהַמִּדְרָשׁ דּוֹרְשׁוֹ יוֹפִי עִתֶּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means your radiance, a word for the look of the face, and the midrash reads it as יופי עתך.

sources.quote: ענין זוהר וזריחה וכן הופיע מהר פארן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means brightness and shining, as in הופיע מהר פארן.

28:8.headline: ממותי is a plural: 'you will die many deaths'
28:8.body: The word is a plural of מות. Radak says it means many deaths, in the sense of many stab wounds, like a slain man who is pierced again and again. Malbim says the same.

sources.quote: אמר תמות מיתות רבות כלומר בדקירות רבות כמו ממותי החלל
sources.says: Radak says it means you will die many deaths, that is, by many stabs, like the deaths of the slain.

sources.quote: החלל ימות מיתות הרבה בדקירות רבות
sources.says: Malbim says a slain man dies many deaths, by many stabs.

28:9.headline: מחלליך: 'those who kill you', or 'those who profane you'?
28:9.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as 'those who slay you', from חלל, a slain man. Malbim also reads it as those who bring you down to the ordinary, which shows you are only a man.

sources.quote: מְחַלְלֶיךָ. כְּמוֹ הֹרְגֶךָ
sources.says: Rashi says מחלליך means the same as הורגך, 'those who kill you'.

sources.quote: מלשון חלל והרג
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is from the word for a slain man and killing.

sources.quote: ומצד שהם מחלליך ויוציאוך לחולין
sources.says: Malbim says that those who profane you and take you out to the ordinary show that you are a man.

28:12.headline: תכנית: a seal for every pattern, or something prepared?
28:12.body: Rashi says the king was full of wisdom to seal and stamp every pattern and shape. Metzudat Zion ties תכנית to הכנה, 'preparing'. Radak says it means the full content of all wisdom, honor and wealth.

sources.quote: אַתָּה הוּא מָלֵא חָכְמָה לַחְתֹּם וְלִטְבֹּעַ כָּל תַּבְנִית וְצוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says you are full of wisdom to seal and stamp every pattern and form.

sources.quote: מל׳ הכנה ומתוקן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תכנית is from the word for preparing and fixing.

sources.quote: פירוש תוכן כל החכמות והכבוד והעושר
sources.says: Radak says it means the content of all wisdom, honor and wealth.

28:13.headline: עדן means delight; the Targum reads 'as if you were in Eden'
28:13.body: Malbim says עדן comes from עידון, delight, and Metzudat Zion calls Eden a place of great pleasure. Rashi quotes the Targum, which says it was as if the king lived in the garden of the Lord.

sources.quote: מלת עדן מענין עידון ותענוג
sources.says: Malbim says the word עדן is from the idea of delight and pleasure.

sources.quote: והוא מקום עדון ותפנוק רב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Eden is a place of great delight and pampering.

sources.quote: כְּאִלּוּ בְּעֵדֶן גִּינְתָא דַה׳ אַתְּ שָׁרֵי
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: you are pampered as if you were dwelling in the garden of the Lord.

28:17.headline: לראוה: 'to look at you', or 'for a disgrace'?
28:17.body: Rashi says לראוה means to look at your shame, and that it is like לראיה. Radak gives both readings: to look at you and see the opposite of what you were, or a disgrace.

sources.quote: לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בְּבָשְׁתְּךָ, לְרַאֲוָה כְּמוֹ לִרְאִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means to look at your shame, and לראוה is like לראיה.

sources.quote: כלומר לראות בך הפך מה שהייתה
sources.says: Radak says it means to see in you the opposite of what you were.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים לראוה ענין בזיון
sources.says: Radak says some explain לראוה as meaning disgrace.

28:18.headline: 'Fire from within': proud words, sin, or a fiery army?
28:18.body: Rashi says the fire is the proud words that came out of the king's mouth, 'I am a god'. Radak says the fire is a picture of sin. Rashi also gives the Targum's reading: mighty nations, like fire.

sources.quote: דִּבְרֵי גַאֲוָה שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִפִּיךָ, לֵאמֹר אֵל אָנִי
sources.says: Rashi says the fire is the proud words that came out of your mouth, saying 'I am a god'.

sources.quote: האש הוא משל לעון
sources.says: Radak says the fire is a parable for sin.

sources.quote: לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר, כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ: ״וְאַיְיתֵי עַמְמִיָּא דְּתַקִּיפִין כְּאֶשָּׁתָא
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading, as the Targum has it: I will bring mighty nations like fire.

28:19.headline: בלהות, 'terrors', is בהלות with its letters swapped
28:19.body: Metzudat Zion says בלהות is a reversal of בהלות, from the word for being alarmed. Metzudat David reads the phrase as 'you will be full of terror, and never be found again'.

sources.quote: בלהות. הוא הפוך מן בהלות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בלהות is the reverse of בהלות.

sources.quote: תהיה מלא מבהלה ולא תמצא עוד עד עולם
sources.says: Metzudat David says you will be full of terror and never be found again.

28:24.headline: סלון is a kind of thorn; Targum Jonathan reads it as 'king'
28:24.body: Rashi says סלון is a kind of bramble, and Metzudat Zion says a kind of thorn. Targum Jonathan instead translates סלון ממאיר as 'a foul king'. Rashi says ממאיר means causing pain, like צרעת ממארת.

sources.quote: סִלּוֹן. מִין קַמְשׁוֹנִים וְחוֹחִים הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says סלון is a kind of bramble and thorn.

sources.quote: סילון. מין קוץ כמו וסלונים אותך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says סילון is a kind of thorn, as in וסלונים אותך.

sources.quote: מְלַךְ מַבְאִישׁ וְשִׁלְטוֹן מָעֵיק
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates the phrase as 'a foul king and an oppressive ruler'.

sources.quote: עִנְיַן הַכְאָבָה, כְּמוֹ ״צָרַעַת מַמְאֶרֶת״
sources.says: Rashi says ממאיר is about causing pain, like צרעת ממארת.

29:3.headline: Pharaoh as the great river creature, with an odd spelling
29:3.body: Pharaoh is pictured as a huge snake-like creature in the Nile, and his people as its fish. The usual spelling is תנין; here the word ends in מ, which Radak points out.

sources.quote: התנים הגדול. במ"ם במקום נון וכמוהו כמהם וכמהן
sources.says: Radak says the word is written with מ in place of נ, and means the great fish that Egypt's king is compared to.

sources.quote: כמו התנין בנו״ן וכן נקרא מין דג הדומה לנחש במראיתו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the same as תנין with a נ, a kind of fish that looks like a snake.

sources.quote: הַנָּבִיא מְמַשֵּׁל אֶת מַלְכָּהּ לְתַנִּין, וְאֶת עַמָּהּ לִדְגַת יְאוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says Egypt's wealth came from the Nile, so the prophet pictures its king as the great creature and its people as the river's fish.

29:3.headline: Why the Nile is called 'his rivers', in the plural
29:3.body: Egypt has one great river, yet the verse says 'his rivers'. Metzudat Zion says the plural fits because many pools were drawn off the Nile to water the land.

sources.quote: נחל מצרים נקרא יאור לפי שהמשיכו ממנו בריכות הרבה להשקות הארץ לכן אמר יאוריו בלשון רבים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the river of Egypt is called יאור, and the plural is used because many pools were drawn from it to water the land.

29:3.headline: Pharaoh's boast: did he make the river, or make himself?
29:3.body: Radak reads ואני עשיתני two ways: 'I made the Nile for myself to water my land', or 'I made myself a great king by my own wisdom'. Rashi and Malbim take the second.

sources.quote: אני עשיתי ותקנתי לי היאור להשקות את ארצי או פירושו עשיתיני עשיתי ותקנתי אותי בחכמתי ובתבונתי עד שנעשיתי מלך גדול
sources.says: Radak says it means either 'I made the river to water my land' or 'I made myself, by my own wisdom, into a great king'.

sources.quote: בִּגְבוּרָתִי וּבְחָכְמָתִי הִגְדַּלְתִּי גְּדֻלָּתִי וּמֶמְשַׁלְתִּי
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'by my strength and my wisdom I made myself great'.

sources.quote: עשיתני.  עשיתי את עצמי
sources.says: Malbim says it means 'I made myself'.

29:7.headline: Made them stand, or made them slip? A disputed letter swap
29:7.body: Plain sense: when the reed snaps, the man leaning on it must stand up on his own. Some swap two letters to read והמעדת, 'you made their hips slip', but Rashi, Radak and Malbim keep the plain reading.

sources.quote: יש מפרשים והעמדת בהפוך האותיות והמעדת מן ולא מעדו קרסולי והנכון כמשמעו
sources.says: Radak reports a reading with the letters swapped, meaning 'you made them slip', but says the plain meaning, 'you made them stand', is right.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ מַחֲלִיפִין וְהַעֲמַדְתָּ לָהֶם לוֹ הִמְעַדְתָּ, וְאֵינִי רוֹאֶה אֶת דִּבְרֵיהֶן
sources.says: Rashi says that once the reed breaks they must stand on their own, and he rejects those who swap the letters to read 'you made them slip'.

sources.quote: והעמדת י"מ מענין לא מעדו קרסולי, ואני פירשתי מענין עמידה כפשוטו
sources.says: Malbim notes that some take it from 'slipping', but he reads it as plain 'standing'.

29:20.headline: Two words for pay: wages for the army, reward for the king
29:20.body: Verse 19 calls Egypt's plunder שכר, pay for Nebuchadnezzar's army. Verse 20 uses פעלתו for the king's own work, and Malbim says the two words are chosen on purpose.

sources.quote: ובשתי אלה השקפות תפס לשון שכר אצל החיל ולשון פעולה על אשר עבד בעצמו
sources.says: Malbim says שכר is used for the army and פעולה for what the king did himself.

sources.quote: ר"ל השלל והבזה יהיה שכר חילו ופעולת נבוכדנצר עצמו יהיה מה שארץ מצרים תהיה שלו
sources.says: Malbim says the plunder is the army's pay, and the land of Egypt itself is Nebuchadnezzar's own reward.

29:21.headline: A growing horn means power returning to Israel
29:21.body: קרן is an animal's horn. Metzudat Zion says it stands for rule, since horned animals fight with their horns, and Targum Jonathan renders it 'redemption'.

sources.quote: כינה את הממשלה בשם קרן על כי בעלי הקרנים יתחזקו בהן בהלחמם עם מי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says rule is called a horn because horned animals draw strength from their horns when they fight.

sources.quote: בְּיוֹמָא הַהוּא אַיְתֵי פוּרְקַן לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates 'I will make a horn grow' as 'I will bring redemption to the house of Israel'.

30:3.headline: "A time of nations": when nations break, or when they gather?
30:3.body: Rashi follows the Aramaic: it is the time when nations are broken. Radak says it is the time when nations gather against Egypt to destroy it, and Malbim says all of Egypt's allies will fall with it.

sources.quote: עֵת גּוֹיִם. ״עִידָּן תְּבַר עַמְמַיָּא״
sources.says: Rashi quotes Jonathan: "a time of the breaking of nations".

sources.quote: עת שיאספו גוים על מצרים להחריבה
sources.says: Radak says it is the time when nations gather against Egypt to destroy it.

sources.quote: כי אז יפלו כל הגוים שהיו בברית עם מצרים
sources.says: Malbim says that then all the nations in alliance with Egypt will fall.

30:5.headline: הערב: a mixed crowd, or the allies who vouch for Egypt
30:5.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak read הערב as a mixture, peoples blended together. Rashi follows the Aramaic "supporters" and reads it as those who stood guarantor, ערב, for Egypt.

sources.quote: הערב. מל׳ תערובות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הערב comes from the word for mixture.

sources.quote: עם מקובץ מעמים נתערבו יחד
sources.says: Radak says it is a people gathered from many peoples who mixed together.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְכָל סוּמְכָוָותָא״, כָּל הָעוֹרְבִים עֲרוּבַת מִצְרַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says Jonathan translated it "all the supporters": all who stand as guarantors for Egypt.

30:9.headline: These מלאכים are not angels but troops sent on God's errand
30:9.body: מלאך means a messenger, human or heavenly. Rashi and Radak say these are bands of soldiers, called messengers because they come on God's mission.

sources.quote: גְּדוּדֵי גַּיָּסוֹת הוֹלְכִים בִּשְׁלִיחוּתִי
sources.says: Rashi says they are troops of soldiers going on My mission.

sources.quote: מלאכים. שלוחים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מלאכים means messengers.

sources.quote: וקראם מלאכים כאילו בשליחות האל יתברך באים
sources.says: Radak says he calls them messengers as if they come on God's mission.

30:9.headline: Messengers in ships, because a great river rings Kush
30:9.body: Radak and Malbim say צים are ships, warships, as in Isaiah's "mighty ship". Radak explains that a great river surrounds Kush, so the only way in is by ship, while the Aramaic translation reads "in legions".

sources.quote: בצים הם הספינות כמו וצי אדיר לא יעברנו
sources.says: Radak says צים are ships, as in "no mighty ship shall pass".

sources.quote: ואמר בצים כי נהר גדול סובב ארץ כוש ולא יוכלו להכנס לה אלא בספינות
sources.says: Radak says it says "in ships" because a great river surrounds the land of Kush and one can enter only by ship.

sources.quote: הם אניות גדולות, אניות מלחמה
sources.says: Malbim says they are large ships, warships.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ ״וְצִים מִיַּד כִּתִּים״ (במדבר כד:כד), וְכֵן תִּרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן: ״בְּלִגְיוֹנִין״
sources.says: Rashi compares "and ships from Kittim", and notes Jonathan translated it "in legions".

30:12.headline: Drying the Nile channels: a picture, or neglected canals?
30:12.body: Radak says all of Egypt's wealth comes from the river, so dry channels is a picture of losing all its good. Malbim reads it more plainly: foreign rulers will not keep up the canals that carried water across the land.

sources.quote: ולפי שארץ מצרים כל טובה ושבחה היא היאור אמר דרך משל שיחרבו היאורים רוצה לומר שיכלה מהם כל טובה
sources.says: Radak says that since all of Egypt's good and glory is the river, he says as a figure that the rivers will dry, meaning all good will end for them.

sources.quote: אנשיה יגלו ממנה ולא יבוא להם עוד טובה מן היאורים וכאלו נתייבשו
sources.says: Metzudat David says its people will be exiled and get no more good from the rivers, as if they had dried up.

sources.quote: והם לא ישמרו לתקן את היאורים, שהם החפירות שהיו מן היאור הגדול שבאמצע הארץ להוביל המים לכל חלקי המדינה
sources.says: Malbim says the new rulers will not take care to repair the channels, the ditches dug from the great river to carry water to every part of the land.

30:16.headline: A besieged city writhes like a woman giving birth
30:16.body: Radak says חול תחיל is the writhing of a woman in labor. Malbim says the prophet pictures the city's walls breaking open like a womb opening at birth.

sources.quote: והוא לשון חיל כיולדה
sources.says: Radak says it is the word for writhing, like a woman giving birth.

sources.quote: המליץ יצייר הבקעת העיר כחבלי יולדה ובקעית הרחם להפתח
sources.says: Malbim says the prophet pictures the breaching of the city as birth pangs and the womb breaking open.

sources.quote: עד שתחיל סין כיולדה בעת תחיל על המשבר להוציא הולד ויבקע הקרום ויפתח ויצא הנולד, שזה משל להבקעת המצור
sources.says: Malbim says Sin will writhe like a woman in labor when the membrane bursts and the baby comes out, a picture of the siege being broken.

30:16.headline: צרי יומם: foes every day, foes by daylight, or haters of day
30:16.body: Rashi says enemies will come day after day, and Metzudat David says they will attack openly by day, not like thieves at night. Malbim reads צרי as haters: the people of Noph will hate the daylight and long for dark to hide in.

sources.quote: צָרִים יָבוֹאוּ עָלֶיהָ יוֹם יוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says enemies will come upon it day after day.

sources.quote: הצרים יבואו עליה באור היום לכבשה ולא בלילה כגנבים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the enemies will come in daylight to capture it, not at night like thieves.

sources.quote: ונף צרי יומם הם ישנאו את היום כי יאהבו את הלילה שאז ימצאו סתר באופל מן האויב
sources.says: Malbim says the people of Noph will hate the day and love the night, when they can hide in the dark from the enemy.

sources.quote: שונאים את היום, כמו המה היו במרדי אור
sources.says: Malbim says it means haters of the day, like "they are among the rebels against light".

30:17.headline: "And they shall go captive": the cities, or the women?
30:17.body: הנה is a feminine "they". Rashi and Malbim say it means the two cities, since a city is feminine in Hebrew, while Metzudat David and Radak's father say it means the wives of the young men who fell.

sources.quote: שְׁתֵּיהֶן הַמְּדִינוֹת אָוֶן וּפִיבֶסֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it means both cities, Aven and Pi-beseth.

sources.quote: הערים עצמם, (שהעיר לשון נקבה) ר"ל יושביהם
sources.says: Malbim says it means the cities themselves, since "city" is feminine, that is, their people.

sources.quote: נשי החללים תלכנה בשבי
sources.says: Metzudat David says the wives of the slain will go into captivity.

sources.quote: ופירש אדוני אבי ז"ל כי על הנשים אמר
sources.says: Radak says his father explained that it speaks of the women.

30:21.headline: Pharaoh's broken arm is his defeat at Carchemish
30:21.body: Rashi and Radak say the arm already broken is the battle at Carchemish on the Euphrates, where Nebuchadnezzar beat Pharaoh's army. Radak says the strong arm still to be broken is Egypt itself, the land Pharaoh still held.

sources.quote: כְּבָר פַּעַם אַחֶרֶת, שֶׁנָּתַתִּי חֵילוֹ בְּיַד נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר בַּשָּׁנָה הָרְבִיעִית לִיהוֹיָקִים
sources.says: Rashi says it was broken once before, when God gave Pharaoh's army into Nebuchadnezzar's hand in Jehoiakim's fourth year.

sources.quote: זהו שנאמר בירמיה על חיל פרעה נכה מלך מצרים אשר היה על נהר פרת בכרכמיש
sources.says: Radak says this is what Jeremiah said about the army of Pharaoh Necho at the Euphrates in Carchemish.

sources.quote: והחזקה משל על ארצו שנשארה לו אחר שהכה אותו נבוכדנצאר על נהר פרת
sources.says: Radak says the strong arm is a picture of the land left to him after Nebuchadnezzar beat him at the Euphrates.

30:21.headline: Setting a broken arm: medicine, a soft wrap, then a tight bind
30:21.body: Malbim says חתול is a soft wrap around the break and חבישה is the tight binding over it, and Rashi links חתול to swaddling a newborn. Pharaoh's arm was never set this way, so it could not hold a sword again.

sources.quote: החיבוש הוא הקשירה בחזקה (עי' ישעיה א' ו), והחיתול היא כריכה סביב בדברים רכים
sources.says: Malbim says חבישה is tight binding, and חיתול is wrapping around with soft things.

sources.quote: צריך לשום רפואות במקום השבר להוציא הדם הנצרר והנגלד, ואח"כ לשים חיתול מדברים רכים, ואח"כ לחבש ולכרוך היטב על החיתול בחזקה
sources.says: Malbim says one must first put medicine on the break to draw out the clotted blood, then a soft wrap, then bind it tightly over the wrap.

sources.quote: מַעֲשֵׂה בְּגָדִים וּרְטִיָּה, כְּמוֹ ״וְהָחְתֵּל לֹא חֻתָּלְתְּ״
sources.says: Rashi says it is made of cloth and a plaster, like "and you were not swaddled".

30:25.headline: Two forms of one verb: God strengthens, then God holds up
30:25.body: In verse 24 וחזקתי means "I will strengthen". Rashi and Malbim say והחזקתי here means "I will grip": God holds Babylon's arms so they do not fall, while Pharaoh's arms, held by no one, drop.

sources.quote: וְחִזַּקְתִּי. לְשׁוֹן חוֹזֶק
sources.says: Rashi says וחזקתי in verse 24 is the word for strength.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן אֲחִיזָה, שֶׁאוֹחֵז בְּיָדוֹ לִסְמִיכָה שֶׁלֹּא תִּפֹּל; וְסוֹפוֹ יוֹכִיחַ: וּזְרֹעוֹת פַּרְעֹה תִּפֹּלְנָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹחֵז בָּהֶן
sources.says: Rashi says והחזקתי means gripping: He holds his arm to support it so it will not fall, and the end of the verse proves it, Pharaoh's arms will fall since He does not hold them.

sources.quote: חזק בבנין הכבד מורה על נתינת גבורה ואומץ, והחזיק בהפעיל משתתף עם תופש אוחז
sources.says: Malbim says חזק in one verb form means giving might and courage, while החזיק in another form shares a sense with grasping and holding.

31:3.headline: Above the tangled branches: Assyria stayed out of Babel's plot
31:3.body: עבתים means thick, braided branches. Radak brings a midrash on the word. When the whole world became 'one braid' to rebel at the Tower of Babel, Assyria kept apart, and so its top rose above them.

sources.quote: עבותים. ענין קליעה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means braiding.

sources.quote: שנעשו כל בעלי עולם קליעה אחת לבא בעצה ולמרוד בו
sources.says: Radak cites the midrash: when all the world became one braid to plot against God, Assyria stood apart.

31:4.headline: Raised by the deep, because Nineveh listened to Jonah
31:4.body: Plainly the deep is endless water, a picture of lasting success. Rashi and Radak bring a midrash. Assyria was raised because Nineveh listened to Jonah, the prophet who went down into the deep.

sources.quote: ואמר תהום שהוא לשון עומק מים רבים שלא יפסקו
sources.says: Radak says the deep means great waters that do not stop, so his greatness lasted a long time.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֶׁשָּׁמַע לְקוֹל יוֹנָה בֶּן אֲמִתַּי, שֶׁיָּרַד לַתְּהוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says it was because Assyria listened to Jonah son of Amittai, who went down into the deep.

31:5.headline: A rare word for branches, related to 'thoughts'
31:5.body: סרעפות appears only here. It means branches. Metzudat Zion suggests it shares a root with שרעפים, thoughts, just as סעיף can mean both a branch and a divided thought.

sources.quote: ויתכן שהוא מלשון ברוב שרעפי (תהלים צד) שהיא ענין מחשבה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means branches and may come from the word for thoughts in Psalms 94.

sources.quote: כי סרעפותיו והסעיף והפארה אחת בשמות שונים
sources.says: Radak says סרעפות, סעיף and פארה all mean branch, under different names.

31:8.headline: No cedar could hide him, or none could stand with him
31:8.body: עממהו is a rare verb. Metzudat Zion reads it as hiding or covering: no cedar could cast him in shadow. Malbim reads it from עם, with: no tree was his equal companion.

sources.quote: ענין הסתר וכסוי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means hiding and covering.

sources.quote: לא היו עמו ממלת עם
sources.says: Malbim says it means they were not with him, from the word עם.

sources.quote: לֹא כִּהוּ תָּאֳרוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says they did not dim his appearance; none was finer than he.

31:8.headline: Like him in beauty, not in shape
31:8.body: דמה means to be like. Maimonides cites this verse to show the word can mean being alike in one quality, not in shape. The trees of Eden were not like the cedar in its beauty. Malbim adds that דמה means a likeness, not being the same thing.

sources.quote: הוא דומוּת בעניין היופי
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse speaks of likeness in beauty, not in form.

sources.quote: לא היה כצבי רק נדמה לו
sources.says: Malbim says 'like' with דמה means resembling in one way, not being the thing itself.

31:11.headline: The mightiest of nations, or the one they treat as a god
31:11.body: איל גוים is said of Nebuchadnezzar. Metzudat Zion reads איל as strength: the mightiest of the nations. Malbim adds a second layer: the nations held him to be a god, אל.

sources.quote: ענין חוזק כמו אלי גבורים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means strength, like 'the mighty ones'.

sources.quote: ועפ"י המליצה שהגוים מחזיקים אותו לאל
sources.says: Malbim says it also hints that the nations treated him as a god.

sources.quote: בְּיַד קָשֶׁה שֶׁבַּגּוֹיִם, בְּיַד נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר נְתַתִּיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is the hardest of the nations, Nebuchadnezzar, who conquered Nineveh in his first year.

31:14.headline: 'To them', or 'their mighty ones', or a kind of tree
31:14.body: אליהם looks like 'to them'. Metzudat Zion reads it as 'their mighty ones', like אילי הארץ. Radak reads it as a name for great trees, from אלה and אלון, oak and terebinth.

sources.quote: ענין חוזק כמו ואת אילי הארץ לקח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means strength, like the mighty of the land.

sources.quote: ויהיו שם כלל לכל עצים
sources.says: Radak says it comes from the names of big trees like אלה and אלון, used here for all trees.

31:15.headline: The trees fainted
31:15.body: עלפה means to faint, a word used for people. Here it is said of trees. Rashi says their sap stopped, like a person who faints and whose breath leaves him.

sources.quote: כְּאָדָם שֶׁמִּתְעַלֵּף וְרוּחוֹ פּוֹרַחַת
sources.says: Rashi says their moisture stopped, like a person who faints and his breath flies away.

sources.quote: ענין העדר הרגשה וחלשות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means losing feeling and growing weak.

32:2.headline: "You were like a lion": or you only imagined you were
32:2.body: Radak says Pharaoh was among the nations like a young lion among wild beasts. Rashi reads it as Pharaoh's pride: he should have stayed in his rivers like a fish, but pictured himself a lion ruling the land.

sources.quote: כמו כפיר אריות בתוך חית השדה כן נדמית אתה בתוך הגוים
sources.says: Radak says that like a young lion among the beasts of the field, so were you among the nations.

sources.quote: היה לך לרבץ תוך יאורך כמשפט הדגים ולא לצאת אל היבשה, ונתגאית בלבך ונדמית בעצמך לכפיר השליט ביבשה
sources.says: Rashi says Pharaoh should have lain in his river like fish and not come out onto dry land, but he grew proud and pictured himself as a young lion ruling the land.

32:2.headline: The river monster: a crocodile, which Egypt held sacred
32:2.body: Metzudat Zion says the tannin is a large fish shaped like a snake. Malbim says the Egyptians believed the great tannin, the crocodile, was holy and ruled the waters.

sources.quote: כמו כתנין והוא דג גדול כדמות נחש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like "tannin", a large fish shaped like a snake.

sources.quote: כי המצרים היו מאמינים שהתנים הגדול שהוא הקראקאדיל קדוש ומושל במים
sources.says: Malbim says the Egyptians believed the great tannin, the crocodile, was holy and ruled the waters.

32:2.headline: A fish with feet: Pharaoh made himself legs
32:2.body: Rashi notes that a river creature has no feet. Pharaoh made himself legs like a land animal, so he could cross into other lands and trample their rivers.

sources.quote: רגלים לא היו לך, ועשית לך רגלים כחית הארץ לעבר מימי ארצות ולרפס נהרותם
sources.says: Rashi says you had no legs, and you made yourself legs like a land animal, to cross the waters of other lands and trample their rivers.

32:3.headline: A net for many fish, and a cherem for the great one
32:3.body: Rashi and Radak say חרם is another word for a net. Malbim says a net catches many fish at once, while the cherem is what destroys the one great fish, as in "cherem", utter destruction.

sources.quote: בחרמי. לשון מצודה
sources.says: Rashi says cherem is a word for a trap.

sources.quote: ברשת צדים דגים רבים בפעם א'
sources.says: Malbim says with a net one catches many fish at once.

sources.quote: מחריב הדג הגדול, כמו והכיתי את כל הארץ חרם
sources.says: Malbim says the cherem destroys the great fish, as in "I will strike the whole land with cherem".

32:6.headline: "The land you float in": Egypt flooded by the Nile
32:6.body: Rashi says it is the land where Pharaoh floats on his river, from צף, floating. Radak's father says Egypt is called this because the Nile's water floats over it, the way Israel "flows" with milk and honey.

sources.quote: ארץ אשר אתה צף בה על פני מימי יאוריך
sources.says: Rashi says it is the land where you float on the waters of your rivers.

sources.quote: וקרא הארץ צפה לפי שצפים המים עליה כמו שקרא הארץ זבת חלב ודבש לפי שהחלב זב עליה
sources.says: Radak says, in his father's name, that the land is called "floating" because water floats over it, just as a land is called "flowing with milk and honey" because milk flows on it.

32:7.headline: When Pharaoh is put out, the smoke darkens the sky
32:7.body: Rashi and Radak picture Pharaoh as a burning lamp: when it goes out, the smoke covers the sky. Radak says the whole verse is a picture of the disaster, and Maimonides lists it as Ezekiel describing the end of Egypt's kingdom.

sources.quote: כשתכבה תבערתך, יעלה העשן ויכסה השמים ויחשיך המאורות
sources.says: Rashi says that when your fire goes out, the smoke will rise, cover the heavens and darken the lights.

sources.quote: כאילו היה נר מאיר מרוב גדולתו ובכבותו יעלה עשן גדול עד שיכסה השמים
sources.says: Radak says Pharaoh was like a lamp shining in his greatness, and when it goes out a great smoke rises until it covers the heavens.

sources.quote: ויחזקאל אמר בתיאור אובדן ממלכת מצרים ומות פרעה על ידי נבוכדנצר
sources.says: The Guide says Ezekiel says this when describing the loss of Egypt's kingdom and Pharaoh's death by Nebuchadnezzar.

32:8.headline: "All the lights of heaven": stars, or Egypt's heavenly protectors
32:8.body: Radak says these are the bright planets, and the darkness is a picture: to anyone in trouble, the whole world seems dark. Rashi says the lights are the heavenly princes who speak up for Egypt.

sources.quote: חמשת הככבים המאירים על הארץ וכל זה דרך משל כי כל מי שתבא עליו הצרה ידמה לו כל העולם חשך
sources.says: Radak says these are the five planets that shine on the earth, and it is all a parable, since to anyone struck by trouble the whole world seems dark.

sources.quote: שרים של מעלה, מליציך
sources.says: Rashi says they are the princes above, your advocates.

32:10.headline: God's sword "flies": an army sent through, or a flashing blade
32:10.body: Rashi reads it as a flying bird: God sends an army through their lands. Radak says it means flashing and gleaming, or swinging the sword before their faces.

sources.quote: לשון עוף פורח (תנחומא, בשלח יח): בשלחי עליך חיל שלוחי דרך ארצם
sources.says: Rashi says it is the language of a flying bird: when I send an army against you through their land.

sources.quote: בעופפי ענין בהירות והברקה כמו תעופה בבקר תהיה ויש לפרש גם כן ענין תנועה
sources.says: Radak says it means brightness and flashing, as in "it shall shine like the morning", and it can also be read as movement.

32:10.headline: "They will tremble lirga'im": every moment, or for fear of breaking
32:10.body: Radak and Menachem, cited by Rashi, read it as moments: kings will tremble moment by moment. Rashi's first reading is "breakings": each fears the disaster will break upon him too.

sources.quote: לשברים, פן גם עליהן יבא השבר. לשון אחר: לשון ׳רגע׳ ממש, כן חברו מנחם
sources.says: Rashi says it means "for breakings", lest the breaking come on them too, and another reading takes it as a real moment, as Menachem grouped it.

sources.quote: מרגע לרגע יחרדו
sources.says: Radak says they will tremble from moment to moment.

32:16.headline: "Daughters of the nations" will lament: women, villages, or peoples
32:16.body: Radak gives three readings: villages, as in the Aramaic; women, since lamenting is women's custom; or whole peoples, as in "daughter of Zion". Metzudat Zion says it means a community.

sources.quote: בני הכפרים אשר בגוים יקוננו אותה וכן תירגם יונתן
sources.says: Radak says the people of the villages among the nations will lament, as Targum Jonathan translates.

sources.quote: ויש לפרש בנות כמשמעו נשים כי המספד והקינה היא מנהג הנשים
sources.says: Radak says "daughters" can be read plainly as women, since mourning and lament are the custom of women.

sources.quote: או פירוש בנות הגוים קהלות הגוים כמו בת ציון בת אדום שפירושו עדה
sources.says: Radak says it can mean the communities of the nations, as in "daughter of Zion", which means a community.

32:18.headline: "Wail for Egypt": the prophet is not really mourning
32:18.body: Radak says Ezekiel does not truly weep for Egypt. He would rejoice at its fall, but he speaks the words that mourners will say.

sources.quote: לא שהנביא יקונן וינהה עליהם אבל ישמח על חרבנם ועל אבדם אלא שיאמר הדברים שיקוננו בהם המקוננים
sources.says: Radak says it is not that the prophet will lament and wail over them, since he would rejoice at their ruin, but that he will say the words the mourners will use.

32:18.headline: "Bring him down": by prophecy, or by lament
32:18.body: Radak says the prophet brings Egypt down to the pit by his words of prophecy; others take it from "I lament in my grief". Rashi says God showed Ezekiel that all who deny prophecy go down to Gehinnom.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר שיורידוהו בדברו ובנבואתו ויש מפרשים אותו מענין אריד בשיחי
sources.says: Radak says it means the prophet will bring him down by his word and prophecy, and some explain it from "I lament in my complaint".

sources.quote: כאן הראהו הקדוש ברוך הוא ליחזקאל, שכל מכחישי הנבואה יורדין לגיהנם
sources.says: Rashi says here God showed Ezekiel that all who deny prophecy go down to Gehinnom.

32:21.headline: "They will speak to him": Rashi says it means "about him"
32:21.body: Rashi sets a rule: "to him", "to me" or "to them" next to a verb of speaking means "about". So the mighty dead will talk about Pharaoh and his helpers, not to them.

sources.quote: כל לו ולי ולהם ולך הסמוכין לדבור, אינם אלא לשון על
sources.says: Rashi says every "to him, to me, to them, to you" placed next to speaking means "about".

sources.quote: ידברו לו. ידברו עליו ועל עוזריו
sources.says: Rashi says "they will speak to him" means they will speak about him and his helpers.

sources.quote: כל דבור שאחריו למ"ד היינו בשבילו, כמו שיסד רש"י ז"ל
sources.says: Malbim says every "speaking" followed by lamed means "on his account", as Rashi established.

32:23.headline: "The land of the living": this world, or the land of Israel
32:23.body: Radak says it is the world of the living: they spread terror while alive, and now lie in the land of the dead. Rashi and the Aramaic say it is the land of Israel, which they broke.

sources.quote: שנתנו מוראם וחתיתם בבני אדם בעודם חיים ולפיכך אמר בארץ חיים לפי שהם עתה בארץ מתים
sources.says: Radak says they spread fear and terror among people while alive, and the verse says "land of the living" because they are now in the land of the dead.

sources.quote: ויונתן תירגם על דשליטו בארעא דישראל
sources.says: Radak says Targum Jonathan translates it "because they ruled over the land of Israel".

sources.quote: אשר נתנו שבר בארץ ישראל
sources.says: Rashi says it means those who brought ruin on the land of Israel.

32:27.headline: "Fallen ones": warriors who died in bed, or simply "lesser"
32:27.body: Radak first reads it as warriors who "fell" by dying a natural death, not by the sword. Rashi, and Radak's second reading, take it as "lesser", as in Job 12:3: these dead rank below those warriors.

sources.quote: אמר כי עם חללי חרב ישכבו ולא עם הגבורים שנפלו כלומר שמתו מיתת עצמם שלא נפלו בחרב
sources.says: Radak says they will lie with those slain by the sword, not with the warriors who fell, meaning those who died a natural death and not by the sword.

sources.quote: כי נופלין וגרועים יהיו מערלים אשר מתו מיתת עצמם
sources.says: Rashi says they will be lower and lesser than the uncircumcised who died a natural death.

sources.quote: ויש לפרש נופלים מערלים כמו לא נופל אנכי מכם כלומר פחותים יהיו מאותם ערלים
sources.says: Radak says "noflim" can be read as in "I am not inferior to you", meaning they will be lower than those uncircumcised.

sources.quote: לא פחות וגרוע וכן נופלים מערלים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says "not fallen" means not lower or lesser, and so too "fallen from the uncircumcised" in Ezekiel.

32:27.headline: "Their sins on their bones": unforgiven, or bones broken by swords
32:27.body: Rashi says their sin stayed whole, because a death by the sword, which would have atoned, never came. Radak reads it plainly: their punishment fell on their bones, stabbed and broken by swords.

sources.quote: לא נחסר מעוונם כלום, שלא כפרה עליהם חרב הריגה, שלא נהרגו
sources.says: Rashi says nothing was taken off their sin, since no killing sword atoned for them, because they were not killed.

sources.quote: כלומר שדקרו אותם בחרב ושברו עצמותיהם
sources.says: Radak says it means they were stabbed with the sword and their bones were broken.

sources.quote: שלא יתכפר להם ע"י כלות בשרם כי עוד ישאר עונם על עצמותיהם
sources.says: Malbim says they will not be atoned through the wasting of their flesh, since their sin will remain on their bones.

32:32.headline: Written "his terror", read "My terror"
32:32.body: The word is written חתיתו, "his terror", but read חתיתי, "My terror". Radak says the written form means God gave Pharaoh his power to frighten; the reading means God puts His own terror on those who spread terror.

sources.quote: כתוב בוי"ו וקרי ביו"ד
sources.says: Radak says it is written with a vav and read with a yod.

sources.quote: כי חתית פרעה אני נתתי אותו לא בכח ידו ובגבורתו והקרי פירוש כי אני נתתי חתיתי בארץ חיים באותם שנתנו חתית
sources.says: Radak says the written form means "I gave Pharaoh his terror, not by his own strength", and the reading means "I put My terror in the land of the living on those who spread terror".

sources.quote: כי אתן אני את מוראי בארץ ישראל
sources.says: Rashi says it means God will put His own fear in the land of Israel.

33:4.headline: Hearing that understands, and hearing that only hears
33:4.body: Malbim says the first "hear" in verse 4 means understanding the shofar's signals, and the second, in verse 5, means only hearing the sound. Either way the listener should have fled, so his blood is on his own head.

sources.quote: הראשון מלשון הבנה, והשני מלשון שמיעה
sources.says: Malbim says the first is the word for understanding and the second the word for hearing.

sources.quote: ר"ל מי ששומע ומבין סימני התקיעות והאותות שהקול מורה עליהם ולא נזהר דמו בראשו יהיה
sources.says: Malbim says it means one who hears and understands the signals of the blasts and does not take care: his blood is on his own head.

sources.quote: שאף מי שאינו יודע אותות השופר וסימניה, עכ"פ את קול השופר שמע והיה לו להזהר ולברוח
sources.says: Malbim says even one who does not know the shofar's signals at least heard the sound and should have taken care and fled.

33:7.headline: The prophet is the watchman, and his words are the shofar
33:7.body: Rashi says God set Ezekiel to warn Israel the way a city sets a watchman to warn of an enemy, and Radak says the shofar is the prophet's voice. The Aramaic translation calls him not a watchman but a teacher.

sources.quote: כְּאוֹתוֹ הַצּוֹפֶה הַנִּיתָּן לְהַזְהִיר שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאבַד נֶפֶשׁ, כֵּן נְתַתִּיךָ לְהַזְהִיר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says like the watchman set up to warn so no life is lost, so I set you to warn Israel.

sources.quote: וקול השופר. הוא דבר הנביא כמו שאמר הרם כשופר קולך והגד לעמי פשעם
sources.says: Radak says the sound of the shofar is the word of the prophet, as it says "raise your voice like a shofar and tell My people their sin".

sources.quote: וְאַתְּ בַּר אָדָם מַלֵיף מַנִיתָךְ לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and you, son of man, I have appointed you a teacher for the house of Israel".

33:8.headline: "I will seek his blood from you": the prophet as guarantor
33:8.body: Malbim says "demand from the hand of" in verse 6 means punishment, but "seek from your hand" here is how one claims a debt from a guarantor. It is what Judah said of Benjamin: "I will be his surety, from my hand you may seek him."

sources.quote: ויש הבדל בין דרישה ובקשה שאחריה מלת מיד, הדרישה היא להעניש
sources.says: Malbim says there is a difference between "demand" and "seek" when followed by "from the hand of": demanding is to punish.

sources.quote: והבקשה היא בקשת התשלומין בדבר שנכנס לערבון עליו, כמו אנכי אחטנה מידי תבקשנה, אנכי אערבנו מידי תבקשנו
sources.says: Malbim says seeking is claiming payment for something one took on as a guarantor, as in "I will be his surety; from my hand you may seek him".

sources.quote: ר"ל את הנכנס כערב בעד הנפשות שמסרתים בידך להשגיח עליהם
sources.says: Malbim says it means you, who stood as guarantor for the souls I handed to your care.

33:10.headline: Two words for sin: rebellion, and giving in to desire
33:10.body: Malbim says פשע is rebellion and חטא is a wrong done out of desire, not defiance. The people fear both: they rebelled against the King and spoiled His work.

sources.quote: הפשעים הם המרדים, והחטאות הם הנעשים מסבת התאוה, לא מצד המרד
sources.says: Malbim says פשעים are rebellions, and חטאות are done because of desire, not out of rebellion.

sources.quote: כי פשעינו עלינו שמרדנו במלכו של עולם, ועוד שחטאותינו עלינו שהם המעשים עצמם שקלקלנו מלאכתו ועבודתו
sources.says: Malbim says "our rebellions are on us" because we rebelled against the King of the world, and "our sins" are the acts themselves by which we spoiled His work.

33:10.headline: Rotting away in our sins: the people think it is too late
33:10.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak say נמקים means melting or rotting away, as flesh rots. Malbim says the people picture a patient who ignored the doctor and is now wasting away, too far gone for regret to help.

sources.quote: נמקים. מל׳ המקה והמסה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the words for rotting and melting.

sources.quote: שרשו מקק מענין המק בשרו
sources.says: Radak says its root is מקק, as in "his flesh shall rot".

sources.quote: ואם עבר החולה על דברי הרופא עד שהוא נימק בחליו מה יועיל לו החרטה והתשובה
sources.says: Malbim says if a patient disobeyed the doctor until he is rotting in his illness, what good will regret and return do him?

33:11.headline: When one wicked man dies, God wants another to return
33:11.body: Malbim notes the verse says "the wicked" and then "a wicked one", and reads the second as a different person. God does not want the sinner's death for its own sake: it is meant to move another sinner to come back.

sources.quote: שהשם הנשנה יורה שאינו השם הראשון, ור"ל בשוב רשע אחר
sources.says: Malbim says a repeated noun shows it is not the first one, so it means when another wicked man returns.

sources.quote: וגם אם יגזור מיתה על הרשע אין תכליתו מות הרשע, רק תכליתו שעי"כ יראה רשע אחר וישים על לבו לשוב
sources.says: Malbim says even if God decrees death on the wicked, the aim is not his death, but that another wicked man will see it and resolve to return.

sources.quote: אין כוונתי בהבאת העונש להתנקם בו כאלו הייתי חפץ במיתתו אלא הכוונה היא לעוררו לשוב מדרכו הרעה למען יחיה
sources.says: Metzudat David says God means by punishment not revenge, as if He wanted his death, but to stir him to turn from his bad way and live.

33:31.headline: Their heart follows their בצע: stolen goods, or just desire?
33:31.body: Rashi reads בצע as robbery, and the Aramaic speaks of money taken by force. Metzudat Zion reads it as desire, and Metzudat David says what they crave is the mockery itself.

sources.quote: בִּצְעָם. גְּזֵלָתָם
sources.says: Rashi says בצעם means their robbery.

sources.quote: בָּתַר מָמוֹן אוּנְסֵיהוֹן לִבְּהוֹן טָעֵי
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "their heart strays after the money of their extortion".

sources.quote: בצעם. ענין חמדה כמו מה בצע בדמי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means desire, as in "what gain is there in my blood".

sources.quote: ולבם הולך אחר חמדתם הוא הלצון אשר חמדו
sources.says: Metzudat David says their heart goes after what they desire, which is the mockery they crave.

33:32.headline: A love song, a joke, or a tune on the pipes
33:32.body: Radak calls שיר עגבים a song of desire and jest, and Metzudat David says the people treat the prophecy as clever entertainment. The Aramaic hears עוגב, a pipe, and renders it "like the song of pipes".

sources.quote: כשיר חשק ודברי שחוק
sources.says: Radak says it is like a song of desire and words of jest.

sources.quote: עֲגָבִים. שְׂחוֹק, כְּמוֹ ״עוּגָב״
sources.says: Rashi says עגבים means laughter, like the word עוגב.

sources.quote: הנה דברי נבואתך בעיניהם כשיר הלעג בצחות המליצה
sources.says: Metzudat David says your prophecies are in their eyes like a song of mockery in polished speech.

sources.quote: תירגם עגבים כמו עוגבים כי תרגום עוגב אבובא
sources.says: Radak says Jonathan translated עגבים as if it were עוגבים, because the Aramaic for עוגב, a pipe, is אבובא.

sources.quote: וְהָא אַתְּ לְהוֹן כִּזְמַר אֲבּוּבִין
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and behold you are to them like the song of pipes".

34:2.headline: Shepherds who fed 'them', meaning themselves
34:2.body: The verse says the shepherds were רעים אותם, feeding 'them'. Rashi, Radak and the Targum read 'them' as themselves: the leaders fed themselves at the people's cost. Malbim says a paid shepherd feeds the flock and is fed by it in turn.

sources.quote: אֶת עַצְמָם הָיוּ מְעַנְּגִין, מִמָּמוֹן חֲבֵרֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they pampered themselves with the money of the people under them.

sources.quote: עצמם וכן וירעו הרועים אותם עצמם
sources.says: Radak says אותם means themselves, as again in verse 8.

sources.quote: דַהֲווֹ מְפַרְנְסִין נַפְשֵׁיהוֹן
sources.says: The Targum says they were providing for themselves.

sources.quote: נמצא הוא רועה אותם והם רועים אותו ג"כ
sources.says: Malbim says a paid shepherd tends the flock and the flock also feeds him.

34:4.headline: The weak and the sick are not the same
34:4.body: The shepherds did not strengthen הנחלות or heal החולה. Malbim says נחלה is an animal just starting to fall ill, which only needs strengthening. החולה is already sick and needs healing. Rashi says the נחלות are the weak ones that need holding up by hand.

sources.quote: נחלה מצייר תחלת פעולת החולי
sources.says: Malbim says נחלה describes the start of an illness.

sources.quote: הראשון די לו בחיזוק, והשני צריך רפואה
sources.says: Malbim says the first only needs strengthening and the second needs healing.

sources.quote: שֶׁצְּרִיכוֹת חִזּוּק, לִתְמֹךְ בָּהֶן בַּיָּד
sources.says: Rashi says they are weak ones that need strengthening, to be held up by hand.

34:6.headline: Nobody searched for the lost sheep, or asked who found it
34:6.body: The verse says no one דורש and no one מבקש. Malbim says בקשה is searching to find the lost sheep. דרישה is asking for it back from whoever found it, by naming its marks. Here nobody did either one.

sources.quote: בקשת האובד הוא כדי למצאו
sources.says: Malbim says בקשה of a lost thing is searching in order to find it.

sources.quote: ודרישת האובד הוא לקחתו מיד המוצאו ע"י סימנים
sources.says: Malbim says דרישה is taking it back from the finder by giving its identifying signs.

sources.quote: ולא לבד שאין דורש מאת המוצא האבדה, כי גם אין מבקש את האבדה כלל
sources.says: Malbim says no one asked the finder for the lost sheep, and no one even searched for it.

34:10.headline: Seeking the sheep from the shepherds means making them pay
34:10.body: God says ודרשתי את צאני מידם. Metzudat Zion says this word is used for paying someone back, and Radak says God will punish the shepherds. In verse 11 the same word means God will go looking for His sheep.

sources.quote: זה הלשון יאמר על תשלומי הגמול וכן אנכי אדרש מעמו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says this word is used for paying back what is due, as in Deuteronomy 18:19.

sources.quote: שאעניש אותם על אשר לא רעו אותם
sources.says: Radak says God will punish them for not tending the sheep.

sources.quote: ואני אדרוש את צאני ואחקור אחריה׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says that in verse 11 God will seek His sheep and search for them.

34:11.headline: God will check on His flock, like visiting the sick
