34:11.body: Rashi says ובקרתים is the word used for visiting the sick. Metzudat Zion says it means searching and inquiring, as a priest examines a sore (Leviticus 13:36). Malbim says it means counting the flock and checking where the missing ones are.

sources.quote: וּבִקַּרְתִּים. לְשׁוֹן בִּקּוּר חוֹלִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is the word used for visiting the sick.

sources.quote: ענין חקירה ודרישה כמו לא יבקר הכהן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means searching and inquiring, as in Leviticus 13:36.

sources.quote: הביקור הוא לדעת מנינם, ולהשגיח על החסרים היכן הם
sources.says: Malbim says it means knowing their number and looking out for where the missing ones are.

34:18.headline: Clear water, after the mud has sunk to the bottom
34:18.body: The strong sheep drink משקע מים and muddy the rest with their feet. Rashi and Malbim say it is clear water, where the mud has sunk down. Its opposite is the trampled, muddy water in the next verse.

sources.quote: הַמַּיִם הַצְּלוּלִים, שֶׁשָּׁקַע הַטִּיט, וְלֹא נֶעֶכְרוּ בְרַגְלַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says it is clear water whose mud has settled and that feet have not stirred up.

sources.quote: שנשקע הטיט למצולת המים והם נקיים, והפוכו הוא הנרפש
sources.says: Malbim says the mud has sunk to the bottom and the water is clean, and the opposite is נרפש, muddied.

sources.quote: מים צלולים ששקעה הטיט אותם תשתו ואת הנותר תדרכו ברגליכם לעכור אותם
sources.says: Metzudat David says you drink the clear water and tread the rest with your feet to muddy it.

34:20.headline: A fat sheep and a thin one stand for rich and poor
34:20.body: בריה is a short spelling of בריאה, fat. Malbim and Radak say so, and Metzudat Zion compares Eglon, 'a very fat man'. Radak follows the Targum: God will judge between the rich man and the poor man.

sources.quote: משפטו בריאה, ר"ל שמנה
sources.says: Malbim says the full form is בריאה, meaning fat.

sources.quote: כמו בריאה ופירושו שמנה והמשל כתרגומו בין גבר עתיר ובין גבר מסכן
sources.says: Radak says it is like בריאה, fat, and the parable means, as the Targum says, a rich man and a poor man.

sources.quote: שמנה כמו ועגלון איש בריא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means fat, as Eglon was 'a fat man' (Judges 3:17).

34:25.headline: Sleep safely in the woods, or grow old there?
34:25.body: Radak reads וישנו as sleep: they will sleep in the forests with no fear of wild animals. The Targum instead uses ויתעתקון, from the Aramaic word for old, as if from ישן, 'old'. Rashi quotes the Targum and adds that it can also mean sleep.

sources.quote: כי לא יפחדו מחית היער. וישנו ענין שינה
sources.says: Radak says they will not fear the forest animals, and וישנו means sleeping.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְיִתְעַתְּקוּן בְּחוּרְשָׁא״, וְיֵשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ בִּלְשׁוֹן שִׁינָה
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum's ויתעתקון and says it can also be explained as sleep.

sources.quote: וְיִתְעַתְּקוּן בִּרְחוּשָׁא
sources.says: The Targum renders the phrase with ויתעתקון in the forest.

34:31.headline: The flock turns out to be people
34:31.body: After a whole chapter calling Israel sheep, God says אדם אתם, 'you are human'. Rashi says: you are not like animals in my eyes. Radak says a flock fed on knowledge and understanding is called human, not cattle.

sources.quote: אָדָם אַתֶּם. אֵינְכֶם כַּבְּהֵמוֹת בְּעֵינַי
sources.says: Rashi says it means you are not like animals in my eyes.

sources.quote: כשתהיו צאן מרעיתי שארעה אתכם דעה ובינה והשכל אז תקראו אדם לא צאן ובהמה
sources.says: Radak says that when God feeds them knowledge and understanding, they will be called human, not sheep and cattle.

sources.quote: דעו שאדם אתם ר״ל אינכם בעיני כבהמות
sources.says: Metzudat David says: know that you are human, not like animals in God's eyes.

36:2.headline: 'Heights of the world': the high land, or the high trade?
36:2.body: The enemy gloats that the 'everlasting heights' are now theirs. Rashi and Radak say this is the Land of Israel, higher than all other lands, while Malbim says it means the rich trade that the whole world came up to.

sources.quote: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא גָּבְהוֹ וְנוֹיוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Land of Israel, the height and beauty of the world.

sources.quote: קרא הרי ישראל במות עולם לפי שא"י גבוה מכל הארצות
sources.says: Radak says the mountains of Israel are called heights because the land is higher than all lands.

sources.quote: ר"ל שנירש במות עולם והמסחר הגבוה שכל העולם עולים שמה לסחורה
sources.says: Malbim says the enemy meant to inherit the high trade that the whole world went up to for business.

36:3.headline: Swallowed up, the way one gulps in a breath
36:3.body: שאף means to draw in breath. Metzudat Zion and Malbim say that here it means to gulp something down, so the nations around wanted to swallow Israel whole, and Rashi says they longed for it.

sources.quote: ענין בליעה והמשכה אל הפה כמו שאפה רוח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means swallowing and drawing into the mouth, as in 'sniffs the wind' in Jeremiah 2.

sources.quote: הושאל ממשיכת הרוח אל תוכו אל כל התאב לבלוע איזה דבר
sources.says: Malbim says the word is borrowed from drawing breath in, and used for anyone eager to swallow something.

sources.quote: וְשׁוֹאֲפִים וְתָאֵבִים וּמְצַפִּים לִהְיוֹתְכֶם מוֹרָשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says the neighbors longed and waited for Israel's land to become theirs.

36:8.headline: 'They are near to coming', or 'bring your coming near'
36:8.body: The mountains must bear fruit, 'for they are near to coming'. Radak says it can also mean 'bring your coming near' through repentance and good deeds, and the Targum says the day of redemption is near.

sources.quote: או פירושו קרבו לבא קרבי ביאתכם בתשובה ומעשים טובים
sources.says: Radak offers a second reading: bring your coming near by repentance and good deeds.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי קָרִיב יוֹם פּוּרְקָנִי לְמֵיתֵי
sources.says: The Targum says the day of my redemption is near to come.

36:13.headline: The land as a mother who loses her children
36:13.body: משכלת comes from שכול, losing children. Malbim says the land is pictured as a mother and the nations driven out of it as the children she lost, and Rashi says driving people out of the land is called bereavement.

sources.quote: שמציין הארץ כאם היולדת והגוים הנגרשים ממנה שמשכלת אותם
sources.says: Malbim says the land is shown as a mother who gives birth, and the nations driven from it are the children she loses.

sources.quote: לְגָרֵשׁ יוֹשְׁבַיִךְ מִקִּרְבֵּךְ, הוּא קָרוּי שִׁכּוּל
sources.says: Rashi says driving out the land's people is called bereavement.

36:14.headline: Written 'stumble', read 'bereave'
36:14.body: The word is written תכשלי, from the root for stumbling, but read תשכלי, 'you will bereave'. Radak notes the two forms and says their meanings are close.

sources.quote: כתיב וקרי תשכלי וענינה קרוב
sources.says: Radak says the word is written one way and read תשכלי, and the two meanings are close.

36:15.headline: No more stumbling: into death, or into sin?
36:15.body: God promises the land will no longer make its nation stumble. Metzudat David says the people will no longer perish there, while Malbim says they will no longer stumble into sin, because they will be righteous.

sources.quote: כי מאז לא תכשילי עוד את גוייך להיות נאבדים בך
sources.says: Metzudat David says the land will no longer cause its people to be lost in it.

sources.quote: כי גויך לא תכשילי עוד בחטא כי יהיו צדיקים
sources.says: Malbim says the land will no longer make its people stumble in sin, because they will be righteous.

36:17.headline: A comparison that promises return: the husband waits to come back
36:17.body: Israel's impurity is compared to a woman's monthly impurity. Rashi and Radak say the point is that the husband keeps apart only for a time and longs to return, so God sent Israel away and will bring them back.

sources.quote: הִמְשִׁילָהּ הַכָּתוּב לְנִדָּה, שֶׁבַּעְלָהּ מְצַפֶּה מָתַי תִּטְהַר וְתָאֵב לָשׁוּב אֵלֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says the verse compares Israel to a niddah, whose husband waits for her to be pure and longs to return to her.

sources.quote: שהבעל מרחיקה כל ימי נדותה ומקרבה אחרי טהרתה וכן הרחיק האל יתברך ישראל והגלם לארצות העמים מפני חטאתם ועתיד להחזירם
sources.says: Radak says as a husband keeps apart in those days and comes close after, God exiled Israel for their sins and will bring them back.

36:20.headline: 'And he came': the people, or God going with them into exile?
36:20.body: The verb is singular, 'he came', though it speaks of the whole people. Rashi says it treats the house of Israel as one, but also brings a midrash that God himself went with them into exile, and Malbim reads it as God's name going with them.

sources.quote: קָרָא כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה בִּלְשׁוֹן יָחִיד. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא עִמָּהֶם בַּגּוֹלָה
sources.says: Rashi says the passage speaks in the singular, and cites a midrash that God came with them into exile.

sources.quote: לשון יחיד דרך כלל ובדרש על דרך בכל צרתם לו צר
sources.says: Radak says the singular speaks of the people as one, and the midrash reads it like 'in all their trouble He was troubled'.

sources.quote: ששם ה' בא עמהם לגלות, כי שם ה' נקרא עליהם
sources.says: Malbim says God's name went with them into exile, because His name is called upon them.

36:27.headline: 'My spirit': prophecy returning, or a new nature?
36:27.body: God promises to put His spirit inside them. Metzudat David says this is the spirit of prophecy, missing all through the exile, while Malbim says the holy spirit will give them a new nature that leans toward holiness.

sources.quote: אחזיר לכם רוח הנבואה מה שהיה נחסר כל ימי הגולה
sources.says: Metzudat David says God will return the spirit of prophecy that was missing all the days of exile.

sources.quote: תקבלו טבע אחרת נוטה אל הקדושה והטהרה
sources.says: Malbim says they will receive a different nature, inclined to holiness and purity.

sources.quote: וְיַת רוּחַ קוּדְשִׁי אֶתֵּן בְּמֵיעֵיכוֹן
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'my holy spirit I will put inside you'.

36:31.headline: Loathing yourselves: wasting away, or cut off in your own eyes
36:31.body: ונקטתם is a rare verb. Rashi says they will waste away in shame for repaying God's good with evil, while Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as being cut off in their own eyes, admitting the exile was just.

sources.quote: תִּמַּקּוּ בְּעַצְמֵיכֶם, בְּבָשְׁתְּכֶם עַל הַגְּמוּל הָרָע אֲשֶׁר גְּמַלְתֶּם לְפָנַי
sources.says: Rashi says they will waste away inside, in shame over the evil they paid back to God.

sources.quote: תהיו נכרתים בעיני עצמכם כשתזכרו עונותיכם תאמרו בדין הכריתנו האל יתברך
sources.says: Radak says they will be cut off in their own eyes and say God was just to cut them off.

sources.quote: ענין כריתה כמו ונקוטו בפניהם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means cutting off.

36:38.headline: Flocks of holy offerings, or a holy people?
36:38.body: The empty cities will fill 'like the holy flock' of Jerusalem at the festivals. Rashi says these are the flocks brought for Passover, while the Targum turns the sheep into people: the holy, purified people who come to Jerusalem.

sources.quote: שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּמוֹעֲדֵי פְּסָחִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is the flock that comes to Jerusalem at the Passover festivals.

sources.quote: כְּעַמָא קַדִישָׁא כְּעַמָא דִמְדַכָּן וְאָתָן לִירוּשְׁלֵם בִּזְמַן מוֹעֲדֵי פִּסְחָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'like the holy people, the purified people who come to Jerusalem at Passover'.

39:2.headline: Lure you on, or leave only a sixth of you?
39:2.body: Rashi and the Metzudat Zion read וששאתיך as 'I will lead you on', the way the serpent misled Eve. Radak brings readings from the word for six: only a sixth of Gog's army will be left, or, as his father taught, Gog will be judged with six punishments.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ וְהִשֵּׁאתִיךָ עַל עַמִּי
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'I will lead you on', like the Psalm's 'no enemy shall deceive him'.

sources.quote: וששאתיך. ענין הסתה ופתוי כמו הנחש השיאני
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means enticing and luring, as in Eve's 'the serpent misled me'.

sources.quote: פירשו בו שהוא מלשון ששה כלומר שלא ישאר בהם כי אם ששית המחנה
sources.says: Radak reports a reading from the word six: only a sixth of the camp will remain.

sources.quote: פירש אשפטף בששה שפטים כמו שאמר ונשפטתי אתו
sources.says: Radak says his father read it as 'I will judge you with six punishments', which the previous chapter lists.

39:7.headline: Israel crushed makes God's name look weak
39:7.body: The verse says God will no longer let his name be profaned. Rashi explains how: when Israel is low, people say these are God's people and he could not save them. Radak says a long exile makes it look as if God himself shamed his name.

sources.quote: שִׁפְלוּתָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל חִלּוּל שְׁמוֹ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says Israel's low state is itself a profaning of God's name, since people say he could not save them.

sources.quote: כי בהאריכו הגלות שמו מחולל בגוים
sources.says: Radak says that while the exile drags on, God's name is profaned among the nations.

39:9.headline: Two words for lighting fires: one to warm, one to bake
39:9.body: השיקו is a rare word. Rashi reads it from the Mishnah's word for heating an oven. Radak says it just repeats 'they will burn', but Malbim says the first fire is for warmth and the second is for baking bread.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ תַּנּוּר שֶׁהִשּׂיקוּהוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is the word the Mishnah uses for heating an oven.

sources.quote: ובערו והשיקו. כפל הענין במלות שונות
sources.says: Radak says the two verbs say one thing twice in different words.

sources.quote: הביעור הוא לחמם, וההסק הוא לאפות בו
sources.says: Malbim says בער is a fire for warmth and השיק is a fire for baking.

39:9.headline: How do you burn weapons? You burn their wooden handles
39:9.body: The verse says Israel will make fires from the enemy's weapons for seven years. The Metzudat David says what burns is the wooden handles. Malbim adds that Israel will not need weapons anymore, since God fights for them.

sources.quote: בנשק וגו׳. ר״ל בידות הכלים ההם שהם של עץ
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it means the handles of those weapons, which are made of wood.

sources.quote: כי לא יצטרכו מעתה לכלי נשק אחר שה' נלחם להם
sources.says: Malbim says they will not need weapons from then on, since God fights for them.

39:11.headline: Why Gog gets a grave: a reward for his ancestor Japheth
39:11.body: Rashi brings a midrash: Gog descends from Japheth, who covered his father Noah's nakedness, so his people earn a burial. Radak gives the same midrash, then says the plain reason is in the text: the dead are buried to make the land clean.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל יֶפֶת, שֶׁכִּסָּה אֶת עֶרְוַת אָבִיו, לְפִיכָךְ זָכָה לִקְבוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says Gog comes from Japheth, who covered his father's nakedness, so he earned burial.

sources.quote: וזכה יפת לקבורה בארץ ישראל ועל דרך פשוטו הרי כתוב למען טהר את הארץ
sources.says: Radak says the midrash rewards Japheth with burial, but by the plain meaning the reason is to purify the land.

39:11.headline: Blocking the road, or blocking the nose?
39:11.body: חסם means to block, as with a muzzle. Rashi and the Metzudat David say the piles of bodies will block travelers from passing. Menachem, cited by Rashi, and Radak say travelers will block their noses against the smell.

sources.quote: וְסוֹגֶרֶת הִיא אֶת הָעוֹבְרִים
sources.says: Rashi says the valley will close off the travelers, because the many bodies stop them from crossing.

sources.quote: יַחְסְמוּ אֶת אַפָּם מִלְּהָרִיחַ רֵיחַ הַפְּגָרִים
sources.says: Rashi cites Menachem, who reads it as people blocking their noses from the smell of the bodies.

sources.quote: שיחסמו ויסגרו אפיהם מריח הרע
sources.says: Radak says the travelers will block and close their noses from the bad smell.

sources.quote: מפלת מרבית הפגרים תסתום ותסגור את העוברים
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the fallen bodies will block the way for those passing.

39:14.headline: Burying with the travelers, or burying the travelers?
39:14.body: The little word את can point to the object, or it can mean 'with'. Rashi and Radak read 'with': the burial crews work together with people passing through. Malbim reads it as the object: these 'passers' are Gog's soldiers who wandered off and died.

sources.quote: מְקַבְּרִים עִם הָעוֹבְרִים אֶת הַפְּגָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says they bury the bodies together with the travelers.

sources.quote: את העוברים. כמו עם העוברים
sources.says: Radak says את here means 'with' the travelers.

sources.quote: אלה מן הצובאים שנודדו ועברו בארץ ומתו במגפה
sources.says: Malbim says the passers are invading soldiers who wandered through the land and died in the plague.

sources.quote: את העוברים.  מאנשי גוג
sources.says: Malbim says the passers are Gog's men.

39:17.headline: Gather, then come in: two verbs, two steps
39:17.body: The verse uses two words for gathering, הקבצו and האספו. Malbim says they are not the same. First the scattered birds flock together, then the flock comes in to the battlefield.

sources.quote: הקבוץ הוא שיתקבצו הנפזרים
sources.says: Malbim says קבץ is the scattered coming together, and אסף is then entering the battlefield.

sources.quote: הקבצו המפוזרות יתקבצו ביחד, ואחר שיהיו מקובצים יתאספו לבא ביחד אל מקום ההרוגים
sources.says: Malbim says the scattered birds first group together, and once grouped they come together to where the dead lie.

39:18.headline: A fattened ox, a word Rashi also finds in Arabic
39:18.body: מריאי בשן means animals fattened in the rich pastures of Bashan. Rashi says Arabic calls a fattened ox by a similar word, almari. The Metzudat Zion links it to Amos's 'your fatted offerings'.

sources.quote: שׁוֹר שֶׁל פַּטָּם קָרוּי אַלמְרִ״י בִּלְשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי
sources.says: Rashi says a fattened ox is called almari in Arabic.

sources.quote: מריאי בשן. ענין פטום ושמן כמו ושלם מריאכם
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means fattened, as in Amos's 'the peace offerings of your fatlings'.

39:25.headline: Jacob and Israel: two names for two parts of the people
39:25.body: The verse says God will bring back יעקב and have mercy on בית ישראל. Malbim says Jacob here means the ten northern tribes, who only need to be brought home. Israel means Judah and Benjamin, who suffered much and need mercy.

sources.quote: יציין עשרת השבטים בשם יעקב, ושבט יהודה ובנימין בשם ישראל
sources.says: Malbim says the prophet marks the ten tribes with the name Jacob, and Judah and Benjamin with the name Israel.

sources.quote: ויעקב הם עשרת השבטים הם רק נדחים ולא סבלו שמדות
sources.says: Malbim says Jacob is the ten tribes, who were only scattered and did not suffer persecution, so they need only to be returned.

39:29.headline: God's 'face' is a picture for his presence
39:29.body: God says he will no longer hide his face. The Metzudat David says this borrows a human picture: a person hides his face from someone he will not help. The Aramaic translation avoids the word face and says God will no longer remove his Presence.

sources.quote: אחז במשל מבן אדם שאם אינו רוצה למלאות שאלת מי מסתיר פניו ממנו
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the verse borrows a human image: someone who will not grant a request hides his face.

sources.quote: וְלָא אֲסַלֵק עוֹד שְׁכִנְתִּי מִנְהוֹן
sources.says: The Aramaic translation says 'I will no longer remove my Presence from them'.

4:3.headline: Why an iron griddle stands for a wall
4:3.body: Ezekiel sets up a מחבת, a flat iron griddle, as a wall between himself and the city. Radak says a griddle was chosen because it is flat. Its hardness stands for Israel's hard heart, and its black color for sins that separate them from God.

sources.quote: מחבת אין לו ענין קבול אלא שהיא פשוטה יותר מפרור ושאר כלי ברזל לדמותה לקיר
sources.says: Radak says a griddle has no hollow; it is flatter than a pot and other iron vessels, so it can look like a wall.

sources.quote: לחזק הברזל שלב ישראל חזק כברזל והשחרות לשחרות הברזל משל לעונותיהם
sources.says: Radak says iron's strength stands for Israel's heart, hard as iron, and its blackness for their sins.

sources.quote: כי עונותיהם היו מבדילים כקיר ברזל בין ה' ושלוחי השגחתו ובין העיר
sources.says: Malbim says their sins separated God and His messengers from the city like an iron wall.

4:4.headline: Ezekiel 'bears' their sin: suffers it, or atones for it?
4:4.body: תשא את עונם can mean to carry their sin or to forgive it. Radak reads it as endure: lying on one side for so long is very hard. Metzudat Zion reads it as atonement, as in 'forgive all sin' in Hosea.

sources.quote: ופירוש תשא את עונם תסבול עונם כי השכיבה על צד אחד זמן רב שלא יהפך לצד אחר הוא קשה מאד
sources.says: Radak says it means you will suffer their sin, since lying on one side a long time without turning is very hard.

sources.quote: תשא. ענין כפרה וסליחה כמו כל תשא עון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means atonement and forgiveness, as in Hosea 14:3.

4:5.headline: The 'years' of their sin, or 'two for one'?
4:5.body: שני עונם most simply means 'the years of their sin', counted as days. Rashi gives a second reading, which the Targum follows: שני as 'two', so God counts their sin double. Radak finds the Targum's reading strange.

sources.quote: לְמִנְיַן שָׁנִים שֶׁחָטְאוּ לְפָנַי, הֲפַכְתִּים לְךָ לְמִנְיַן יָמִים
sources.says: Rashi says God turned the number of years they sinned into a number of days for the prophet.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵי כְּמוֹ שְׁנַיִם, וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: שני means two, as the Targum translates 'for one, two'.

sources.quote: ותימה הוא מה שת"י את שני עונם על חד תרין בחוביהון
sources.says: Radak says the Targum's 'two for one' reading is puzzling.

4:12.headline: A barley cake, or a mixed loaf eaten like one?
4:12.body: Ezekiel's bread is made of six grains and beans, yet it is called a barley cake. Radak says the verse means he eats it as if it were plain barley. Rashi says it is kneaded as coarsely as barley dough. Metzudat David says barley was animal food, a sign of hunger.

sources.quote: חסר כף הדמיון
sources.says: Radak says the word 'like' is missing: eat it like a barley cake.

sources.quote: עֲרִיבָתָהּ מְנֻוֶּלֶת כַּעֲרִיבַת שְׂעוֹרִים
sources.says: Rashi says its kneading is as crude as barley dough, not fine like a wheat cake.

sources.quote: שמעקת רעבון יאכלו עוגת שעורים שהוא מאכל בהמות
sources.says: Metzudat David says from the pain of hunger they will eat barley cakes, which is animal food.

4:12.headline: Dung is called גלל because it rolls
4:12.body: Ezekiel must bake his bread over dried human dung. Radak and Malbim say dry dung is called גלל from the verb to roll, because it rolls.

sources.quote: ונקראת הצואה היבשה גלל לפי שהיא מתגלגלת
sources.says: Radak says dry excrement is called גלל because it rolls.

sources.quote: בגללי,  צואה יבשה המתגלגלת
sources.says: Malbim says it is dry excrement that rolls.

4:14.headline: Torn meat, or only meat that came close to it?
4:14.body: Ezekiel says he never ate נבלה וטרפה, an animal that died or was torn. Rashi and Radak, following the sages, say that would be no great claim. So it means an animal near death, slaughtered in a rush, that only looks like such meat.

sources.quote: בָּשָׂר מְסֻכֶּנֶת, שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לִנְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means meat of an animal in danger of dying, which resembles a carcass or torn animal.

sources.quote: וְלֹא יִתָּכֵן לוֹמַר נְבֵלָה וּטְרֵפָה מַמָּשׁ, דְּאִם כֵּן – מַאי רְבוּתֵיהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it cannot mean an actual carcass or torn animal, for then what would be special about him?

sources.quote: שלא אכלתי מבשר כוס כוס מעולם פירוש בהמה מסוכנת שאומרים עליה שחוט שחוט
sources.says: Radak says it means he never ate from an animal near death, over which people cry 'slaughter it, slaughter it'.

41:1.headline: Doorposts named after a round tree
41:1.body: אילים here means the doorposts of the sanctuary. Metzudat David says the name was first given to posts that were round like the trunk of an אלה tree.

sources.quote: בעבור שהיו עגולים כאילן אלה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the posts are called אילים because the name was given to posts round like an אלה tree, even though these were square.

41:7.headline: A winding stair, named for going around
41:7.body: ונסבה comes from the word for 'around'. Rashi says it was a stone column with steps on it, so a person climbing it walks in circles around the column.

sources.quote: שֶׁל בִּנְיַן אֲבָנִים הוּא כְּמִין עַמּוּד וּמַעֲלוֹת עוֹלוֹת בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a stone structure like a column with steps going up it, so the climber seems to circle the column.

sources.quote: מל׳ סביב ויאמר על בנין המדרגות שהיתה בתמונת עמוד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from 'around' and describes stairs built in the shape of a column.

41:20.headline: A word marked with dots in the scroll
41:20.body: ההיכל here carries dots over its letters, one of fifteen such places in the Bible. Radak asks why the wall is mentioned at all, since 'the whole house' was already said, and thinks the dots may mark that.

sources.quote: ואני תמה למה הזכיר זה שהרי אמר עשוי אל כל הבית סביב
sources.says: Radak wonders why the verse mentions the wall of the sanctuary when it already said the whole house was carved.

sources.quote: נקוד אולי לזה הטעם והוא אחד מט"ו נקודין שבמקרא
sources.says: Radak says the word is dotted, perhaps for that reason, and it is one of fifteen dotted words in Scripture.

41:22.headline: It starts as an altar and ends as a table
41:22.body: The verse calls this wooden object an altar, then says 'this is the table before God'. The sages learn that while the Temple stood the altar atoned, and now a person's own table atones.

sources.quote: הַשֻּׁלְחָן קוֹרֵא מִזְבֵּחַ, שֶׁמְּכַפֵּר בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה כְּמִזְבֵּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says the verse calls the table an altar, because today it atones like an altar.

sources.quote: פתח במזבח וסיים בשלחן
sources.says: Radak brings the sages' remark that the verse opens with altar and closes with table: once the altar atoned, and now a person's table does.

41:25.headline: A thick beam, not a cloud
41:25.body: עב often means a cloud or something thick. Here Radak reads it as 'thick wood', and Rashi says these were cedar poles set between two walls so the wall would not bulge out.

sources.quote: פירושו עץ עב ויקרא בלא סמיכות עב
sources.says: Radak says it means thick wood, and the beam itself is called עב.

sources.quote: כְּלוֹנְסוֹת שֶׁל אֶרֶז הָיוּ קְבוּעִים מִכּוֹתְלוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל לְכוֹתְלוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִבְעַט
sources.says: Rashi says, from the Mishnah, that cedar poles ran from the sanctuary wall to the porch wall so it would not bulge.

43:2.headline: Did the earth shine, or did it light up the sky?
43:2.body: Radak reads האירה as 'the earth shone' with God's glory. Malbim reads it as 'the earth gave light', so that the earth itself became a lamp for the heavens.

sources.quote: פעל עומד מהנוסף והשאר שבאו מן הבנין הם יוצאים
sources.says: Radak says this form means the earth itself shone, while other forms of the verb mean to light up something else.

sources.quote: פעל יוצא, שמן אור הכבוד שהתלבש עליה נעשית כדבר מאיר להאיר לשמים
sources.says: Malbim says the verb acts on something: clothed in God's light, the earth became a thing that lights up the heavens.

43:6.headline: God's voice is described as speaking to itself
43:6.body: The verb מדבר here is a reflexive form, 'speaking with himself'. Rashi says this is the respectful way to describe God: He spoke within His own glory, and the voice reached the prophet.

sources.quote: כָּבוֹד הוּא לוֹמַר כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה מִדַּבֵּר, כְּמוֹ מִתְדַּבֵּר, כְּלוֹמַר: בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין כְּבוֹדוֹ מְדַבֵּר, וְהַקּוֹל בָּא אֵלַי
sources.says: Rashi says it is respectful to say of God that He was 'speaking to Himself', and the voice came to the prophet.

sources.quote: מדבר כמו מתדבר מבנין התפעל והתי"ו נבלעת בדגש
sources.says: Radak says מדבר stands for מתדבר, a reflexive form whose letter tav has dropped out.

43:13.headline: The altar's 'bosom' is its base
43:13.body: חיק usually means the lap or bosom. Here it names the altar's base. Rashi links it to a word for something fixed in place. Malbim says the base sits in the 'bosom' of the earth.

sources.quote: חֵיק לְשׁוֹן חִיקּוּי וּקְבִיעוּת, וְהוּא הַיְסוֹד
sources.says: Rashi says חיק means something set and fixed, and it is the altar's base.

sources.quote: כן נקרא היסוד שהוא בחיק הארץ
sources.says: Malbim says the base has this name because it lies in the bosom of the earth.

43:14.headline: Here 'the courtyard' is a ledge of the altar
43:14.body: עזרה usually means the Temple courtyard. In this chapter it names the stepped ledges of the altar itself. Malbim says the root sense is a border in front of something.

sources.quote: דפוס בנין המזבח קורא בשם עזרה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the verse calls a tier of the altar's structure an עזרה.

sources.quote: מחיצה וגבול שלפני איזה דבר, ובא על חצר שלפני ההיכל
sources.says: Malbim says the word means a partition or border in front of something, and so also the court in front of the sanctuary.

sources.quote: וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם עֲזָרָה: ״מְסַתְּמְתָא״, לְשׁוֹן רִצְפָּה
sources.says: Rashi says the Aramaic translation renders עזרה with a word meaning a floor.

43:17.headline: An altar with steps, though the Torah forbids them
43:17.body: The Torah says not to go up to the altar by steps (Exodus 20:23). So the commentators read מעלות here as ramps. Metzudat David counts three: the main ramp and two side ramps.

sources.quote: לא שהיה בו מעלות כי התורה אמרה ולא תעלה במעלות על מזבחי
sources.says: Metzudat David says the altar did not have steps, because the Torah forbids going up to it by steps.

sources.quote: כי שלשה היו אחד כבש הגדול ואחד פנה ליסוד ואחד פנה לסובב
sources.says: He says the plural means three ramps: the large ramp and two that turned off to the lower ledges.

sources.quote: והנה כתוב ולא תעלה במעלות על מזבחי אפשר שהיו המעלות עשויות כמין כבש
sources.says: Radak raises the same verse from Exodus and suggests the steps were built like a ramp.

43:21.headline: Burned at the edge of the house, or a set place?
43:21.body: Rashi reads מפקד as the place where the Temple area ends, as in 'not one man was missing'. Malbim reads it as a place appointed for burning. The Aramaic translation says 'a fitting place'.

sources.quote: מָקוֹם שֶׁהַבַּיִת כָּלֶה, כְּמוֹ ״לֹא נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ״
sources.says: Rashi says it means the place where the house ends, like 'not a man of us is missing' in Numbers.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״בַּאֲתַר דַּחֲזִי לְבֵיתָא״, כְּלוֹמַר: בְּמָקוֹם קָדוֹשׁ
sources.says: Rashi also brings the Aramaic translation, 'in the place fit for the house', meaning a holy place.

sources.quote: מקום המופקד ומוכן לצורך הבית, לשרוף שם את הנשרפין
sources.says: Malbim says it is the place set aside for the Temple's needs, where things to be burned were burned.

44:2.headline: God 'came in' through the gate: His presence settling there
44:2.body: בא usually means a body walking somewhere. Maimonides says that when it is said of God it means His presence settling in a place, and he gives this verse as an example.

sources.quote: כִּי ה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּא בוֹ" (יחזקאל מד,ב) וכל הדומה לכך משמעותו שריית שכינה
sources.says: Maimonides says 'come' is borrowed for God to mean His word coming true or His presence resting, and reads this verse as His presence resting.

sources.quote: ה' אלהי ישראל בא בו. רוצה לומר ענין הכבוד שנכנס בו
sources.says: Radak says it means the divine glory that entered through that gate.

44:3.headline: An odd little word: 'to the prince', or 'the prince's coming'
44:3.body: את usually just marks the object of a verb, which does not fit here. Radak reads it as 'to the prince'; Malbim suggests it comes from a root meaning 'come', so 'the coming of the prince'.

sources.quote: את הנשיא כמו אל הנשיא וכן הראה את הכהן
sources.says: Radak says את here means אל, 'to': the closed gate belongs to the prince.

sources.quote: מלת את זרה, ויל"פ שהוא משורש אתא, רצה לומר ביאת הנשיא
sources.says: Malbim calls this את strange and suggests it comes from the root for 'come', meaning 'the coming of the prince'.

44:3.headline: 'Bread' here means the meat of the offerings
44:3.body: The prince sits in the gate to eat לחם, usually 'bread'. Metzudat Zion says the word also means meat, and Radak says what he eats there is his peace offerings.

sources.quote: לחם. כן יקרא גם הבשר כמו את קרבני לחמי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says meat is also called לחם, as in 'my offering, my bread' in Numbers.

sources.quote: כשאוכל זבחי שלמיו לפני ה' יאכלם בזה המקום
sources.says: Radak says that when the prince eats his peace offerings before God, he eats them in this place.

sources.quote: את לחמי הוא החלב והדם
sources.says: Metzudat David says 'my bread' in verse 7 means the fat and the blood of the offerings.

44:7.headline: 'Foreigners' who may really be Israelites estranged from God
44:7.body: בני נכר usually means foreigners, and Targum Jonathan reads it that way. Rashi and Radak say it means Israelites whose deeds made them strangers to God.

sources.quote: שֶׁנִּתְנַכְּרוּ מַעֲשָׂיו לְאָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, זֶהוּ מְשׁוּמָּד
sources.says: Rashi says it is one whose deeds became foreign to his Father in heaven, an Israelite who left the faith.

sources.quote: זה שאני אומר בן נכר איני אומר על הגוים כי אין צריך לומר זה אלא בעבור בן נכר אשר בתוך בני ישראל
sources.says: Radak says the verse does not mean other nations, which goes without saying, but an estranged person among Israel.

sources.quote: בְּאַיְתָיוּתְכוֹן בְּנֵי עַמְמַיָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'sons of the nations', that is, foreigners.

44:7.headline: An 'uncircumcised heart' is a heart sealed shut
44:7.body: ערל means uncircumcised, but the commentators say the root means blocked, so ערלי לב are people closed to God. For ערלי בשר Rashi brings the case of a priest whose brothers died from circumcision.

sources.quote: ערלי לב. ענין חתימה וכן ערלה אזנם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ערלי לב means sealed, like 'their ear is ערלה' in Jeremiah.

sources.quote: כָּל עָרְלָה לְשׁוֹן ׳אֹטֶם׳ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says every ערלה means blocking, and brings this verse as an example.

sources.quote: כֹּהֵן שֶׁמֵּתוּ אֶחָיו מֵחֲמַת מִילָה
sources.says: Rashi says ערלי בשר is a priest left uncircumcised because his brothers died from circumcision.

44:18.headline: Sweat: the priests' belts must not sit where the body sweats
44:18.body: יזע comes from the same root as 'by the sweat of your brow' in Genesis. The sages read the verse as a rule: do not tie the belt where you sweat.

sources.quote: אֵין חוֹגְרִין בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁמְּזִיעִין
sources.says: Rashi cites a teaching that the priests do not tie their belt where the body sweats.

sources.quote: ושרשו "יזע" וכמוהו "לא יחגרו ביזע"
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the root of 'sweat' in Genesis is יזע, the same word as in this verse.

sources.quote: פי' רז"ל לא יחגרו במקום שמזיעין
sources.says: Radak says the sages explain it as not girding in the place where one sweats.

44:20.headline: פרע: long hair or a bare head? This verse decides
44:20.body: פרע can mean hair grown long or a head left uncovered. Malbim says this verse shows the priests' rule is about not letting their hair grow long.

sources.quote: מבואר שהזהיר את הכהנים מלגדל שער בבואם למקדש
sources.says: Malbim notes פרע is used both for long hair and for uncovered hair, and says this verse shows it warns priests against growing their hair long.

sources.quote: ופרע. כן יקרא גדול השער
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says פרע means grown-out hair.

44:20.headline: A haircut named after spelt, a grain whose kernels overlap
44:20.body: כסום יכסמו comes from כוסמת, spelt. The sages read it as a haircut where the tip of each hair lies by the root of the next, like spelt grains on the stalk.

sources.quote: כַּכֻּסֶּמֶת הַזּוֹ, שֶׁסְּדוּרִין בַּשִּׁבֹּלֶת רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה לְצַד עִקָּרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it is like spelt, whose grains lie on the ear with the tip of one beside the base of the next; he also offers 'an even, measured cut'.

sources.quote: מענין החטה והכוסמת, שהכוסמת גדלה ראשה של זו בצד עקרה של זו
sources.says: Malbim says the word comes from spelt, which grows with the head of one grain beside the root of the next.

sources.quote: שהיה מספר כל ראשו ולא לגמרי אלא מניח כל השערות קצת כדי שיהא ראשו של זה בצד עיקרו של זה והיינו כסום יכסמו
sources.says: Rashi on the Talmud says this is the high priest's haircut, cut short but not bare, with each hair's tip by the next one's root.

44:22.headline: 'From a priest': a priest's widow, or some of the priests?
44:22.body: מכהן יקחו can mean priests may marry a widow whose late husband was a priest. Rashi and the sages read it as 'some priests may marry a widow', the ordinary priests but not the high priest.

sources.quote: וְזֶהוּ מִכֹּהֵן יִקָּחוּ – יֵשׁ מִן הַכֹּהֵן שֶׁמּוּתָּרִין בְּאַלְמָנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'some of the priests', the ordinary ones, may marry a widow.

sources.quote: אלמנת כהן גדול ואפילו כהן הדיוט יכול לקחתה כהן אחר וזהו שאמר אשר תהיה אלמנה מכהן יקחו
sources.says: Radak first reads it as a priest's widow whom another priest may marry, then gives the sages' reading, 'some of the priests'.

sources.quote: ולפי הפשט היה נראה מדברי יחזקאל כי אלמנות כהן מותרות לכהנים לכן דברי הקבלה הוא הנכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the plain sense seems to allow priests' widows to priests, but the received tradition is right.

44:26.headline: Seven days after he is pure, or seven days to become pure?
44:26.body: Read plainly, the priest waits seven more days after he is already pure. The sages read 'after his purification' as 'after he leaves the dead body', so these are the usual seven days.

sources.quote: אַחַר פְּרִישָׁתוֹ מִן הַמֵּת
sources.says: Rashi, following the Talmud, says 'after his purification' means after he separates from the dead.

sources.quote: אפשר שיהיה זה לעתיד לתוספת קדושה שאחר שיטהרו לסוף שבע עוד יספרו לו שבעה ימים אחרים
sources.says: Radak says it may mean seven more days after he is already pure, an added strictness for the future, though the sages read it as after he leaves the dead.

44:26.headline: Why 'they' count his days: the other priests keep watch
44:26.body: The verse says 'they shall count for him', not 'he shall count'. Radak and Metzudat David say his fellow priests count, so he cannot come in early if he forgets.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר יספרו לו ולא אמר יספור לו רוצה לומר יספרו אחיו הכהנים
sources.says: Radak asks why it says 'they shall count' and not 'he shall count', and answers that his fellow priests do the counting.

sources.quote: אחיו הכהנים יספרו לו שאם שכח הוא לא יניחוהו הם ליכנס למקדש
sources.says: Metzudat David says his fellow priests count for him, so if he forgets they will not let him into the sanctuary.

44:27.headline: His 'sin offering' may be a flour offering, say the sages
44:27.body: חטאת usually means an animal brought for a sin. Rashi, following the Talmud, says here it is the flour offering a priest brings on his first day; Radak reads it as a sin offering for his impurity.

sources.quote: יַקְרִיב חַטָּאתוֹ זוֹ עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says 'his sin offering' is the tenth of an ephah of flour a priest brings on the day he starts to serve.

sources.quote: עתה אחרי שיטהר יקריב קרבן חטאת בעבור טמאתו וזה יהיה חידוש לעתיד
sources.says: Radak reads it as a real sin offering for his impurity, a new rule for the future, and questions the flour-offering reading.

46:4.headline: This 'Sabbath' may be a festival, not the weekly Sabbath
46:4.body: Ezekiel's Sabbath offering is six lambs, but the Torah asks for two. Rashi says שבת can mean the weekly Sabbath or a festival day, and here he reads it as a festival.

sources.quote: וּבְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת מַשְׁמַע שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית וּמַשְׁמַע יוֹם טוֹב
sources.says: Rashi says 'the Sabbath day' can mean the weekly Sabbath and can mean a festival.

sources.quote: שַׁבָּת זוֹ אֵינָהּ שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית אֶלָּא יוֹם טוֹב
sources.says: He says this Sabbath is not the weekly one but a festival.

46:6.headline: One bull, but 'unblemished' in the plural
46:6.body: The verse says פר, one bull, then תמימם, 'unblemished ones'. Radak brings two readings: the bull and its mother must both be whole, or, with the Sages, if he finds two bulls as the Torah asks, he brings two. Metzudat Zion says it covers the bulls of every new month.

sources.quote: אמר פר יחיד ואמר תמימים רבים יש מפרשים שיהיה הפר ואמו תמימים
sources.says: Radak notes the verse says 'bull' in the singular and 'unblemished' in the plural; some explain that the bull and its mother must be unblemished.

sources.quote: לפיכך אמר תמימים שאם מצא שנים יביא שנים
sources.says: He brings the Sages: it says 'unblemished ones' to teach that if he finds two, he brings two.

sources.quote: או אמר לשון רבים על כל הפרים של כל ראשי החדשים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the plural may speak of all the bulls of all the new months.

46:9.headline: Written 'they go out', read 'he goes out'
46:9.body: The written text has יצאו, plural, but it is read יצא, singular. Radak says the written form speaks of the whole crowd, and the reading speaks of each person in it.

sources.quote: נכחו יצאו כתיב על העם שהם רבים וקרי יצא על כל אחד ואחד
sources.says: Radak says the written plural is about the people as a crowd, and the read singular is about each one of them.

46:11.headline: Feasts and set times are not the same thing
46:11.body: The verse names both חגים, feasts, and מועדים, set times. Radak says a feast can be a time of joy with no fixed date, like Solomon's dedication of the Temple. A set time can be a fixed date that is no feast.

sources.quote: לפי שיש חג שאינו מועד אלא שמחה שישמח אדם ויאכל וישתה ויקרא חג
sources.says: Radak says there is a feast that is not a set time, only a celebration where people eat and drink, and it is called a feast.

sources.quote: ויש מועד גם כן שאינו חג
sources.says: He says there is also a set time that is not a feast.

sources.quote: ובחגים היינו בחג השבועות שנקרא חג, על שמביאים שלמי חגיגה
sources.says: Malbim says 'feasts' here means Shavuot, called a feast because festival peace offerings are brought.

46:14.headline: To crush the flour, or to sprinkle it like dew
46:14.body: לרס appears only here. Rashi links it to רסיסים, broken bits: the oil is worked into crushed flour. Radak and Metzudat Zion link it to רסיסי לילה, drops of night dew: the oil is sprinkled on the flour.

sources.quote: לְכַתֵּת וְלִבְלוֹל בּוֹ אֶת הַסֹּלֶת, לְשׁוֹן רְסִיס
sources.says: Rashi says it means to crush and mix the flour with the oil, from the word for fragments.

sources.quote: ולשון לרוס ענין זלוף כמו רסיסי לילה
sources.says: Radak says the word means sprinkling, like 'drops of the night'.

sources.quote: לרוס. ענין זלוף ונטיפה כמו רסיסי לילה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means sprinkling and dripping, like drops of the night.

46:20.headline: 'To make the people holy' is a warning, not a goal
46:20.body: The priests cook the holiest offerings inside so as not 'to make the people holy'. Radak says carrying the meat out would make it look as if ordinary people may eat it. Malbim calls it a figure of speech: holiness leaking out to the common.

sources.quote: אם היו מוציאין שם הבשר יראה שגם ישראל היו מותרין באותו בשר וזהו שאמר לקדש את העם
sources.says: Radak says if they took the meat out there, it would look as if ordinary Israelites were allowed that meat, and that is what 'to make the people holy' means.

sources.quote: הוא על צד המליצה שיוציא הקדש ממחיצתו אל העם והחול
sources.says: Malbim says it is a figure of speech for taking the holy out of its bounds to the people and the everyday.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״לְאִתְעָרְבָא עִם עַמָּא״
sources.says: Rashi cites the Targum: 'to mix with the people'.

46:22.headline: Roofless, smoky, or joined: three readings of one word
46:22.body: קטרות appears only here. The Mishnah, cited by Rashi, says it means courts with no roof. Metzudat David adds they were open so the smoke, קיטור, could rise. Radak says the plain sense is 'joined', like קשורות, tied into the corners.

sources.quote: אֵין קְטוּרוֹת אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינָן מְקוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi cites the Mishnah: 'ketorot' means only that they were not roofed.

sources.quote: היו פתוחות ממעל למען יצא קיטור העשן
sources.says: Metzudat David says they were open above so the smoke could go out.

sources.quote: ולשון קטורות לפי הפשט כמו קשורות
sources.says: Radak says that by the plain sense the word means tied, joined.

46:22.headline: A word written with dots over it, one of fifteen
46:22.body: Radak says this word has dots written above its letters, one of fifteen such words in the Bible. He reads it as courts having corners. Malbim reads it as 'scraped': the plaster peeled off from the constant fire and smoke.

sources.quote: ומלה זו היא נקודה מלמעלה והיא אחת מט"ו נקודין שבמקרא
sources.says: Radak says this word is dotted above and is one of the fifteen dotted words in Scripture.

sources.quote: בנין הפעל מן ואת הבית יקציע, שהוקלף הסיד מעליהם
sources.says: Malbim says it comes from 'he shall scrape the house': the plaster was peeled off them.

6:4.headline: חמנים are sun idols, named from חמה, the sun
6:4.body: Rashi says חמנים were idol images set up on rooftops for the sun. Metzudat Zion says the word comes from חמה, 'sun'.

sources.quote: הָעֲשׂוּיִין עַל הַגַּגּוֹת לַחַמָּה
sources.says: Rashi says these were idol images made on the rooftops for the sun.

sources.quote: צורת חמה היו עושים להם לפסל כי עבדו לחמה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they made a sun shape as an idol because they worshipped the sun.

sources.quote: חמניכם. מל׳ חמה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from חמה, the sun.

6:4.headline: Idols called גלולים, a word that sounds like dung
6:4.body: Ezekiel's usual word for idols is גלולים. Metzudat Zion says they are called this because they are as disgusting as גלל, dung.

sources.quote: דמות עובדי גלולים המאוס כגלל של רעי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the idols are named for being loathsome like dung.

6:8.headline: 'I will leave some over', or 'I will gain something'
6:8.body: Radak reads והותרתי as 'I will leave survivors among you'. Malbim reads it as 'I will have a gain': the punishment will bear fruit when the survivors remember God.

sources.quote: בכם שלא תפלו כלכם בחרב
sources.says: Radak says it means God will leave some of them so that not all fall by the sword.

sources.quote: כמו בכל עצב יהיה מותר, ר"ל ריוח ותועלת
sources.says: Malbim says it means profit and benefit, as in 'in all toil there is profit'.

6:9.headline: Did God break their heart, or was God heartbroken?
6:9.body: The Aramaic reads נשברתי as 'I broke their heart'. Radak says the form means 'I was broken': God speaks as if hurt by their straying heart, like 'He was grieved to His heart' in Genesis 6:6.

sources.quote: אמר האל על דרך משל שאני נשברתי מלבם הזונה
sources.says: Radak rejects 'I broke' and says God speaks in a figure: I was broken by their straying heart.

sources.quote: שכביכול נשבר לבו בשברון לבם
sources.says: Malbim says the form hints that God's heart, as it were, broke along with theirs.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר נִכְנַעְתִּי אֶצְלָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means God humbled Himself before them and kept asking them to come back.

6:12.headline: The one 'kept safe' in the city, or the one under siege
6:12.body: Radak gives two readings of הנצור. It may mean 'guarded', safe inside the city, or 'besieged', from מצור, siege. Either way he dies of hunger.

sources.quote: והנצור פעול מן נוצר תאנה ענינו שהוא שמור בתוך העיר או הוא מענין מצור
sources.says: Radak says it means either guarded inside the city, from 'he who guards a fig tree', or besieged.

sources.quote: הַנֶּאֱסָף אֶל הָעִיר וְיָצוּרוּ עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is the one who gathers into the city and is besieged there.

6:14.headline: The land will be empty, and people will stare in shock
6:14.body: שממה and משמה come from the same root. Rashi says the first means empty of people and the second means a shock to everyone who sees it.

sources.quote: תִּמָּהוֹן, שֶׁיִּתְמְהוּ עָלֶיהָ רוֹאֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says משמה means amazement: those who see the land will be stunned.

sources.quote: משמה גדול מן שממה, מורה על התמדת השממון
sources.says: Malbim says משמה is stronger than שממה and shows the ruin will last.

6:14.headline: Divlah is Riblah, where Zedekiah was brought before Nebuchadnezzar
6:14.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read דבלתה as רבלתה, Riblah, with dalet for resh, as with Deuel and Reuel. Nebuchadnezzar camped there during the siege, and Zedekiah was brought to him there.

sources.quote: בדל"ת כמו רבלתה ברי"ש וכן דעואל רעואל
sources.says: Radak says Divlah is Riblah, and it is named because Nebuchadnezzar stayed there and Zedekiah was brought to him there.

sources.quote: כמו רבלתה ברי״ש וכן דעואל רעואל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is Riblah, where Nebuchadnezzar sat when Zedekiah was brought to him.

7:4.headline: Two kinds of pity: sparing what is useful, sparing what is good
7:4.body: Malbim says חס means sparing something because you get use from it. חמל means sparing it because it is good in itself. God says neither will apply.

sources.quote: החס לא ישחית את הדבר מצד שישיג ממנו צורך ותועלת
sources.says: Malbim says one who has חס spares a thing because he gets use from it.

sources.quote: והחומל לא ישחית מצד שהדבר עצמו טוב ויפה ואין ראוי להשחיתו
sources.says: Malbim says one who has חמל spares a thing because it is good and fine in itself.

7:5.headline: One unique disaster, or one disaster after another?
7:5.body: Rashi reads 'one evil' as a single evil beyond all others: the Temple's destruction. Radak notes the Targum says 'evil after evil', as if it read אחר, after, instead of אחת, one.

sources.quote: רָעָה שְׁלֵימָה וּמְיֻחֶדֶת, לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל הָרָעוֹת, וְהוּא חֻרְבַּן הַבַּיִת
sources.says: Rashi says it is one complete, unique evil above all others: the destruction of the Temple.

sources.quote: וידמה כי יונתן היה קורא אחר רעה שתרגם בישתא בתר בישתא
sources.says: Radak says the Targum seems to have read 'after' here, since it translates 'evil after evil'.

7:7.headline: A shout of alarm, an echo, or splendor on the hills?
7:7.body: Rashi says הד is a cry calling people to flee to the hilltops. Radak says this noise is real, not like an echo in the hills. Metzudat Zion reads it as splendor: the hills will lose their glory.

sources.quote: וְהֵד – לְשׁוֹן צַעֲקַת הַכְרָזָה לָקוּם לִבְרוֹחַ אֶל רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is a shouted call to get up and flee to the mountaintops.

sources.quote: לא תהיה כמו קריאת הד הרים כשאדם נותן קולו בין ההרים ידמה שיוצא קול
sources.says: Radak says the shouting will not be like an echo in the mountains, but a real cry.

sources.quote: הד. הוא מל׳ הוד והדר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from splendor and glory.

7:11.headline: Their crowds, or their wealth? המון has both senses
7:11.body: המון usually means a crowd, and Metzudat Zion reads it so. Radak reads it as their great wealth, as in 'whoever loves wealth'.

sources.quote: ולא מרבוי ממון שלהם כמו מהמון רשעים ומי אוהב בהמון שפירושם רוב ממון
sources.says: Radak says it means their great wealth, as in other verses where המון means much money.

sources.quote: מהמונם. המון עם רב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a great crowd of people.

7:17.headline: Knees 'turning to water': sweat of fear, or melting?
7:17.body: Rashi says the knees will run with the sweat of terror. Radak says it is a picture: the knees seem to melt away, with no strength left.

sources.quote: תֵּלַכְנָה מָּיִם. מִזִּיעַת אֵימָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means from the sweat of terror.

sources.quote: תלכנה כמים על דרך משל כאילו נמסו
sources.says: Radak says it is a figure of speech: as if the knees melted like water.

7:19.headline: Their gold becomes something to push away
7:19.body: נדה is the word for a woman kept apart during her period. Metzudat Zion says it comes from moving away: their gold will be loathed and kept at a distance. Rashi says it will disgust them.

sources.quote: לרחוק ולתעוב כנדה והוא מל׳ נדידה והרחקה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means distant and loathed like a niddah, from a root meaning to move away.

sources.quote: לְשִׁקּוּץ יִהְיֶה לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it will be an abomination to them.

7:20.headline: 'The beauty of his ornament': the Temple, or their gold?
7:20.body: Rashi and Radak say God's 'beautiful ornament' is the Temple, which the people filled with idols. Malbim reads it as their gold jewelry, which they made into their pride and their idols.

sources.quote: הוּא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא גְּאוֹן עֻזָּם
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Temple, which is called the pride of their strength.

sources.quote: וצבי עדיו. זהו בית המקדש
sources.says: Radak says this is the Temple.

sources.quote: שצבי עדיו של הזהב זאת שמו להם לגאון ותפארת
sources.says: Malbim says it is the beauty of their gold ornaments, which they made their pride.

7:21.headline: Written one way, read another: God's Presence or the house
7:21.body: The word is written וחללוה, 'they will profane her', but read וחללוהו, 'they will profane it'. Radak says the written form means God's Presence and the spoken form means the Temple.

sources.quote: הכתיב על השכינה והקרי על הבית
sources.says: Radak says the written form refers to the Divine Presence and the read form to the house.

7:22.headline: God's 'hidden place': the inner room where he dwelt
7:22.body: צפוני means my hidden thing. Rashi says it is the place where God was hidden among them. Radak says it is the Holy of Holies, where the Ark stood.

sources.quote: אֶת הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁהָיִיתִי צָפוּן שָׁם בֵּינֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it is the place where God was hidden among them.

sources.quote: המקום הצפון שלי בבית והוא הדביר שהוא קדש הקדשים ששם הארון
sources.says: Radak says it is God's hidden place in the Temple, the Holy of Holies where the Ark was.

7:24.headline: Whose holy places? The Temple, or their own shrines?
7:24.body: Metzudat David says 'their holy places' are the Temple and its inner rooms. Rashi says they are the halls of their high places, where they used to gather.

sources.quote: בָּתֵּי הֵיכַל הַבָּמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹעָדִים שָׁם, לְשׁוֹן בֵּית זִמּוּנָם
sources.says: Rashi says these are the halls of the high places where they would gather.

sources.quote: יחללו ויבזו בתי מקדשיהם הם הבית וההיכל ובית קה״ק
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are the Temple, its hall and the Holy of Holies.

7:26.headline: Event upon event, or ruin upon ruin?
7:26.body: Rashi reads הוה as 'happening', from the verb to be: one event after another. Menachem, and Radak with the Targum, read it as breaking: ruin upon ruin.

sources.quote: מְאוֹרָע עַל מְאוֹרָע, הֲוָיָה אַחַר הֲוָיָה. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ לְשׁוֹן שֶׁבֶר
sources.says: Rashi says it means event upon event, and Menachem took it as breaking.

sources.quote: שבר על שבר וכן ת"י תבר על תבר
sources.says: Radak says it means breaking upon breaking, as the Targum translates.

8:1.headline: The 'hand of God' falls: prophecy arriving with force
8:1.body: Radak says the spirit of prophecy, when it comes with force, is called the hand of God. The Targum translates it as 'a spirit of prophecy'.

sources.quote: רוח נבואה כשתבא בחזקה נקראת יד ה'
sources.says: Radak says the spirit of prophecy, when it comes strongly, is called the hand of God.

sources.quote: וּשְׁרַת עֲלַי תַמָן רוּחַ נְבוּאָה
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'a spirit of prophecy rested on me there'.

8:2.headline: חשמלה read as 'hush, a word': keep silent about it
8:2.body: חשמל is a shining substance in Ezekiel's vision. Metzudat David splits the word into חש, hush, and מלה, word: close your mouth and do not speak about it.

sources.quote: וגם חשמלה היא מלה מורכבת חש מלה ר״ל שתוק ובלום פיך מן המלול בו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the word is made of 'hush' and 'word', meaning be silent and do not speak of it.

8:3.headline: The idol that 'stirs jealousy' by standing in God's house
8:3.body: המקנה looks like 'acquiring', but Radak says it stands for המקניא, provoking jealousy. Rashi says the idol was set there to provoke and anger God.

sources.quote: ומשפטו המקניא בשקל משגיא לגוים ופירושו שהסמל מקניא האל בהיותו בביתו
sources.says: Radak says the proper form is המקניא, and the image provokes God by standing in his house.

sources.quote: צוּרַת הַקִּנְאָה מְקַנֵּא וּמַקְנִיט לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says it was an image of jealousy that provoked and angered God.

8:6.headline: Who is being pushed away from the Temple?
8:6.body: Rashi says their deeds drive God away from his own sanctuary. Malbim says they meant to drive away a power of evil they feared, and in doing so they truly drove God away.

sources.quote: כְּדֵי שֶׁאֶתְרַחֵק מֵעַל מִקְדָּשִׁי
sources.says: Rashi says it means so that God will distance himself from his sanctuary.

sources.quote: כדי שיתרחק פועל הרע ולתכלית זה עבודתם פה להרחיק הקנאה, ובזה הם מרחיקים את ה' באמת
sources.says: Malbim says they worshipped to keep the evil power away, and by this they really pushed God away.

8:8.headline: Digging through the wall: a vision, and a picture of the siege
8:8.body: Maimonides notes Ezekiel was in Babylon when he dug through a Temple wall, so it happened only in vision. Radak says the digging pictured the enemy breaking through Jerusalem's walls.

sources.quote: וכך תיאר שהוא נצטווה לחפור בקיר אשר בהר הבית בעודו בבבל
sources.says: Maimonides says Ezekiel describes digging in a Temple Mount wall while he was in Babylon, so it was only in a vision.

sources.quote: וזו המראה משל חתירת הקיר להראותו בקיעת העיר
sources.says: Radak says the digging is a picture of the city being broken into.

8:11.headline: Why name Yaazaniah? His generation learned from him
8:11.body: Only one of the seventy elders is named. Rashi says he was an important man whom his generation copied, so God was strict with him.

sources.quote: חָשׁוּב הָיָה, וּלְמֵדִין דּוֹרוֹ הֵימֶנּוּ, לְפִיכָךְ הִקְפִּיד עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says he was important and his generation learned from him, so God was strict with him.

sources.quote: גדול שבכולם היה
sources.says: Radak says he was the greatest of them all.

8:16.headline: Backs to the Temple, faces to the sun: a deliberate reversal
8:16.body: Maimonides and Radak say the Holy of Holies was in the west so worshippers would turn their backs on the sun. These men turned around to bow to the sun. Rashi adds, from the sages, that they exposed themselves toward the Temple.

sources.quote: ולכן פנה אברהם אבינו למערב בהר המוריה, כלומר במקדש, כדי להפנות עורף לשמש
sources.says: Maimonides says Abraham faced west on Mount Moriah to turn his back on the sun, and cites this verse as the reversal.

sources.quote: לכוונה זו צוה האל פתח המשכן למזרח וקדש הקדשים למערב לבטל עבודת השמש
sources.says: Radak says God put the Tabernacle's entrance in the east and the Holy of Holies in the west to undo sun worship.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא מַגִּיד שֶׁהָיָה אֲחוֹרֵיהֶם מְגֻלֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says the extra words teach that they bared their backsides toward the Temple.

9:2.headline: Who is the seventh man, the one dressed in linen?
9:2.body: Among the six destroyers walks a man dressed in בדים, linen. Radak brings the sages: he is the angel Gabriel, who throws fire on the city. Malbim says he is the angel who speaks up for the people, and in the vision's picture he stands for Jeremiah the priest.

sources.quote: וכן אמרו זה גבריאל והם אמרו כי גבריאל מלאך של אש
sources.says: Radak brings the sages that the man in linen is Gabriel, the angel of fire.

sources.quote: ואיש אחד בתוכם לבוש בדים שהוא מלאך המלמד זכות
sources.says: Malbim says the man in linen is the angel who pleads for the people's merit.

sources.quote: וירמיה היה כהן לבוש בגדי הבד
sources.says: Malbim says in the parable he stands for Jeremiah, a priest dressed in linen.

9:2.headline: The scribe's קסת: an inkwell, or a wax writing tablet?
9:2.body: The man in linen carries a קסת at his waist. Rashi says it is a set of tablets covered in wax, written on with a stylus. Radak says it is the inkwell, since the man must mark the foreheads with ink.

sources.quote: פִּנְקָס; הֵם לוּחוֹת שֶׁמְּחֻפִּין בְּשַׁעֲוָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a writing tablet, boards coated with wax.

sources.quote: קסת הוא כלי הדיו
sources.says: Radak says the קסת is the ink holder.

sources.quote: ענין הפסוק הוא על צורך הדיו לא על הלוח
sources.says: Radak says the verse is about the ink, not the tablet, because the man is told to mark a tav.

9:3.headline: God's glory leaves the cherub: the first of ten departures
9:3.body: God's glory rose from the כרוב, the cherub, to the doorway of the Temple. Rashi says the Presence left in ten stages, little by little, and this was the first. Radak asks why it says one cherub when there were two. He brings the sages: it moved from one cherub to the other, then to the doorway.

sources.quote: וְהִתְחִילָה לְהִסְתַּלֵּק וְלָצֵאת לַחוּץ מְעַט מְעַט, עֶשֶׂר מַסָּעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the Presence began to leave little by little, in ten journeys, and this is the first.

sources.quote: ולא אמר הכרובים כי שנים כרובים היו ארז"ל כי נסע מכרוב לכרוב ומכרוב למפתן
sources.says: Radak notes it says 'cherub' though there were two, and brings the sages that the glory moved from cherub to cherub and then to the threshold.

9:4.headline: The mark on the foreheads: a sign, or the letter tav
9:4.body: God tells the man in linen to put a תו on the foreheads of those who grieve. Radak takes it as a sign in ink, like the blood on the doors in Egypt. He also brings the sages: it is the letter tav, in ink for the righteous and in blood for the wicked. Rav says tav begins both 'you shall live' and 'you shall die'.

sources.quote: לסימן שלא יגעו בהם המשחיתים וזה הענין כענין דם הפסח במצרים
sources.says: Radak says the mark is a sign so the destroyers will not touch them, like the Passover blood in Egypt.

sources.quote: כתוב על מצחן של צדיקים תי"ו של דיו ועל מצחן של רשעים תי"ו של דם
sources.says: Radak brings the sages that God told Gabriel to write a tav in ink on the righteous and in blood on the wicked.

sources.quote: רב אמר תי"ו תחיה תי"ו תמות
sources.says: Radak cites Rav that tav stands for 'you shall live' and for 'you shall die'.

9:4.headline: Sighing and groaning: Malbim separates two kinds of grief
9:4.body: The marked people are הנאנחים והנאנקים, those who sigh and those who groan. Malbim says sighing is over the evil of the whole people. Groaning comes from one's own pain: these people were pressed and hurt for refusing to go along with the wicked.

sources.quote: הנאנח יהיה גם על רעת הכלל, והנואק הוא מפני לחצו ומכתו
sources.says: Malbim says one sighs even over the community's evil, but groans because of one's own pressure and blows.

sources.quote: ונאנקים מפני שנלחצים ונענים על שבלתי מסכימים אל מעשי הרשעים
sources.says: Malbim says they groaned because they were oppressed for not agreeing with the wicked.

9:5.headline: Written 'on', read 'do not': two ways to hear the order
9:5.body: The written text says על תחס. Radak reads it as 'strike even those your eye would pity, and surely the rest'. The reading tradition says אל תחס, 'let your eye not pity'. Radak says the read word means just what it says.

sources.quote: והכתוב רוצה לומר והכה על אשר תחוס עיניכם וכל שכן על האחרים
sources.says: Radak says the written word means strike even the ones your eye pities, and all the more the others.

sources.quote: והקרי כמשמעו הזהירם שלא יחוסו על האדם
sources.says: Radak says the read word means what it says: do not pity anyone.

9:6.headline: 'Begin at My sanctuary', or 'begin with My holy ones'
9:6.body: God says to begin ממקדשי, at My sanctuary. Rashi brings the sages: read it as 'from My holy ones', the very people marked with the tav. The charge was that they had not protested the evil around them. Radak says these were people who kept the Torah from aleph to tav.

sources.quote: אַל תִּקְרֵי מִמִּקְדָּשִׁי אֶלָּא ׳מִמְּקֻדָּשַׁי׳
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: do not read 'from My sanctuary' but 'from My holy ones'.

sources.quote: הֲרֵי לֹא מִחוּ בָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the attribute of justice argued that the marked ones had not protested.

sources.quote: אלו בני אדם שקיימו כל התורה כולה מאל"ף ועד תי"ו
sources.says: Radak brings the sages that these were people who kept the whole Torah from aleph to tav.

9:8.headline: One odd word blends two forms of 'I was left'
9:8.body: Ezekiel says ונאשאר אני, 'and I was left'. Radak says the word is built from two forms, ונשאר and אשאר. It puts two meanings in one word to be brief: Ezekiel looked to see who was left, and saw only himself.

sources.quote: ומלה זו מורכבת מן ונשאר שהוא נפעל עבר ומן אשאר
sources.says: Radak says the word is a blend of ונשאר and אשאר.

sources.quote: ואמר שני טעמים במלה אחת לקצר
sources.says: Radak says the prophet put two meanings into one word to be brief.
